jobs.title: Director, Cloud Governance
jobs.description:
Scopely
is seeking a Director, Cloud Governance
to lead efforts in establishing and enforcing standards, policies, and guardrails across Scopely’s multi-cloud environment. This is a remote opportunity for individuals in Canada or the United States.

As a Director, Cloud Governance
you will play a pivotal leadership role in defining and executing the Scopely’s Cloud Governance strategy. This team will define, implement, and enforce the policies and controls that govern how cloud infrastructure is used across a decentralized organization of game, platform, and product teams.

This role is critical to bringing structure, consistency, and guardrails to Scopely’s cloud footprint, and will be key in modernizing our overall governance posture. As a central leader, you will drive alignment across highly autonomous teams and translate governance into practical, adoptable solutions while balancing control and development velocity.

This is a foundational leadership role; you will establish governance from the ground up, introduce scalable and enforceable controls, and drive adoption and buy-in across various teams, stakeholders, and senior leaders.

What You Will Do

Build & Lead Cloud Governance

Build and lead a Cloud Governance team
Define the operating model for how governance partners with game teams, security, and FinOps
Establish clear ownership and enforcement mechanisms for cloud policies

Define & Enforce Cloud Guardrails

Design and implement enforceable controls across AWS and GCP, including:
AWS Organizations, Service Control Policies (SCPs)
GCP Organization Policies and IAM constraints

Establish guardrails around:
Resource provisioning and service usage
Region restrictions and data residency
Identity and access management
Network architecture and environment isolation

Own the mandate to enforce policies, including the ability to restrict or block non-compliant usage

Standardize Cloud Structure

Define and implement standards for:
AWS account structure and GCP project/folder hierarchy
Environment segmentation (prod, staging, dev)
Naming conventions and resource organization

Bring consistency across a fragmented, multi-team cloud footprint

Tagging & Governance

Define and enforce tagging standards in partnership with FinOps
Ensure all resources are attributable (ownership, environment, cost center)
Enable downstream cost allocation and operational visibility

Stakeholder Partnership

Collaborate with FinOps on cost allocation and optimization levers (budgets, quotas, usage controls)
Partner with Security to align governance with security and compliance requirements
Work directly with game teams to safely roll out and drive adoption of policies and standards

AI-Forward Governance & Automation

Define and execute an AI-native vision for cloud governance, transforming the function into an intelligent, policy-driven operating model powered by autonomous and agentic systems
Establish the organization’s strategy for governance autonomy, defining where fully autonomous operations, human-on-the-loop oversight, and human-in-the-loop approvals are appropriate based on risk, business impact, and compliance requirements
Architect and drive agentic governance capabilities that continuously monitor cloud environments, detect risk, and autonomously remediate anomalies at scale
Partner across engineering, data, and security, and platform teams to embed responsible AI governance into cloud platforms, establishing guardrails for AI adoption, autonomous decision-making, and auditability

What We're Looking For

10+ years in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or SRE
3–5+ years leading teams in complex, multi-team environments
Experience operating in decentralized or federated engineering organizations
Proven track record implementing cloud governance and enforcement at scale
Experience managing or influencing environments with $50M+ cloud spend
Deep hands-on experience with AWS and/or GCP
Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform)
Experience with policy-as-code and governance tooling (e.g., OPA, Sentinel, AWS Config)
Strong understanding of cloud networking, identity, and multi-account design

For candidates in CA, CO, NJ, NY, and WA, the annual salary range is provided below. In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible for equity, bonuses, and a comprehensive benefits package, including healthcare benefits, retirement benefits, pet insurance, paid holidays, paid Scopely free days, and unlimited paid time off. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

jobs.title: Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance
jobs.description:
Overview

AtkinsRéalis is looking for a Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance to turn the potential of AI into measurable improvements in how Finance works and how the business makes decisions.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The Director will define a practical AI strategy, identify the opportunities worth pursuing and lead a disciplined portfolio from business case through adoption and verified results. They will also personally design, build, test and help deploy practical Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows within approved enterprise environments.

Success means tangible outcomes: capacity released for higher-value work, faster and better-informed decisions, stronger controls, improved cash performance and protection of project margins. The role is not about deploying technology for its own sake or accumulating pilots that never change how Finance operates.

Leading a small team with a global mandate, the Director will bring together Finance leaders and process owners with the Financial Systems Centre of Excellence (CoE), IT, Global Digital, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, and data, cybersecurity, privacy and risk specialists. They will develop Finance-specific strategy and governance within enterprise standards, not create competing platforms or policies.

You are a business-led AI and transformation leader who combines strategic ambition, financial discipline and genuine hands-on ability. You can inspire executives, challenge a weak business case and align Finance, Digital, IT and control teams. You are as comfortable discussing strategy as you are building an agent to test an idea with users.

Your role

Set The Strategy And Build Alignment

Define and communicate a value-first AI strategy and roadmap for Global Finance, aligned with Finance priorities, enterprise AI strategy, technology standards and the Financial Systems roadmap.
Determine where AI can materially improve outcomes, where conventional automation or process redesign is preferable, and where an opportunity should not proceed.
Build a shared agenda across FP&A, Controllership, Project Finance and other Finance teams; engage regional and business leaders to identify needs that can scale.
Advise Finance leadership on investment choices, dependencies and risks; secure sponsorship and rally teams that do not report to the Director.

Own a Disciplined Portfolio Of Use Cases

Establish transparent intake and prioritization connected to enterprise channels and governance; assess business value, process and data readiness, feasibility, adoption, total cost and risk.
Maintain a sequenced portfolio with named sponsors, accountable process owners, delivery partners, milestones and clear decisions to proceed, change direction or stop.
Prioritize a few opportunities with a credible path to impact over a large collection of pilots. Candidate areas include reporting commentary, Finance knowledge access, exception handling, forecasting support, collections and project-margin early warning; each requires its own assessment and business case.

Make The Business Case And Prove The Return

Require proportionate business cases before material investment, with baselines, expected benefits, implementation and ongoing costs, risks, dependencies, adoption assumptions and alternatives.
Distinguish time saved from capacity genuinely redeployed and from cost removed; do not treat these as interchangeable financial benefits.
Agree measurement methods and benefit owners before delivery; track investment and realized value at use-case and portfolio levels, with independent validation where appropriate.
Report candidly on adoption, net value, cost and control effectiveness; recommend whether to improve, scale or discontinue initiatives that underperform.

Build, Test And Demonstrate Solutions Personally

Personally design, build and refine selected Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows, especially early prototypes and focused solutions that accelerate learning.
Use Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio hands-on to configure agents, test them with users, assess reliability and improve outputs based on feedback.
Use AI tools regularly in professional work to improve analysis, research, drafting and workflow execution, applying appropriate review and data-handling requirements.
Turn Finance problems into working demonstrations; assess limitations and costs, and decide whether a solution should stop, improve or enter the approved production route.
Stay close enough to delivery to challenge designs, troubleshoot barriers and coach builders, without being the sole developer of enterprise-scale products; partner with Digital and IT on supported deployment.

Establish Practical, Responsible Governance

Translate enterprise AI policy and standards into a Finance operating model covering ownership, intake, risk assessment, testing, approvals, human oversight, monitoring and lifecycle management.
Partner with Digital, IT, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, Risk and Internal Audit to clarify decision rights and navigate the path from idea to approved production use.
Protect sensitive Finance and client information through appropriate access, validation, traceability and human review before AI outputs inform reporting or decisions.
Work with data and process owners on source quality, definitions and controls; reuse approved enterprise platforms and challenge unnecessary complexity without bypassing security or technology accountabilities.

Deliver Through Partnership And Adoption

Partner with the Financial Systems CoE so initiatives fit ERP, EPM and reporting architecture without creating competing technology roadmaps.
Agree delivery responsibilities with Digital and IT while retaining Finance accountability for business outcomes; redesign workflows with process owners around human decisions, exceptions and controls.
Lead communications, training and feedback to build user confidence; create reusable approaches that can scale across regions while respecting genuine process and risk differences.

Lead a Lean, High-impact Team

Build and coach a small team with commercial judgment, hands-on capability and delivery discipline; mobilize a federated network of Finance champions, process owners and enterprise specialists.
Create a culture of curiosity, constructive challenge, accountability and collaboration, including the confidence to recommend "not AI" when appropriate.
Represent Finance in enterprise AI forums and lead by example as both sponsor and practitioner: demonstrate tools, share what works and acknowledge limitations.

About You

A degree in Finance, Business, Technology, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience, is expected.
Significant experience leading AI, data, automation or digital transformation in a complex organization, with demonstrated outcomes beyond proofs of concept.
Experience navigating architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance and risk requirements without losing sight of business value or delivery pace.
Deeper practical experience with Copilot Cowork or Claude Cowork, including a proven record of deploying agentic workflows and demonstrating value in another organization.
Demonstrated hands-on experience building, testing and deploying AI agents, preferably in Microsoft Copilot Studio, with examples you personally created or materially developed.
Experience in an engineering, professional-services or project-based business; familiarity with enterprise Finance platforms, including Oracle-based environments.
Working knowledge of generative AI, agents, analytics and intelligent automation, sufficient to build focused solutions and challenge complex technical designs.
Strong understanding of Finance processes and decisions, ideally including FP&A, reporting, project or contract performance, working capital and financial controls.
Evidence of moving solutions beyond demonstrations to adoption, changed workflows and measurable business outcomes.
Active, capable use of Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT or Claude in day-to-day professional work, with sound judgment about approved tools, sensitive information and human review.
Proven ability to build investment cases, evaluate total cost and alternatives, establish benefit baselines and demonstrate return on investment.
Exceptional collaboration, executive communication and matrix leadership skills; sound judgment about when to scale, simplify or stop.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Make the most of diverse opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise.

And take advantage of our hybrid working culture and generous time-off policies to balance a fulfilling career with your personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

About AtkinsRéalis

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Find out more.

Additional information

Please consult our Privacy Notice on our Careers site to know more about how we collect, use, and transfer your Personal Data.

By submitting your personal information to AtkinsRéalis, you confirm that you have read and accept our Privacy Notice.

Clear and tested experience in leading cross-functional teams and managing P&L responsibilities

In-depth knowledge of Data Engineering, Data Science, and AI technologies and tools

Track record of being a dynamic decision-maker and having adaptability in a quickly changing environment
Deep knowledge of customer experience strategies and digital transformation

Exceptional leadership and people management skills, inspiring and motivating cross-functional teams
Excellent strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities, with strong business acumen

Outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present complex ideas effectively to C-level and Executive audiences

jobs.title: Head of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Enterprise AI | Manufacturing | Supply Chain | Private Label | Business Transformation

Scope:
Enterprise-wide, multi-site
Locations:
Toronto, Wixom, Chicago and Sardis; regular site travel required
Role model:
High-leverage individual contributor / transformation owner, supported by internal teams, vendors and consultants
Primary measure:
Measurable business value from AI-enabled process and decision improvement

About the Company

The company is a large contract manufacturer and packager of household cleaning products serving branded and private-label customers across North America.

Position Overview

This position will define and drive the company’s practical adoption of artificial intelligence across the business. This is not primarily an IT infrastructure, software development or research role. It is a business transformation role for someone who can understand how the company makes money, how its plants and customer programs operate, where decisions and processes break down, and where AI can create measurable advantage.
The person will own the AI opportunity portfolio from discovery through value realization: identifying and sizing high-value use cases, redesigning workflows and decision processes, determining data and technology requirements, coordinating internal and external technical resources, guiding pilots into scaled deployment, building organizational capability, and measuring financial and operational results.
The role will initially operate as a high-leverage individual contributor. Success depends less on personally building every model and more on asking the right questions, selecting the right problems, challenging vendors and specialists, and ensuring solutions are adopted in the business and sustained.

Core Mandate

Build a phased enterprise AI roadmap tied directly to company business priorities, plant economics and customer-program economics.
Create a repeatable method for finding, evaluating and prioritizing AI opportunities based on value, feasibility, data readiness, adoption requirements and risk.
Turn selected opportunities into implemented solutions that change how work is performed and how decisions are made, rather than producing disconnected pilots or demonstrations.
Develop the internal operating model, governance, external partner ecosystem and AI literacy required to scale successful solutions across facilities and functions.
Own value realization: each meaningful initiative should have a baseline, business case, accountable owner, adoption plan and measurable outcome.

Key Responsibilities

1. AI Strategy, Opportunity Portfolio & Roadmap
Develop and maintain the enterprise AI transformation roadmap across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, quality, R&D/formulation, commercialization, commercial/customer processes, finance and supporting functions.
Build a decision and process inventory to identify repetitive, high-value, data-rich business situations where AI, automation or advanced analytics can materially improve outcomes.
Prioritize use cases by expected economic value, strategic importance, feasibility, data readiness, scalability, change impact and risk; stop low-value or poorly grounded initiatives early.
Continuously assess the AI landscape—including generative AI, agents, machine learning, computer vision, optimization, digital twins and industrial AI—and translate relevant advances into practical recommendations for the company.

2. Manufacturing & Intelligent Operations
Work directly with plant, engineering, maintenance, quality and operations leaders to identify AI-enabled improvements in process control, batch optimization, yield, quality, line performance, changeovers, reliability, downtime, energy, waste and safety.
Identify opportunities for predictive quality, predictive maintenance, machine vision, intelligent scheduling, digital twins and decision support where the operational data and economics justify them.
Design pilots with clear operating baselines and success measures, then create the playbook required to replicate proven solutions across relevant sites and assets.
Ensure AI is embedded into standard operating processes and decision routines with appropriate human oversight, rather than operating as a separate technology layer.

3. Contract Manufacturing, Customer Programs & Commercialization
Apply AI to the full customer-program lifecycle, including opportunity identification, RFQ/quoting, formulation and product development, packaging/specification management, commercialization, production readiness, fulfillment and ongoing program profitability.
Develop better decision support around bid/no-bid, pricing floors, capacity implications, changeover burden, working capital, forecast reliability, customer service requirements and true program economics.
Explore AI-enabled customer and category intelligence that can identify assortment gaps, private-label opportunities, cross-sell opportunities, packaging gaps and product concepts the company can proactively bring to customers.
Use connected data to improve launch execution, specification/artwork consistency, retailer/customer compliance, deductions/chargebacks and root-cause learning from complaints and service failures.

4. Supply Chain, Procurement & Planning
Identify AI opportunities in forecasting, S&OP/IBP, inventory, raw-material planning, procurement, sourcing, supplier intelligence, production scheduling, warehousing and transportation.
Improve the company’s ability to predict customer demand and forecast reliability, allocate capacity and materials, sequence production and manage working capital under uncertainty.
Use AI to surface exceptions and recommended actions so teams can spend less time assembling information and more time resolving the decisions that matter.

5. Data, Technology & Partner Orchestration
Define practical data-readiness requirements for AI use cases and work with IT, plant systems, Finance, Quality, R&D and other data owners to improve access, context and reliability.
Evaluate AI platforms, specialist vendors, consultants and implementation partners based on business fit, architecture, security, scalability, interoperability, total cost and expected value.
Make informed build-vs-buy-vs-partner recommendations and ensure the company retains appropriate knowledge, control and portability as capabilities scale.
Act as the business product owner for AI initiatives while technical specialists own the detailed engineering, infrastructure and model construction where appropriate.

6. Governance, Risk & Responsible AI
Establish proportionate AI governance covering privacy, cybersecurity, customer confidentiality and IP, data access, model risk, human oversight, transparency, validation and regulatory requirements.
Create clear decision rights defining where AI may inform, recommend or execute, and where human approval remains required.
Ensure use cases involving regulated products, quality systems or customer-sensitive information are developed and validated with the appropriate functional experts.

7. Change, Adoption & Capability Building
Build AI literacy among executives, plant leaders, managers and frontline users through practical education tied to the company’s work rather than generic technology training.
Create a network of functional and site champions who can identify opportunities, support adoption and help scale what works.
Address resistance, role changes, trust and skill gaps directly; redesign processes and responsibilities where AI changes how work should be performed.
Communicate wins, failures and lessons openly so the organization becomes progressively better at selecting and deploying AI.

8. Value Realization & Executive Reporting
Build business cases and establish measurable baselines before meaningful investment is made.
Track value across cost, margin, working capital, throughput, yield, quality, service, innovation speed, risk reduction and employee productivity as relevant to each use case.
Maintain a portfolio view of AI investments, adoption and realized value, and report progress, risks and priorities to senior leadership.
Treat adoption and sustained operating impact—not the number of pilots launched—as the primary definition of success.

Illustrative Initial Opportunity Areas

Manufacturing:
Batch/process optimization; predictive quality; machine vision; maintenance/reliability; line scheduling/changeovers; energy, yield and waste.
Product & R&D:
Formulation optimization; raw-material substitution; experiment prioritization; specification knowledge; faster customer/product development.
Supply Chain:
Demand forecasting; customer forecast quality; inventory; procurement; supplier intelligence; production planning; logistics and working capital.
Private Label / Commercial:
RFQ and quote intelligence; bid/no-bid; customer/program profitability; assortment whitespace; cross-sell; customer opportunity intelligence.
Commercialization & Quality:
Launch control tower; specification/artwork consistency; complaints-to-root-cause; regulatory/product-stewardship impact analysis; customer compliance.
Knowledge & Administration:
Plant/SOP/maintenance knowledge assistants; document processing; management reporting; finance and back-office workflow automation.

Candidate Profile

The strongest candidate is likely an experienced manufacturing, operations, supply-chain, analytics or business-transformation leader who has become sophisticated in AI—not necessarily a career AI researcher or software engineer. Because modern generative AI and agent technologies are new, depth of practical use and demonstrated outcomes matter more than an arbitrary number of years with “AI” in a title.
Typically 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, supply chain, digital/business transformation, advanced analytics or a closely related environment.
Demonstrated recent ownership of meaningful AI, advanced-analytics, automation or digital-transformation initiatives from problem definition through deployment and measurable business impact.
Strong understanding of manufacturing economics and operational processes; experience in process manufacturing, CPG, chemicals, private label, contract manufacturing or other complex multi-site industrial environments is strongly preferred.
Practical fluency in current AI capabilities, including generative AI, AI agents, machine learning, predictive analytics, optimization, computer vision and intelligent automation. The candidate does not need to personally code every solution, but must understand enough to challenge technical assumptions and vendors.
Strong financial and business acumen: can build a credible business case, quantify value, understand trade-offs and distinguish an interesting technology from an investable business opportunity.
Proven ability to lead through influence across plant operations, engineering, supply chain, quality, R&D, Finance, IT/data teams and senior leadership without necessarily owning those functions directly.
Experience working with external consultants, software/platform providers and specialist technical partners; capable of making build/buy/partner decisions.
Excellent facilitation and communication skills, from plant-floor working sessions to executive presentations.
Comfort with ambiguity and an entrepreneurial bias toward practical experimentation, learning and scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, Computer/Data Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degree is beneficial but not required.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly among company facilities as projects require.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 Days
Visit key company sites and build a grounded view of operations, customer-program workflows, current systems/data and organizational readiness.
Create an enterprise AI opportunity map and prioritized initial roadmap with business cases, data requirements,

jobs.title: Director, AI Delivery
jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What you'll be doing

Our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) team within Operations helps turn high-value opportunities into practical solutions that improve how work gets done across the business. As the Director, AI Delivery, you'll lead the end-to-end delivery of a growing portfolio of AI and Generative AI initiatives, from opportunity identification and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and value realization. You'll lead and develop a team of data scientists while creating the structure, operating rhythm, and accountability needed to deliver consistently in a complex enterprise environment. Working closely with Operations leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll translate business problems into clear, well-scoped initiatives with measurable outcomes. You'll also manage competing priorities across the portfolio, remove barriers to progress, and help ensure solutions are successfully embedded into business workflows. Success in this role means building a delivery organization that scales effectively, delivers predictably, and creates measurable business impact.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How you'll succeed

Lead delivery excellence
- Own the end-to-end delivery of the Operations AI portfolio, from intake and prioritization through development, production, adoption, and realized value. Create clear ownership, execution discipline, and accountability across initiatives.
Build trusted business partnerships

Citi, the leading global bank, has approximately 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. About the Team:

Citi is looking for a Lead AI/ML Data Scientist
to join the Olympus Data Reconciliation and Engineering team, where you will shape the next generation of AI and machine learning capabilities powering enterprise-scale reconciliation across global processing hubs.

In this role, you will drive the full lifecycle of ML model development — from ideation and architecture through to deployment and adoption — delivering measurable impact across Capital Markets operations, risk, and finance. Your work will sit at the intersection of advanced data science and real-world financial systems, influencing outcomes at a global scale.

Responsibilities:

Design, build, and deploy AI and machine learning models — including Agentic AI and Generative AI solutions — to solve complex reconciliation and data engineering challenges at enterprise scale.
Lead the end-to-end ML model development lifecycle, from requirements gathering and data preprocessing through to ensemble modeling, validation, and production integration.
Analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured financial data to uncover trends, patterns, and opportunities for optimization across banking platforms.
Define and deliver ML model roadmaps in collaboration with technical and business teams, ensuring alignment with project timelines, budgets, and Citi's architecture standards.
Translate complex data findings into clear visualizations and strategic recommendations that inform decisions made by senior business and technology leaders.
Partner with engineering, operations, and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless model integration, long-term scalability, and reliable performance in production environments.
Identify and communicate technology risks and their business implications, developing mitigation strategies and maintaining transparency with stakeholders at all levels.
Maintain comprehensive model documentation and support knowledge transfer to ensure continuity and adoption across teams.

Technical Expertise:

6+ years hands-on experience in AI/ML development and big data engineering within Financial Services, Insurance, or Telecom environments
Expert-level proficiency in Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Pandas, NumPy), R (caret, tidyverse, mlr3), and SQL (PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL)
Deep technical knowledge implementing supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms: linear/logistic regression, neural networks (CNN, RNN, LSTM, Transformers), k-means clustering, DBSCAN, decision trees (CART, C4.5), and ensemble methods (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost)
Proven experience building and deploying Agentic AI and LLM-based solutions using:
LangGraph for complex agent orchestration and state management
LangChain for chain-of-thought reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Agent Development Kit (ADK) for enterprise-grade autonomous agent development

Beneficial Skills & Qualifications:

Hands-on experience with advanced statistical modeling: Generalized Linear Models (GLM), Random Forest, Gradient Boosting (AdaBoost, XGBoost), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques including text mining, topic modeling (LDA), and sentiment analysis
Experience with model versioning and experiment tracking tools (Mlflow, Weights & Biases, DVC)
Proficiency with Git/GitHub/Bitbucket for version control and collaborative development
Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines for ML model deployment (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions)
Familiarity with data visualization libraries (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly) and BI tools (Tableau, Power BI)
Experience with real-time streaming data frameworks (Kafka, Kinesis)
Passion for staying current with emerging AI/ML frameworks, research papers, and open-source contributions

Under the leadership of the Vice President, Integrated Management Systems, the Director, Enterprise Solutions – Finance and Operations is responsible for the strategy, evolution, operations, and value creation of the platforms that support Pomerleau’s finance functions and construction operations.

This mandate includes platforms that support accounting, payroll, accounts payable and receivable, procurement, project financial management, and construction operations. Working closely with the Finance function and Construction business units, the Director translates business priorities into functional and technology capabilities, ensuring that platforms effectively meet organizational needs.

Working closely with the Finance function and Construction business units, the Director translates business priorities into functional and technology capabilities, ensuring that platforms effectively meet organizational needs.

The Director leads the functional and technical teams, as well as external partners, responsible for platform evolution, integration, operations, and support. They are accountable for platform stability, performance, user adoption, and the value generated for the organization.

Hatfield, a proudly Canadian company, has been serving our clients and our community for over 50 years. We have been recognized as one of Canada’s Top SME Employers in 2025. Financial Oversight And Reporting

Strategic Initiatives

Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

Full time, 40 hours per week, flexible between 7am and 7pm EST. This role is client facing.

The role

You carry a portfolio of eCommerce clients as their strategic finance partner. You lead financial reviews with founders, own forecasting and cash flow strategy, and make sure the numbers tell the story of the business rather than just closing correctly.

Our clients are 7 to 9 figure eCommerce and digital first brands, usually in high growth. You will work alongside our Accounting Managers and Controllers, reviewing their month end work before it reaches the client, and in some cases working directly with accountants. Portfolio size varies with client size and complexity. What stays constant is that you are holding several businesses in your head at once and switching context cleanly between them.

You work a 40 hour week aligned to EST, flexible between 7am and 7pm. You can live anywhere in Canada, and you are welcome to work from abroad for up to two months a year while staying on EST hours. This is not an in house finance role and it is not oversight only. You will build models yourself, present to founders yourself, and be in the detail when the detail matters.

⭐ Must have

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance
Experience managing several clients or business units at once, rather than a single in house employer
Experience reviewing month end work produced by others, for logic as well as accuracy
Advanced financial modelling and forecasting, hands on
Strong understanding of full cycle accounting and financial operations
Confidence presenting to founders and executives. You will be leading these conversations, not supporting them.
English at C1 level or above, written and spoken. Our clients are North American and this role is client facing.

✨ Nice to have

CPA designation, or your country's equivalent. In progress counts.
MBA
eCommerce or consumer products exposure
Experience across varied industries. Retail, manufacturing, and multi industry backgrounds translate particularly well here.
QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite. We do not expect all three.
FP&A leadership in a high growth environment

✅ What you will do

Act as the trusted finance advisor to founders across your client portfolio
Review month end work from Accounting Managers and Controllers before it reaches the client
Lead KPI, profitability, and unit economics reviews
Build and refine forecasting models and cash flow projections
Guide clients on liquidity, financing needs, and capital allocation
Present financial reviews directly to client leadership
Keep accounting operations, financial insight, and client strategy connected

🔍 What the job actually looks like

Client review meetings are the spine of the month, and preparation for them is the bulk of the work
You get real ownership of your portfolio fast. That is the upside and the expectation.
You will be reviewing month end work regularly, not occasionally
You will be presenting to founders regularly, not occasionally
You have biweekly strategic finance office hours with our founder to pressure test your thinking and get quick answers
Some of our processes are mature and others are still being built. When you hit a gap, we expect you to help close it.

🚫 This role is not for you if

You have only ever worked in house for a single business and prefer it that way
You want to step back from hands on modelling and analysis
You are uncomfortable being the person in the room delivering hard numbers to a founder
You want a process that is already finished

We promote from within based on performance and impact.

🔥 Fully remote and async first:
You will report directly to our CEO.

💙 How we hire

Scenario based assessment, reviewed by our leadership team

Offer. If it is a mutual fit, we move quickly.

Le poste

Vous prenez en charge un portefeuille de clients en commerce électronique à titre de partenaire financier stratégique. Vous dirigez les analyses financières avec les fondateurs, vous êtes responsable des prévisions et de la stratégie de trésorerie, et vous veillez à ce que les chiffres racontent réellement l'histoire de l'entreprise, et pas seulement à ce que la clôture soit exacte.

Nos clients sont des marques de commerce électronique et des entreprises numériques dont les revenus se chiffrent en millions ou en dizaines de millions, généralement en forte croissance. Vous travaillerez aux côtés de nos gestionnaires comptables et de nos contrôleurs, en révisant leur travail de fin de mois avant qu'il ne parvienne au client, et dans certains cas directement avec les comptables. La taille du portefeuille varie selon l'envergure et la complexité des clients. Ce qui demeure constant, c'est que vous gérez plusieurs entreprises en parallèle et que vous passez de l'une à l'autre avec aisance.

Vous travaillez 40 heures par semaine selon le fuseau HNE, avec souplesse entre 7 h et 19 h. Vous pouvez résider partout au Canada, et vous pouvez travailler de l'étranger jusqu'à deux mois par année, à condition de demeurer aligné sur les heures HNE. Il ne s'agit ni d'un poste de finance à l'interne, ni d'un rôle de supervision seulement. Vous construirez les modèles vous-même, vous présenterez aux fondateurs vous-même, et vous serez dans le détail lorsque le détail compte.

⭐ Exigences

jobs.description:
EvenUp is on a mission to close the justice gap using technology and AI. We empower personal injury lawyers and victims to get the justice they deserve. Our products enable law firms to secure faster settlements, higher payouts, and better outcomes for victims injured through no fault of their own in vehicle collisions, accidents, natural disasters, and more.

We are one of the fastest-growing vertical SaaS companies in history, and we are just getting started. EvenUp is backed by top VCs, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Bain Capital Ventures, SignalFire, and Lightspeed. We are looking to expand our team with talented, driven, and collaborative individuals who seek to have a lasting impact. Learn more at www.evenuplaw.com.

The Director of FP&A, R&D acts as the strategic finance partner to Engineering, Product, and Data/ML leadership, owning the R&D operating plan and establishing LLM economics as a fundamental financial discipline. This role manages the P&L for R&D headcount and Cost of Revenue (CoR) for AI in production, driving efficiency through direct engagement with our data stack (BigQuery/dbt).

What You'll Do

Partner day to day with engineering, product, and data leaders as their trusted finance counterpart.
Build the analyses that shape build-vs-buy, pricing, and infrastructure decisions.
Support foundation-model and cloud vendor negotiations with data-backed positions.
Deliver clear, concise reporting and variance commentary to the CFO, FP&A leadership, and the board.
Own the R&D budget, forecast, and headcount plan across Engineering, Product, and Data/ML. Drive the re-forecast cycle and keep hiring plans tied to output and priorities.
Make LLM/inference and cloud compute cost a first-class, closely monitored metric. Build the model that tracks unit costs; monitor spend daily; and partner with engineering to find and defend efficiency. This is not a monthly-close afterthought, it's a core operating metric of the business.
Own the connection between usage, inference cost, and gross margin. Model the margin impact of new products, pricing changes, and model/infrastructure choices, and make the tradeoffs legible to leadership.
Bring financial rigor to major R&D spend decisions including foundation-model and API contracts, cloud commitments, data, and dev tooling, including negotiation support and ROI cases.

What We Look For

8+ years in FP&A / corporate finance, with meaningful time supporting R&D, Engineering, or a technical/product org.
Deep comfort with SaaS and AI/usage-based economics: CoR, gross margin, unit economics, and how infrastructure/inference cost drives them.
Strong SQL (BigQuery a major plus) and expert Excel/Sheets modeling, with clean, maintainable model architecture.
Strong grasp of how R&D spend flows through the P&L.
Ability to be a genuine partner to technical leaders, holding substantive conversations with engineering or ML leads to translate technical work into financial views.
Precise, low-ego, self-directed, and concise work ethic.
Nice to have: Experience at a high-growth AI/ML company, familiarity with modern data stacks, contract negotiation experience, people management experience, and CPA/CA/CFA.
Nice to have: Familiarity with a modern data stack (dbt, EPMs) and building repeatable, auditable finance pipelines.

Benefits & Perks:

As part of our total rewards package, we offer attractive benefits and perks to our employees, including:

Choice of medical, dental, and vision insurance plans for you and your family.
Additional insurance coverage options for life, accident, or critical illness.
Flexible paid time off, sick leave, short-term and long-term disability.
10 US observed holidays, and Canadian statutory holidays by province.
A home office stipend.
401(k) for US-based employees and RRSP for Canada-based employees.
Paid parental leave.
A local in-person meet-up program.
Hubs in San Francisco and Toronto.

(Please note the above benefits & perks are for full-time employees)

Other.™ is raising the bar in the North American advertising industry, setting a new standard for measurable impact, transparency, and accountability, for both our team and the clients we partner with.

We're a privately owned, Toronto-based team of about 50, led by a small Leadership Team. Our work runs on Propel™, our proprietary operating methodology, and PerformanceLock™, our outcome-linked compensation model, so clients get a system that's been refined across hundreds of engagements rather than a team starting from scratch on every account.

Our growth speaks for itself: we've been named to The Globe & Mail's list of Canada's Top Growing Companies for three consecutive years, and to the Financial Times' The Americas' Fastest Growing Companies 2026 list. Our headquarters is in Toronto's Financial District, steps from Union Station, with a second office steps from Parliament Hill in Ottawa. We operate as a hybrid team, with no in-office mandate.

What You’d Be Up To

As Director of Finance, you’ll play a critical role in shaping the financial health, operational efficiency, and multi-entity growth of the company. You’ll serve as the primary in-house financial anchor, balancing direct oversight of day-to-day operations across our Canadian and US entities with strategic partnership at the executive level, ensuring we’re running with financial precision today and set up to scale cleanly tomorrow.

: Direct management of in-house finance operations across Canadian and US entities, with direct oversight and day-to-day operational leadership of fractional resources, including a fractional Controller and a fractional Bookkeeper.

Oversee intercompany accounting, transfer pricing compliance, and intercompany agreements to ensure clean multi-entity consolidation and regulatory alignment.
Coordinate cross-border tax strategy, corporate filings, and state-level compliance (e.g., state sales tax, state income tax, nexus considerations) with specialized external advisors.

Treasury, Cash & Foreign Exchange Management

Own consolidated liquidity visibility across CAD and USD accounts; build and maintain rolling 13-week cash flow models to drive proactive cash planning and inform CFO decision-making.
Operationalize treasury management strategies established by the CFO while ensuring seamless working capital across entities.
Monitor FX risk across multi-currency revenue and expense streams; execute CFO-approved hedging strategies, forward contracts, and intercompany currency transfers to protect against volatility.
Manage day-to-day banking workflows, user access, account administration, and credit line monitoring across Canadian and US financial institutions.

Systems, Process Improvement & Vendor Management

Evaluate, implement and optimize the finance tech stack
Identify and execute automation and system integrations to streamline financial workflows, accelerate month-end closes, and eliminate manual reporting errors across entities.
Manage relationships and service agreements with software providers and external financial vendors in both regions.

Strategic FP&A, Commercial Insight & Executive Advisory

Partner directly with the CFO on consolidated budgeting, multi-year forecasting, and strategic capital allocation across business units.
Analyze agency-specific metrics—including client profitability, billable realization rates, and team utilization—to advise leadership on pricing structures and resource planning.
Build dynamic models to evaluate new business scenarios, US expansion initiatives, and service lines.

Experience in advertising, marketing services, or professional services agencies (managing billable rates, project profitability, and client retainers) strongly preferred.

Practical familiarity with multi-entity financial management, consolidated reporting, and cross-border (US/Canada) tax and regulatory structures (hands-on or via external specialized advisors).

Strong knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, experience managing cash flow modeling, and experience selecting & implementing financial tech into an organization.

Strong analytical skills, high ownership, meticulous attention to financial detail, and exceptional collaboration skills across executive leadership teams.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.
Ensures the Museum maintains its tax-exempt charitable status and meets all related tax compliance requirements, including tax reporting, disbursement quotas, and dealings with the CRA.
Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.
Coordinate the integration of enterprise risk management with business continuity planning and reporting to the Board and relevant Committees.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Chief Financial Officer based in Canada.

The Chief Financial Officer will lead the financial strategy and operations of a rapidly scaling technology business, helping shape its next stage of growth. This executive-level role combines strategic leadership with hands-on operational oversight across financial planning, accounting, reporting, and capital strategy. Working closely with the CEO, executive team, and Board, the CFO will strengthen financial discipline, improve decision-making, and build scalable systems and processes. The role requires a proven track record of scaling SaaS or technology companies, navigating complex financial milestones, and preparing organizations for future financing or strategic events. The successful candidate will develop a high-performing finance organization while ensuring reliable forecasting, robust controls, and credible financial reporting. This is a remote opportunity for a senior leader based in Canada or the United States, with required travel to Ottawa and Toronto.

Accountabilities

Lead and develop the FP&A and Accounting functions, establishing clear priorities, strengthening collaboration, and ensuring accurate, timely financial deliverables.
Assess existing financial operations, identify process gaps, and work directly with teams to resolve issues and improve operational effectiveness.
Simplify and document core finance processes, enhance data quality, and introduce automation to reduce manual effort, errors, and reliance on workarounds.
Oversee financial planning and analysis, including budgets, forecasts, financial models, and performance analysis, translating insights into actionable business decisions.
Direct accounting operations, financial close processes, audits, reporting, and internal controls while ensuring compliance with applicable GAAP and IFRS requirements.
Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital requirements, financing opportunities, and investor communications.
Bring financial rigor to company-wide decisions involving pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Evaluate acquisitions and strategic partnerships, leading financial modelling, valuation, due diligence, and post-transaction integration planning.
Build and coach a finance organization capable of supporting significant revenue growth, with systems, controls, and talent aligned to long-term business needs.
Ensure forecasting, financial reporting, and Board materials are accurate, credible, and trusted by executive stakeholders.
Prepare the organization for future fundraising, financing, or other strategic milestones well in advance.

Requirements

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including previous CFO experience within a scaling business.
Demonstrated success scaling SaaS or technology companies from approximately $50 million to more than $200 million in revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep expertise in financial planning and analysis, including strategic planning, forecasting, financial modelling, and performance management.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising, such as Series C, D, or E, or experience operating in public markets.
Strong understanding of SaaS metrics, recurring revenue models, and the financial drivers of technology businesses.
Solid knowledge of GAAP and IFRS, compliance frameworks, internal controls, and audit oversight.
Proven ability to lead, mentor, and develop high-performing finance teams and senior functional leaders.
Strong strategic judgment and analytical skills, with the ability to balance detailed operational problem-solving with a company-wide perspective.
Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with CEOs, executive teams, and Boards, influencing decisions through clear financial insights and sound judgment.
Experience with mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration, is an asset.
Experience in a Canadian business with US and international operations, including multi-currency environments and cross-border tax considerations, is an asset.
Must be a Canadian or American citizen or otherwise eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Must be willing to undergo a criminal records check upon hire and comply with applicable organizational security policies and standards.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Your CFO Opportunity Starts Here

Ready for the Seat You've Been Working Toward?

Not every great CFO starts with the title.

Many earn it through leadership, execution, business acumen, and the ability to help an organization reach its next level.

If you're a VP Finance, Director of Finance, or rising finance leader who has been waiting for the right opportunity to step into a CFO role, this may be exactly what you've been looking for.

Beam is seeking an ambitious, strategic, and hands-on Chief Financial Officer who wants to make a meaningful impact on a growing healthcare organization. This is a unique opportunity to join a collaborative leadership team, work directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a dynamic, physician-led business.

We believe great CFOs are more than financial experts. They're business leaders. They influence strategy. They develop people. They create accountability. They see opportunities others miss. They help organizations grow.

This role is ideal for someone who wants to roll up their sleeves, build credibility, drive results, and ultimately prove they belong at the executive leadership table.

You'll have responsibility for Finance, Accounting, Billing, Revenue Cycle, Treasury, Financial Planning & Analysis, Physician Compensation, and Information Technology, while helping lead strategic planning, operational performance, and organizational growth.

If you're looking for a role where you can build, lead, influence, and leave your mark, we'd like to meet you.

ROLE MANDATE

The CFO is responsible for leading the organization's accounting, financial reporting, and treasury functions, ensuring the delivery of accurate, timely, and meaningful financial information while maintaining strong internal controls and disciplined financial management practices.
As a hands-on member of the senior leadership team, the CFO serves as a trusted business partner, providing reliable financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, cash flow oversight, and business analysis to support strategic decision-making, operational excellence, and the achievement of the organization's objectives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the monthly, quarterly and annual financial close and ensure accurate, timely financial statements.
Lead general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll oversight, reconciliations and the general ledger.
Maintain accounting policies, internal controls and approval processes; identify and remediate control weaknesses.
Coordinate the annual external audit and support tax compliance, regulatory reporting and year-end requirements.
Prepare annual budgets, forecasts, variance analysis and recurring management.
Monitor cash balances, working capital, collections and payment processes; support treasury and banking administration.
Lead and develop the accounting team while improving processes, documentation, systems and automation.

SHORT TERM PRIORITIES

Standardize and accelerate the month-end close with dependable reporting deadlines.
Strengthen reconciliations, internal controls, accounting policies and financial documentation.
Improve accounts receivable, collections, working-capital reporting and cash visibility.
Build useful budget-to-actual and location/service profitability reporting.
Assess accounting team responsibilities and identify opportunities for system and process automation.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

CPA designation strongly preferred.
Approximately 6-12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including Controller, Assistant Controller or senior finance leadership experience.
Strong technical accounting, financial reporting, controls and close-management capabilities.
Experience in a private, entrepreneurial or multi-location operating company preferred.
Hands-on leadership style with the ability to review detail while maintaining strong deadlines and accountability.
Advanced budgeting, forecasting, Excel and financial systems skills; experience improving ERP/reporting processes is an asset.
Healthcare or medical-sector experience is an asset, particularly with multi-location operations, billing or practitioner economics.
Clear communicator who can explain financial results to both finance and non-finance managers.
Proactive, hands-on, and willing to roll up their sleeves.
Strong leadership skills.
Able to think outside the box and find creative solutions.
High energy and driven.
Genuinely passionate about healthcare, MedTech, and innovation.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Accurate and timely reporting
Faster and disciplined close
Strong controls and reconciliations
Improved collections and working capital
Reliable budgets and forecasts
Efficient accounting processes
A capable and accountable finance team

WHY JOIN BEAM?

This is more than a CFO role. It's an opportunity to step into a key leadership position, partner directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization. If you're ready to build, lead, influence, and make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

EQUITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process. If you require accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Thank you for contacting the Government of Nunavut.

Please do not send sensitive or personal information, including (but not limited to): social insurance numbers, birthdates, information of other people, or health information. We will make sure the correct person contacts you if they need more information or if they can answer your question or concern.

This employment opportunity is open to all applicants. Applicants must be currently eligible to work in Canada.

An eligibility list may be created to fill future vacancies.

As this is a term position ending June 2028, current indeterminate Government of Nunavut employees may be offered a competitive transfer assignment for the duration of the term if they are deemed to be the successful candidate, however this is subject to managerial approval.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Corporate Services, the Director, Finance (Director) is the senior financial advisor for the Department of Health. The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land, Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Évaluation des logiciels et analyses de rentabilité

Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences mesurables sur les plans fonctionnel, technique, des données, de la sécurité, de l’intégration, des contrôles, du service et des utilisateurs; diriger les démonstrations, les projets pilotes, les vérifications de références, les grilles d’évaluation, la diligence raisonnable des fournisseurs et la comparaison objective des risques et des solutions de rechange.
Préparer et présenter des analyses de rentabilité pour les décisions d’aller de l’avant ou non, couvrant le coût total de possession, le rendement du capital investi, les échéanciers, les ressources, l’incidence du changement, la formation, l’atténuation des risques, le soutien et les coûts de sortie; soutenir les négociations commerciales et contractuelles.

Gouvernance et responsabilité de la mise en œuvre

Agir à titre de responsable imputable du volet affaires et technologie, en partenariat avec le ou la gestionnaire de projet attitré(e), afin de définir la portée, les résultats, le budget, les ressources, la gouvernance, les jalons, les droits décisionnels, les risques, les communications et les mesures de succès.
Coordonner les parties prenantes et veiller à la conception des processus, à la configuration, aux intégrations, à la conversion des données, aux essais, aux contrôles, à la formation, à la mise en production, au soutien, à la préparation, à la stabilisation, à l’adoption et à la réalisation des bénéfices; faire remonter les lacunes importantes et maintenir la visibilité auprès de la direction.

Gestion du portefeuille, des fournisseurs, des données et des risques

Gérer les budgets logiciels, les licences, l’utilisation, les renouvellements, les fournisseurs, les contrats, les niveaux de service, les indicateurs du portefeuille, la rationalisation et le retrait des solutions.
Collaborer avec les ressources en TI, cybersécurité, protection de la vie privée, affaires juridiques et gestion des risques afin d’encadrer les intégrations, les données, les contrôles d’accès, la continuité des activités, les risques liés aux tiers, l’intelligence artificielle et l’automatisation.

Leadership du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes

Établir des relations de confiance avec les associé(e)s, les dirigeant(e)s, le personnel, les fournisseurs et les prestataires de services; diriger les employé(e)s attitré(e)s et les équipes interfonctionnelles en assurant une responsabilisation claire et une forte orientation vers le service.
Diriger les communications, la formation, l’adoption, la documentation, le soutien et la propriété des applications; développer des ambassadeurs internes, contribuer au plan d’affaires du cabinet et tenir le ou la COFO ainsi que les parties prenantes informés.

Autorité et responsabilité

Responsable du portefeuille de logiciels, de la feuille de route des applications, des normes de gouvernance et de la direction des équipes de mise en œuvre des TI et des processus dans le cadre de la stratégie et des budgets approuvés; peut exiger les examens appropriés en matière d’affaires, de sécurité, de protection de la vie privée, d’intégration, de contrôle et de mise en œuvre.
Recommande la sélection, le séquencement, le renouvellement, l’expansion, la consolidation ou le retrait des logiciels; peut suspendre ou faire remonter les préoccupations non résolues et est responsable de la qualité des recommandations, de la gouvernance de la mise en œuvre, de l’adoption, de la stabilisation et des bénéfices approuvés.

Mesures de succès

Gérer un inventaire à jour des logiciels, une propriété claire, une gouvernance rigoureuse, une feuille de route approuvée, des analyses de rentabilité crédibles et des dépenses contrôlées.
Réaliser les mises en œuvre avec une gouvernance, une préparation, des contrôles, une adoption et un soutien durable efficaces, ainsi qu’avec la réalisation des bénéfices approuvés.
Obtenir des améliorations mesurables en matière d’efficacité, de capacité, de qualité, de fiabilité des données, d’expérience employé et client, de performance des fournisseurs, de gestion des risques et de confiance des parties prenantes.

Les Qualifications Qui Comptent

Baccalauréat en systèmes d’information, administration des affaires, comptabilité, finance, informatique, génie ou dans un domaine connexe; une combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience sera considérée.
Sept années ou plus d’expérience progressive en logiciels, systèmes d’affaires, amélioration des processus, transformation technologique, gestion de produits ou gestion de programmes, dont au moins trois années dans un rôle de leadership ou de responsabilité à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Une expérience dans un cabinet comptable ou un autre environnement de services professionnels est privilégiée, avec une compréhension des décisions dirigées par les associé(e)s, du service à la clientèle soumis à des échéanciers, de la confidentialité et du changement entre les groupes de pratique.
Succès démontré dans la direction d’évaluations de logiciels, d’analyses de rentabilité, de sélection de fournisseurs et de mise en œuvre de solutions SaaS à l’échelle du cabinet ou de l’entreprise.
Expérience pratique de la cartographie et de la refonte des processus, des exigences, des essais, de la formation, de la gestion du changement et de la réalisation des bénéfices.
