jobs.title: Chief Technology and Information Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

POSITION PURPOSE SUMMARY

The Chief Technology and Information Officer (CTIO) provides enterprise leadership and strategic direction for technology, information systems, data, cybersecurity and digital capabilities across The Salvation Army Canada and Bermuda Territory.

As a senior organizational leader, the CTIO ensures technology strategy and investment support The Salvation Army’s mission, strategic priorities and operational needs. The role is accountable for technology, cybersecurity and resilience, enterprise systems, data and digital capability, technology operations, vendor partnerships, financial stewardship and the ongoing development of a high-performing technology function.

Working across a large, geographically dispersed and decentralized organization, the CTIO builds trusted relationships with leaders and stakeholders, balances enterprise consistency with operational realities, and drives technology adoption and organizational efficiencies in a way that reflects The Salvation Army’s mission, values and culture.

Accountabilities

Mission, Culture and Organizational Leadership

Authentically lead in alignment with The Salvation Army’s mission, vision, values, Christian identity and spiritual foundations, recognizing that its social and community services are expressions of its higher purpose to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in communities.
Ensure technology strategy, investment and decision-making ultimately enable people, ministry and services to advance the mission.
Contribute as an enterprise leader to organizational strategy, priorities and decisions beyond the technology portfolio.
Balance enterprise standards and priorities with legitimate operational, geographic and ministry-specific needs.

Executive and People Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing technology leadership team with clear accountability, a service-oriented culture, strong succession and workforce planning, and the appropriate balance of internal and external capability.
Provide strategic advice to senior leadership, translating complex technology, cybersecurity, data and digital issues into clear organizational choices, risks, opportunities and investment decisions.
Lead significant organizational change associated with technology transformation, recognizing that successful adoption depends on people, process, culture and technology.
Build strong relationships with operational leaders and users to understand needs and continuously improve technology effectiveness.
Model strong stewardship, integrity and accountability in leadership and decision-making.

Enterprise Technology Strategy

Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise technology strategy aligned with organizational priorities and mission.
Stabilize and simplify the technology environment, strengthening reliability, integration, interoperability and sustainable adoption.
Optimize existing technology platforms and investments before introducing new solutions.
Improve connectivity and interoperability between systems to create a more seamless technology and user environment.
Establish technology roadmaps, portfolio governance and prioritization that sequence investments appropriately and balance innovation, affordability, risk, organizational readiness and capacity.
Lead targeted modernization and transformation where it creates clear organizational value, while assessing emerging technologies thoughtfully.
Oversee the technology project and investment portfolio, ensuring appropriate governance, stakeholder engagement and benefits realization.

Cybersecurity, Data and Technology Risk

Provide executive oversight of cybersecurity, information security, privacy, technology risk and resilience.
Ensure appropriate controls, governance and compliance are in place to protect organizational information, systems and technology assets.
Maintain effective disaster recovery, business continuity and technology resilience capabilities.
Ensure security, privacy, data protection and risk considerations are embedded in technology investments, vendor relationships and emerging technology adoption.

Technology Operations and Service Delivery

Ensure reliable, secure, responsive and cost-effective delivery of enterprise applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud services, end-user technology and service management.
Establish service standards, performance measures and continuous improvement practices that strengthen user experience and technology effectiveness.
Maintain an enterprise technology architecture that supports integration, scalability, security and future organizational requirements.

Financial, Vendor and Investment Stewardship – Money, Sourcing and Commercial Discipline

Lead technology operating and capital budgets and multi-year investment planning, ensuring investments demonstrate strategic value, affordability and sustainability.
Oversee business cases, cost-benefit analysis and benefits realization for significant technology investments.
Establish effective sourcing strategies and lead strategic vendor relationships, contract performance and commercial negotiations.
Drive cost effectiveness through technology simplification, optimization, disciplined sourcing and effective management of technology assets and services.

Strategic Business Enablement, Data and Artificial Intelligence

Connect technology, data and digital priorities directly to organizational strategy, mission outcomes, service delivery and measurable value.
Act as an enterprise integrator across ministries, functions and geographies, using technology and data to simplify processes, strengthen service delivery and improve decision-making.
Lead enterprise data strategy, governance, stewardship, quality, analytics and reporting to enable trusted and actionable information.
Establish and oversee responsible AI and automation governance, ensuring use cases are mission-aligned, secure, ethical, legally compliant, operationally practical and supported by appropriate human oversight.
Establish governance and performance measures that allow senior leaders to monitor technology value, data maturity, digital adoption and AI readiness.

Education, Experience And Qualifications

Mission and Organizational Alignment

Demonstrated alignment with and ability to authentically lead within The Salvation Army’s mission, values and Christian foundations.
Demonstrated understanding that The Salvation Army’s social and community services are expressions of a broader mission to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in communities.
Ability to operate effectively within a large, complex, values-based and decentralized organization.
Demonstrated commitment to ethical leadership, stewardship, collaboration and service.

Education And Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Engineering or a related discipline is required.
Master’s degree in Business Administration, Technology, Information Systems or a related field may be considered an asset.
Relevant executive technology, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, governance or program management certifications may be an asset.
An equivalent combination of education and significant relevant executive experience may be considered.

Experience and Knowledge

Significant progressive leadership experience in technology, information systems, digital or related discipline, including substantial senior executive or enterprise leadership experience.
Demonstrated success developing and executing enterprise technology strategies and leading transformation or modernization.
Experience leading technology within a large, complex, multi-site and/or geographically dispersed organization.
Broad executive-level understanding of enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, data, integration, digital capability and technology operations.
Demonstrated experience overseeing cybersecurity, technology risk, resilience and business continuity.
Experience with enterprise data governance, analytics and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Significant experience managing technology budgets, investment decisions, strategic vendors and major contracts.
Proven success in building and developing high-performing leadership teams.
Demonstrated experience leading complex organizational change and influencing senior stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience advising executive leadership and governance bodies on technology strategy, investment, cybersecurity, risk and organizational implications.
Experience in a decentralized, faith-based, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector or similarly complex service organization is considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience establishing or maturing enterprise data strategies, data governance, analytics capability and information management practices across a complex organization.
Experience reviewing, governing and deploying artificial intelligence or advanced automation capabilities with appropriate attention to ethics, privacy, cybersecurity, risk, adoption, benefits realization and operational readiness.

Skills And Leadership Capabilities

Strategic enterprise thinker who connects technology, data and digital priorities to organizational strategy and mission outcomes.
Strong executive judgment with the ability to prioritize competing demands and balance innovation, risk, cost, organizational capacity and readiness.
Proven people leader who builds organizational capability, develops senior leaders and creates clarity and accountability.
Exceptional relationship builder and influencer who can navigate a decentralized, relationship-driven organization while advancing enterprise priorities.
Clear and compelling communicator who translates complex technology issues into understandable organizational implications and decisions for technical and non-technical audiences.
Proven people leader who builds organizational capability, develops senior leaders and creates clarity and accountability.
Strong business, financial and commercial acumen, including technology investment, vendor management and benefits realization.
Data-driven and digitally fluent executive who can establish trusted information, enable analytics and guide responsible AI and automation adoption with appropriate governance and human oversight.
Values-based leader who demonstrates integrity, humility, stewardship and a strong service orientation.
Comfortable with complexity and ambiguity, with the ability to bring clarity, structure and direction to challenging organizational situations.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $244,046.40 to $305,052.80 with a maximum of $366,059.20.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

The Salvation Army will provide reasonable accommodation upon request. Please email Recruitment.Accommodations@salvationarmy.ca

Chief Information Officer

Do you believe that technology, data, and digital platforms should open new possibilities? Are you motivated by the opportunity to lead large scale digital transformation while advancing equity, innovation, and employee and student success at one of Canada’s leading post-secondary institutions?

Seneca Polytechnic is seeking a Chief Information Officer
to provide institution-wide leadership and strategic direction for information technology, digital platforms, enterprise systems, and data. Reporting to the Vice President, Students and IT, you will play a critical role in shaping Seneca’s digital future, ensuring secure, reliable, and innovative technology services that support teaching, learning, research, and operations.

In this critical role, you will lead IT modernization, strengthen Seneca’s leadership in artificial intelligence, and partner with academic and administrative leaders to ensure technology investments deliver meaningful organizational value.

How You Approach the Role

Seneca operates in a complex post-secondary environment with rapid technological change, evolving learner needs, and increasing cybersecurity risks. In this context, you will

Set a clear and compelling vision for Seneca’s information technology and digital strategy, aligned with institutional priorities and long-term plans.
Lead the development and execution of a multi-year IT and digital transformation roadmap, including enterprise architecture and technology governance.
Advance innovation by collaboratively identifying and leveraging emerging technologies that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional effectiveness.
Maintain and grow Seneca’s leadership in artificial intelligence, ensuring responsible, ethical, and impactful application across the institution.
Embed principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion into technology strategies, policies, and service delivery.
Build strong partnerships with academic and administrative leaders to translate institutional needs into effective technology solutions.
Foster trust through transparent decision-making, thoughtful communication, and consistent follow through.

What You’ll Do in This Role

As CIO, you will provide strategic, operational, and people leadership across a broad and integrated portfolio, leading a senior IT leadership team and fostering collaboration, accountability, and high performance. You will ensure the secure, reliable, and effective delivery of enterprise technology services while overseeing cybersecurity, data privacy, system resilience, business continuity, and compliance. You will guide the modernization and lifecycle management of enterprise platforms, establish meaningful performance measures, and lead budgeting, resource allocation, vendor management, and contract negotiations. You will also strengthen staff engagement, professional development, and workforce sustainability within a complex and evolving technology environment.

What You Bring

You are a seasoned technology leader who balances strategic vision with operational excellence and brings extensive, progressive experience leading complex IT organizations, enterprise systems, digital transformation, and multi-year initiatives. You exercise strong judgment in managing risk, security, and compliance while enabling innovation, agility, and evidence-based decision-making through data, analytics, and emerging tools. An effective communicator and collaborative partner, you translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable insights and influence diverse stakeholder groups. You have built inclusive, high-performing leadership teams and lead with integrity, accountability, transparency, and respect.

Seneca supports flexible and inclusive work practices, recognizing diverse leadership styles and experiences. We recognize that leadership experience may be gained through a variety of career paths, including community-based work, sector transitions, or lived experience alongside formal roles. A combination of education and experience will be considered.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Director AI Business Solutions will be responsible for guiding and implementing the AI strategy across the Canadian Wealth Management (CWM) businesses, ensuring business strategies, plans and initiatives are executed / delivered in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies and procedures.

The Director AI Business Solutions will be responsible for identifying AI initiatives that are aligned with our strategic objectives, supporting the development and implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives from start (rapid pilots, MVPs) to finish (deployed in production with user adoption). The role will be focused on process improvements, enhancements, or even reimagining them to support the evolution of CWM.

The Director AI Business Solutions will also be responsible for staying current with AI trends and technologies to drive innovation and maintain a competitive market edge in a manner that is compliant and trustworthy in alignment with Scotiabank’s Enterprise AI Governance framework. The role will leverage AI-driven analytics to optimize distribution strategies, enhance efficiency and improve user engagement by identifying patterns, and streamlining processes. This role involves working with cross-functional teams including retail and institutional distribution, finance, operations, product, technology and data.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Align CWM’s AI priorities and initiatives with leadership across the different functional business areas
Define CWM’s AI strategy, vision, and goals in alignment with CWM’s strategic business priorities
Manage AI development, demand portfolio, while maintaining an opportunity pipeline
Define objectives, metrics, KRI’s, and Key Results (OKRs) for the Business Solutions Program

Conduct executive AI labs to deep dive the value of AI in investment management and how to drive a culture change towards AI adoption

Deep experience and knowledge of financial services and Wealth Management

Excellent technical project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.

jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

About The Role

Powerfleet is seeking a Senior Director, AI Transformation to help drive the adoption and business impact of AI across the enterprise. This role will work across functions including Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Product, Operations, Customer Success, and Technology to identify, prioritize, and advance high-value AI opportunities.

The Senior Director will serve as a key partner to the AI Transformation leadership, helping establish and execute the enterprise AI transformation roadmap, AI governance, and AI Center of Excellence (CoE). The role will connect business priorities with emerging AI capabilities, helping teams move from ideas and use cases to practical adoption and measurable outcomes.

This is a highly cross-functional, individual contributor role requiring strong business judgment, program leadership, communication, and the ability to influence stakeholders across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise AI Transformation

Partner with business and functional leaders to identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities across Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Product, Operations, Customer Success, and Technology based on business value, feasibility, readiness, risk, and potential impact.
Build and maintain an enterprise portfolio of AI use cases and support the prioritization, sequencing, and execution of initiatives as part of Powerfleet’s broader AI transformation roadmap.

AI Portfolio & Program Leadership

Lead coordination of major cross-functional AI transformation initiatives, establishing clear objectives, milestones, owners, dependencies, and outcomes while helping teams maintain execution momentum.
Establish metrics to track AI adoption, productivity, business impact, and value realization, and support executive reviews of AI initiatives, progress, risks, opportunities, and outcomes.
Help evaluate build-versus-buy opportunities and identify technologies, platforms, and strategic partners that can accelerate AI adoption.

Executive & Stakeholder Engagement

Prepare and present AI transformation strategies, roadmaps, use cases, recommendations, progress, and business outcomes to executive leadership and translate complex AI concepts and emerging technologies into practical business opportunities and facilitate decision-making across business, product, technology, and executive stakeholders. AI Adoption & Change

Help establish an enterprise culture of responsible AI adoption and experimentation through communication, education, and enablement. Identify and scale successful AI use cases, patterns, and best practices across functions and geographies.

Hybrid Work Model

About The Role

As Director, Technology Delivery Lead, you are accountable for the end-to-end technology delivery of Em, BMO InvestorLine's premier AI agent. You will lead the integrated delivery system across AI engineering, wealth platforms, Microsoft Azure, data, architecture, quality engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and third parties to deliver safe, resilient, scalable, and measurable client outcomes.

You will operate as the principal technology counterpart to the Product Owner for Em. Together, you are jointly accountable for overall delivery: the Product Owner leads product vision, client value, priorities, and acceptance; the Technology Delivery Lead owns the integrated technology plan, engineering execution, technical quality, production readiness, and predictable delivery. This role is not a program coordination position. It is a hands-on senior technology leadership role with clear decision rights and accountability for outcomes.

Mandate and Decision Rights

Own the integrated technology delivery plan for Em from discovery and architecture through build, evaluation, release, operation, and continuous improvement.
Jointly commit scope, sequencing, release outcomes, and delivery forecasts with the Product Owner, balancing client value, technical feasibility, risk, cost, and capacity.
Make or escalate timely technology delivery decisions across architecture, engineering, environments, data, integration, testing, controls, and production readiness.
Hold delivery teams and partners accountable for agreed outcomes, quality standards, dependencies, and evidence-based release criteria.
Protect the product from unmanaged technical debt, fragmented ownership, late-stage controls, and delivery practices that are not fit for AI.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technology Delivery
Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.
AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership
Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.
Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration
Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.
Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery
Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.
Quality, Risk and Responsible AI
Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.
Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership
Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

Key Success Measures

Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

Required Skills And Competencies

Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

Qualifications And Experience

jobs.title: Vice President, Data and AI Foundations
jobs.description:
About The Role

The VP, Data and AI Foundations is an enterprise executive leadership role accountable for defining, governing, and executing SE Health's end-to-end data and AI ecosystem. This role owns the strategy, architecture, engineering, analytics, governance, and business integration of data and artificial intelligence assets across the organization.

This position provides executive oversight for enterprise data strategies, advanced analytics, machine learning/Generative AI capabilities, data architecture, information governance, business intelligence, and responsible AI ethics frameworks. The VP partners with senior executives, clinical operations, technology leadership, legal/privacy teams, and external strategic partners to transform raw enterprise data into actionable intelligence, predictive insights, automated workflows, and measurable business and clinical outcomes.

Enterprise Impact and Scope

Sets enterprise direction for data management, business intelligence, predictive/prescriptive analytics, and enterprise AI adoption strategies.
Accountable for establishing data quality, metadata management, data architecture integration, and AI ethical guardrails in alignment with organizational risk posture and regulatory standards.
Provides executive leadership for the design, scaling, and monetization/operationalization of machine learning models, Generative AI applications, and algorithmic automation.
Builds executive alignment, algorithmic trust, and scalable data-driven operating models that empower enterprise clinical, financial, and operational decision-making.

What You'll Do

Enterprise Data & AI Strategy, Investment & Governance

Enterprise Direction: Sets the enterprise vision, strategic priorities, operating model and multi-year roadmap for data and AI, aligned with SE Health’s organizational strategy, care transformation and growth objectives.
Investment Stewardship: Establishes portfolio priorities and provides executive oversight of operating and capital investments, business cases, funding recommendations and benefits realization across the data and AI portfolio.
Enterprise Standards: Establishes and approves enterprise standards for data architecture, quality, stewardship, interoperability, access, platforms and responsible AI, ensuring alignment with security, privacy, legal, clinical and regulatory requirements.
Decision Authority: Chairs or sponsors enterprise governance forums; resolves cross-enterprise priorities and trade-offs; and recommends whether initiatives should proceed, change course or stop based on strategic fit, risk, readiness and expected value.

Business Transformation, AI Adoption & Value Realization

Transformation Portfolio: Partners with executive and business leaders to identify and prioritize enterprise opportunities where data and AI can transform care delivery, client and employee experience, workforce capacity, productivity, quality, growth and financial performance.
Product and Delivery Accountability: Provides executive oversight for the end-to-end portfolio of analytics, automation and AI products, ensuring disciplined progression from discovery and experimentation through deployment, adoption, scaling and ongoing optimization.
Business Adoption: Establishes shared accountability with business owners for workflow redesign, change readiness, adoption and sustained use of data and AI capabilities across clinical and corporate functions.
Benefits Realization: Defines enterprise performance measures and holds the portfolio accountable for measurable clinical, operational, financial and strategic outcomes, including quality, safety, productivity, user adoption and return on investment.

Enterprise Risk, Privacy & Responsible AI

Risk Framework: Establishes the enterprise data and AI risk framework in partnership with Privacy, Legal & Compliance, Security, Clinical, Technology and other control functions, aligned with organizational risk appetite and regulatory obligations.
Responsible AI: Sets guardrails for ethical, transparent, explainable and equitable use of data and AI, including human oversight, bias monitoring, model validation, third-party risk and appropriate use of sensitive health information.
Executive Assurance: Provides executive visibility into material data and AI risks, control effectiveness, regulatory developments and emerging exposures, with clear recommendations and escalation pathways.
Ongoing Oversight: Ensures deployed data and AI products are monitored for safety, accuracy, security, performance, drift and unintended impacts, and initiates timely remediation where required.

Executive Partnership & Ecosystem Leadership

Executive Advisory: Serves as a trusted advisor to the Chief Digital Officer, CEO and senior leadership on enterprise data and AI strategy, investment choices, opportunities, risks and organizational readiness.
Enterprise Alignment: Builds shared ownership across clinical, operational, financial and corporate leaders and resolves competing priorities, dependencies and decision rights across the enterprise.
Commercial and Partner Strategy: Leads strategic vendor and partner relationships, including build-buy-partner decisions, commercial negotiations, performance governance, technology viability, cost optimization and responsible commercialization opportunities where appropriate.
External Leadership: Represents SE Health in relevant health-sector, technology, research and policy forums, strengthening strategic partnerships, sector influence and access to emerging capabilities.

People, Culture & Organizational Capability

Organizational Leadership: Designs and leads a high-performing, multidisciplinary Data & AI function with clear mandates, accountabilities, decision rights and performance expectations aligned to enterprise priorities.
Talent and Succession: Leads workforce planning, talent acquisition, leadership development, performance management and succession planning for critical data and AI capabilities, balancing internal capacity with strategic external expertise.
Enterprise Capability: Builds data literacy, responsible AI fluency and decision-making capability across the organization so leaders and teams can use data and AI confidently, safely and effectively.
Culture and Leadership: Fosters an inclusive, collaborative and accountable culture that encourages innovation, constructive challenge, continuous learning and disciplined execution.

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
MBA or Master's degree in a related discipline considered an asset.(MS/MBA in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, or AI).
Relevant certifications considered an asset (e.g., Azure Data/AI Engineer, AWS Certified Machine Learning, Google Cloud Data Engineer, CIPP privacy certification, CDMP, or equivalent).
15+ years of progressive technology and data leadership experience, including senior executive accountability over enterprise data systems, business intelligence, data science, and enterprise platform delivery.
Demonstrated experience designing, building, and operating modern data stack architectures (Data Warehouses, Lakehouses, MLOps platforms) within complex enterprise environments.
Proven track record of deploying machine learning models, predictive tools, or Generative AI solutions into core production workflows to drive business value.
Demonstrated experience managing financial planning, cloud consumption/compute budgets, investment prioritization, and portfolio governance for data and AI programs.
In-depth knowledge of health data standards, data privacy laws (e.g., PHIPA, PIPEDA), clinical data structures, and ethical AI/governance frameworks.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

About Gambler First Nation

Gambler First Nation (GFN) is an Ojibway First Nation located near Binscarth in southwestern Manitoba, within Treaty 4 territory. The Nation’s primary reserve, Gambler 63, is situated in a rural setting along the Assiniboine Valley, offering a close‑knit community environment rooted in strong cultural traditions and a deep connection to the land. GFN is one of the smaller First Nations in Manitoba, with a total registered membership of approximately 330 members, the majority of whom live off‑reserve. Despite its size, the Nation maintains an active governance structure and delivers a range of programs and services to support the wellbeing of its members, both on‑ and off‑reserve.

The Nation is a member of the West Region Tribal Council and works collaboratively with regional partners and other First Nations to advance shared priorities and access collective services. Gambler First Nation is led by an elected Chief and Council and is focused on responsible governance, community wellbeing, and sustainable administration. As Gambler First Nation continues to strengthen its organizational capacity and financial stewardship, it is committed to transparent, accountable management of its resources in support of current community needs and future generations.

Download the Full Job Description: Gambler First Nation - Director of Finance - Position Profile.pdf

About The Director Of Finance Position

Reporting to the Chief and Council, the Director of Finance plays a critical leadership role in supporting the financial stewardship and long‑term sustainability of Gambler First Nation. This position is responsible for overseeing the Nation’s financial management, reporting, budgeting, and compliance functions while providing trusted advice to Chief and Council on financial strategy and decision‑making.

The Director of Finance ensures that financial practices align with legislative requirements, funding agreements, and sound governance principles, while also supporting operational leaders in managing programs and services effectively. The role balances strong technical financial expertise with a practical, community‑focused approach, recognizing the unique governance, funding, and accountability environment of a First Nation organization.

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director of Finance contributes to organizational planning, risk management, and capacity building, and plays an important role in strengthening financial systems, controls, and reporting processes in support of transparency, accountability, and service to GFN members.

Gambler First Nation’s administrative office is transitioning from Russell, Manitoba, to Brandon, Manitoba, with the move anticipated by late Fall. The Director of Finance may work remotely, with an expectation of working in the Brandon office a minimum of two days per week once the Brandon office is fully operational.

Financial And Operational Accountabilities

Contribute to the development and execution of Gambler First Nation’s strategic and operational plans by providing financial leadership, analysis, and advice that supports community priorities and long‑term sustainability.
Lead the overall finance and accounting functions, including annual budgeting and forecasting, financial planning and analysis, reporting, capital planning, audits, insurance, asset management, cost control, and related financial activities.
Establish annual financial objectives that align with GFN’s strategic priorities, funding agreements, and governance expectations.
Translate strategic and operational plans into effective financial and accounting plans, ensuring alignment between organizational goals and day‑to‑day financial management.
Review historical financial results and emerging trends, and analyze anticipated changes to inform leadership decision‑making and future planning.
Develop and maintain financial models to support long‑term planning, scenario analysis, and risk‑informed decision‑making.
Monitor financial performance against approved budgets, analyze variances, and provide clear, timely reporting to support discussion and informed decisions by senior leadership and Council.
Ensure all financial reporting requirements are met, including those related to funding agreements, financial administration policies, and reporting obligations to government and other funding partners.
Identify financial and organizational risks within a risk‑management framework and design, implement, and maintain appropriate internal controls to mitigate those risks.
Oversee the development of processes to assess and report on the overall financial and operational performance of the organization.
Maintain effective, efficient, and compliant financial systems, processes, and practices in accordance with recognized accounting standards, policies, and procedures.
Lead the year‑end audit process, including coordination with external auditors and oversight of working papers, schedules, analyses, and supporting documentation.
Evaluate the financial performance of the organization in relation to long‑term operational goals, budgets, and forecasts, and provide strategic insights and recommendations.
Provide Chief and Council and senior leadership with accurate, timely historical, current, and projected financial information to support governance and management decisions.
Coordinate the development, review, and ongoing improvement of financial and administrative policies and procedures that support strong governance, accountability, and sound management practices.

Education And Experience Requirements

Gambler First Nation is seeking a highly collaborative Director of Finance who values relationship‑building, teamwork, and shared accountability. This role is central to supporting the Nation’s long‑term financial sustainability and requires the ability to work closely and respectfully with Chief and Council, the Band Manager, program leaders, staff, external partners, and community stakeholders.

The Director of Finance is expected to build, lead, and sustain a high‑performing finance and administration function. Chief and Council and the organization will rely on the individual in this role for sound professional judgment, strategic financial advice, and technical expertise that supports effective governance and informed decision‑making.

The ideal candidate brings experience working in First Nations or Indigenous organizational environments and understands the governance, funding, and accountability context in which First Nation governments operate.

Education

A post‑secondary degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field, combined with significant progressive experience in finance, accounting, and auditing, including senior‑level leadership of a finance function. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
A professional accounting designation, such as Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) or Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM), is considered a strong asset.
Required experience in First Nations or Indigenous finance, including work within a First Nation government, Indigenous organization, tribal council, or Indigenous advisory or accounting services environment.

Experience

Demonstrated expertise in strategic financial stewardship, including budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, business planning, asset management, cost controls, and the application of generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
Proven experience in financial modelling, financial analysis, cash‑flow management, and the monitoring and management of investments.
Strong working knowledge of federal and provincial legislation, public policy, and funding frameworks applicable to First Nation governments and entities.
Proficiency with financial systems and tools or financial and reporting applications.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex financial data and prepare clear, accurate financial reports, statements, and long‑term projections for a variety of audiences.
A highly collaborative leadership style, with the ability to work effectively across functions and build strong, respectful working relationships throughout the organization.
Demonstrated ability to clearly communicate financial information and concepts to leadership, Council, and staff who may not have financial expertise.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including presentation and negotiation skills appropriate to executive and governance‑level settings.

jobs.title: Director Finance, Fabrication Operations
jobs.description:
Experience Without Limits

Come shape the future of brand experience.

At Jack Morton, we design and build
head-turning, smile-inducing, impact-driving brand experiences that redefine what experiential marketing can achieve. We help our clients unlock the full value of experiences
by turning bold ideas into meaningful connections.

That takes a team that's bold, curious, and acts as one.
We build on each other's ideas, challenge conventions, and show up for one another every day. Here, you'll do your best work, grow quickly, and partner across clients, disciplines, and global teams to bring new ideas to life.

This is a place where curiosity drives what’s next, boldness raises the bar, and every win is shared. Where ownership is expected, egos are left at the door, and the work reflects the passion and talent of the people behind it.

Experience without limits—in your work, your growth, and your impact.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a commercially minded and operationally focused Finance Director, Fabrication Operations
to serve as the finance lead and strategic business partner for our North American fabrication network.

Partnering directly with the Head of Fabrication, you will help build the financial and operational foundation for a growing multi-site production organization. This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and operations, can connect financial performance to what is happening on the production floor, and enjoys transforming data into actionable business decisions.

You will play a critical role in improving profitability, building reporting and forecasting capabilities, optimizing capacity utilization, and supporting the integration and standardization of fabrication operations across the network.

What You'll Do

Financial Performance & Cost Management

Build and maintain consistent individual and consolidated P&Ls across four fabrication facilities, along with separate P&Ls for storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Conduct a comprehensive assessment of facility cost structures, labor models, capacity utilization, and current reporting practices.
Develop budgeting, forecasting, and scenario-planning models covering labor, overtime, freelance resources, subcontracting, storage, fleet, and facility expenses.
Establish project profitability reviews to compare estimated versus actual margins and create feedback loops that improve future estimating and pricing decisions.
Analyze labor productivity, utilization, overhead absorption, and operational drivers of profitability.
Partner with operational leaders to identify opportunities to improve margins, reduce waste, optimize labor deployment, and increase financial discipline.
Lead monthly performance reviews with fabrication leadership teams.

Capacity Planning & Network Optimization

Map capacity against demand across the fabrication network and develop reporting that supports more effective planning and resource allocation.
Improve pipeline visibility to provide a reliable view of future fabrication demand and workload requirements.
Separate fabrication, non-fabrication, and insourced work streams to support accurate capacity planning and decision-making.
Support long-term network planning, including facility footprint decisions, capability investments, and capital expenditure evaluations.
Build financial models that support insource versus outsource decisions, staffing strategies, overtime management, and facility investments.
Support vendor consolidation initiatives, rebate tracking, and procurement savings opportunities.

Reporting, KPIs & Integration

Develop and implement a standardized KPI framework across all fabrication locations, including utilization, throughput, overtime, on-time delivery, rework, and profitability metrics.
Launch and maintain executive dashboards covering network performance, financial performance, pipeline, capacity utilization, storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Establish standardized reporting and performance management processes across all locations.
Support the integration of Jack Morton and Impact XM fabrication operations through common definitions, metrics, and processes for job costing, work orders, change orders, and markup structures.
Support D365 adoption and help reduce reliance on manual processes and offline workarounds.
Partner across Fabrication, Finance, Commercial, Estimating, Creative, Account, and Project Management teams to improve planning, visibility, profitability, and operational execution.

What We're Looking For

8-12+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing, fabrication, production, logistics, or other operational environments.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, job costing, labor utilization, overhead allocation, margin analysis, and operational performance management.
Experience supporting multiple facilities, locations, or operating units.
Demonstrated ability to build financial models, forecasting processes, dashboards, and KPI frameworks from the ground up.
Experience driving finance process improvements, operational standardization, and systems adoption within growing or transforming organizations.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable operational recommendations.
Experience evaluating capital investments and developing ROI-based business cases.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence leaders across functions.
Comfortable working in fast-paced, project-based environments where priorities can shift quickly.
Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills; experience with ERP systems and business intelligence tools preferred.
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. CPA, CMA, or MBA is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first six months, you will have:

Assessed the financial and operational performance of all fabrication facilities and support operations.
Established consistent facility, storage, rental, and fleet P&Ls.
Implemented a standardized KPI and reporting framework across the network.
Launched fabrication performance dashboards that provide clear visibility into profitability, utilization, capacity, and demand.
Built forecasting and scenario-planning tools that support operational decision-making.
Established a regular performance review cadence with facility leaders.
Improved visibility into project profitability and manufacturing economics.
Helped advance the integration and standardization of production operations across Jack Morton.

Success in this role means creating financial visibility where it does not exist today, improving profitability and operational performance, establishing disciplined forecasting and reporting processes, and helping build a scalable fabrication organization capable of supporting future growth.

jobs.description:
Who are we?

Crozier is a leading consulting engineering firm serving the land development industry. Crozier's multidisciplinary team offers expertise in land development, transportation engineering, water resources, construction services, structural engineering, and related infrastructure disciplines. With offices in Toronto, Collingwood, Burlington, Bradford, and Guelph, Crozier supports private-sector clients across Ontario in advancing residential, commercial, and industrial developments, as well as projects across other key industry markets. Crozier has been awarded esteemed top employer, leadership and business growth recognitions, including one of Canada's Top Small & Medium Employers, Southwestern Ontario's Top Employers, and ranked among Canada's Top Growing Companies by Report on Business.

Your Impact:

Crozier is currently seeking a Director of Finance
to join our growing company.
Reporting to the President, the Director of Finance will serve as Crozier’s lead finance executive and be responsible for oversight of all finance, accounting, treasury, and reporting activities. As a strong communicator, you will make it your mission to streamline our budgeting, payroll, and financial reporting processes. You will produce thorough financial-status reports for senior management, to help improve our operational efficiency and aid in our continued growth.

How you will contribute to the team:

In conjunction with the Manager of Finance, oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems ensuring compliance with IFRS and regulatory requirements.
Maintain internal control and safeguards for receipt of revenue, costs, program budgets, and actual expenditures.
In conjunction with the President and senior leadership team, establish financial and operating benchmarks, budgets, program monitoring, and reporting standards on a bi-weekly, monthly, and annual basis.
Achieve budget goals with proper analysis, and corrective action.
Help develop and support short and long-term operational strategies.
Act as a key member of the executive team, providing strategic financial counsel to the President and the Board on investments, growth initiatives, and risk management.
Consistently analyze financial data and present financial reports in an accurate and timely manner; clearly communicate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements; monitor progress and changes.
Develop and enforce internal controls to maximize protection of company assets, policies, procedures, and workflow.
Oversee and support accounting team with dynamic leadership that creates an environment of trust and productivity.

What you bring:

Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, or related field; CPA designation required.
15+ years of proven accounting experience, with 10+ years of experience in a senior finance leadership position.
Strong knowledge of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); knowledge of US GAAP is an asset.
Extremely knowledgeable in financial forecasting, accounting principles, and financial data analysis.
Strong understanding of economic and banking processes.
Keen analytic, organization and problem-solving skills which allows for strategic data interpretation versus simple reporting.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills; experience in effectively communicating key data, including presentations to senior management, board, or other outside partners.
Ability and desire to translate complex financial concepts to individuals at all levels including finance and non-finance managers.

Crozier offers RRSP matching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), parental leave top-up, annual wellness allowance, our unique First-Time Home Buyers' Assistance Program, and more.

Investing in Your Growth
: Your development matters to us. It is our goal to provide programs that support our employee’s experience through personal and professional development. We offer paid professional development support and training, including a Lifelong Learning Assistance Program to support career pathways.

Making a Difference Together
: Giving back is part of who we are. We actively support not-for-profit organizations in the communities where we live and work, and encourage employees to get involved through community initiatives and local events.

Crozier Social
: At Crozier, we believe strong relationships make great teams. From sports leagues and game nights to creative workshops and social events, there are plenty of opportunities to connect with colleagues. Throughout the year, we bring our teams together through activities such as golf tournaments, hikes, boat cruises, and other fun company-wide events.

$130,000 - $170,000

When we make an offer, we consider the responsibilities of the position, market data, and internal equity to ensure consistency across our teams. Your actual offer will depend on your experience, skills, and alignment with the role.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

The Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis leads the Bank’s enterprise financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and management reporting activities and oversees the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence within the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis portfolio. The role establishes an integrated view of financial performance, outlook, risks, and opportunities to support executive decision-making and disciplined resource and capital allocation.

The role partners with business and functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into financial plans, challenge assumptions, assess performance drivers, and provide timely, decision-useful insight. It is accountable for the quality, consistency, governance, and continuous improvement of planning and forecasting processes and for establishing a high-performing Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence that scales common standards, tools, models, data, and insight across the Bank.

Financial Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budget, periodic forecast, and multi-year financial planning processes, integrating business plans, economic assumptions, balance sheet and income statement drivers, and enterprise priorities.
Establish planning calendars, standards, controls, accountabilities, and review forums that support complete, accurate, timely, and comparable submissions across the Bank.
Provide an integrated view of actual and forecast performance, including revenue, net interest margin, expenses, profitability, return on equity, capital implications, and key non-financial drivers.
Lead scenario and sensitivity analysis to assess the financial implications of changing market conditions, strategic choices, investments, and emerging risks.
Identify material variances, trends, and forecast risks; ensure clear ownership of actions and provide concise recommendations to senior leadership.

Capital Forecasting, Strategic Capital Allocation, ICAAP & Stress Testing

Lead enterprise capital forecasting and provide a forward-looking view of regulatory capital, leverage, capital generation, and deployment under the strategic and financial plan.
Assess capital capacity, requirements, and trade-offs to support the allocation of capital to strategic investments, business growth, acquisitions, and other enterprise priorities.
Partner with Treasury, Risk Management, business leaders, and other Finance teams to align capital forecasts with earnings, balance sheet growth, risk-weighted assets, funding plans, internal capital targets, and management buffers.
Lead the consolidation of financial forecasts and capital impacts for the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process, enterprise-wide stress testing, regulatory stress testing, and related scenario analysis.
Evaluate adverse but plausible scenarios, key sensitivities, and management actions; identify potential capital constraints or vulnerabilities and recommend actions to protect resilience and support strategic objectives.
Establish robust governance, controls, documentation, and executive reporting for capital assumptions, methodologies, forecasts, stress-testing outputs, and capital-allocation decisions.

Executive & Strategic Financial Storytelling

Lead the development and presentation of clear, Board-ready financial narratives that explain enterprise performance, outlook, key drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Translate complex financial, operational, and strategic analysis into concise, decision-oriented messages tailored to the Board, executive leadership, and management governance forums.
Provide strategic oversight of consolidated financial results and outlook, ensuring consistency across the income statement, balance sheet, capital, business segments, and key performance indicators.
Connect actual and forecast performance to the Bank’s strategy, external environment, and value-creation priorities, highlighting the implications of trends, trade-offs, and emerging issues.
Establish executive communication standards that are punchline-first, analytically sound, and supported by clear evidence, sensitivities, and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate across Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Investor Relations, Risk Management, and business finance partners to maintain a consistent enterprise financial story across Board, executive, regulatory, and external materials.

Management Reporting, Data & Insight

Oversee recurring management reporting and dashboards, ensuring that measures, definitions, commentary, and source data are consistent and decision-useful.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial drivers that connect strategic objectives, operating activity, and financial outcomes.
Strengthen data quality, model governance, documentation, controls, and review practices for material planning and management reporting outputs.
Drive automation and simplification of planning, forecasting, modelling, and reporting processes to improve speed, accuracy, transparency, and analytical capacity.
Partner with Data and Technology stakeholders on requirements, prioritization, testing, implementation, and adoption of financial planning and analytics capabilities.

Leadership, Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish and oversee the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence, including its mandate, governance, operating model, service catalogue, priorities, measures, and capability roadmap.
Develop common planning, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and business-partnering standards, and support adoption across Financial Planning & Analysis and partner teams.
Build reusable tools, templates, driver libraries, scenario models, data definitions, and analytical practices that improve consistency, speed, and decision usefulness.
Create a community of practice that strengthens capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, quality review, and continuous learning.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of finance professionals; establish clear accountability, effective succession and development practices, and high standards for analysis and communication.
Maintain an effective control environment for planning, forecasting, modelling, and management reporting, and address issues identified through review, audit, or control testing.

Lets Talk About You!

University degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
CPA or CFA designation or an equivalent recognized finance designation.
At least 12 years of progressive finance experience, including substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, management reporting, financial modelling, and executive decision support.
Senior leadership and people-management experience, including experience setting functional priorities, reviewing complex work, coaching leaders and professionals, and delivering through others.
Advanced knowledge of financial statements, performance drivers, budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, profitability, return on equity, and capital-aware decision-making within financial services.
Experience producing and presenting concise analysis for executives and governance forums, with the judgment to distinguish material issues, challenge assumptions, and recommend action.
Advanced spreadsheet and presentation skills and experience with enterprise planning, reporting, business intelligence, and financial data tools. Specific systems: To be confirmed.
Strong written and verbal communication, stakeholder-management, analytical, problem-solving, organization, and change-leadership skills.
Experience in a Canadian bank or other regulated financial institution, including knowledge of banking products, net interest margin, balance sheet drivers, capital, and regulatory considerations.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

The incumbent will be working hybrid and in office time will be spent working from EQ Bank’s additional office space located at 2200-25 Ontario Street, Toronto, ON
.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. We believe our organization is stronger — and our people thrive — when we honour and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives. We’re equally committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally.

As part of our recruitment process, EQ uses AI to help screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position. All AI-enabled outputs are reviewed and validated by our talent team. All candidates considered for hire must successfully complete a criminal background check and credit check. While we appreciate every application, an EQ recruiter will contact only those whose skills and experience most closely match the requirements of the role.
