About Us

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities. For more information, please visit: https://www.alberta.ca/about-the-alberta-public-service .

The Alberta Public Service (APS) is taking a One Finance approach to financial services delivery. This includes how finance delivers and supports strategic decision-making in order to support effective and informed policy and program decisions. Finance professionals play a key role in shaping decisions, solving complex business challenges, and helping government deliver results for Albertans.

Alberta Transportation and Economic Corridors (TEC) serves as a North American leader in transportation systems, contributing to Alberta’s prosperity through safe, innovative, and sustainable infrastructure. TEC offers a rewarding environment with growth opportunities, work-life balance, and the chance to make an impact on Alberta’s transportation network.

For more information, visit https://www.alberta.ca/transportation-and-economic-corridors

This competition may be used to fill the current and future vacancies across government.

Role

The Executive Director, Financial Services will report to the Assistant Deputy Minister/Senior Financial Officer in Transportation and Economic Corridors and will provide strategic leadership and direction to support the Alberta Public Service “One Finance” approach. In this role, you will build strong relationships with ministry business partners, senior ministry representatives, other ministries, and other jurisdictions. You will work collaboratively with other Executive Directors within the finance community and lead a team of management and professional staff.

As the Executive Director, Financial Services, you will lead the day-to-day planning and implementation of all ministry- specific fiscal management activities including budgeting, planning, reporting, accounting, governance, compliance, and internal controls. You will work proactively with the division leaders and program areas to provide strong financial advice and solutions based on technical knowledge, sound data, and effective analysis to support the government’s financial strategy and ministry mandate. Your implementation and innovative processes will enable you to deliver a suite of financial services within Transportation and Economic Corridors.

Qualifications

Your background will include significant related senior financial management experience in planning, reporting and control functions in a large, complex organization. Your solid financial acumen will enable you to leverage effective financial analysis. You have significant experience managing complex budget issues and providing advice to executive leadership. You have demonstrated capacity to influence critical decisions. You have distinguished yourself as a strategic leader with a reputation for empowering, mentoring, and developing capacity within your teams. Your proven leadership to inspire teams to achieve success is essential. Exceptional collaboration skills and a systems approach are essential for delivering results on ministry priorities. Communication and change management skills as well as the ability to develop and maintain effective stakeholder relationships will be key in balancing varying perspectives in a highly complex and changing business environment.

Post-secondary education in a related field is required. A recognized accounting designation is an asset.

jobs.description:
About Toronto Metropolitan

For more than 75 years, Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly known as Ryerson University) has been shaping the next generation of leaders through its uniquely innovative, entrepreneurial and career-focused approach to higher education. Driven by bold leadership, cutting-edge research and a deep commitment to academic excellence, TMU collaborates with students, faculties, staff and partners to push boundaries, reimagine solutions and create meaningful change in an increasingly interconnected world.

For a more in-depth understanding of our vision, core values and ongoing work, please see our academic plan

TMU welcomes those who have demonstrated a commitment to upholding the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion and will assist us in realizing the benefits of embedding these values into the work at every level and in every unit of the university. In addition, to correct the conditions of disadvantage in employment in Canada and to bring lived experiences to the work, we encourage applications from members of equity deserving groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples in Canada, First Nations Peoples in the United States, racialized people, Black people, persons with disabilities, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ people. Preference will be given to candidates with lived experiences as people from equity deserving groups, as well as experience working with these communities with which the University works every day. Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and we welcome newcomers and immigrants to Canada.

In April 2022, the university announced its new name of Toronto Metropolitan University. Learn more about our next chapter.

About The School Of Medicine

It’s time to transform medical education. Toronto Metropolitan University’s School of Medicine has been designed from the ground up to shift the paradigm of healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of individuals, families and communities. With a community-driven, intentionally inclusive approach, the new school is training doctors whose cultural awareness and humility are as crucial as their medical skills.

Led by Dr. Teresa M. Chan, a forward-thinking educational leader, TMU’s School of Medicine draws on the university’s commitment to community, equity, and innovation to address rapidly changing healthcare needs. The school will train a new generation of physicians who are ready to learn, to adapt, and ultimately to be agents of change.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Finance Director to join the School of Medicine! This newly created role leads the development and implementation of school-wide financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and resource management strategies that advance the academic, research, and operational priorities of the School of Medicine.

Serving as a trusted strategic advisor, the position provides expert financial counsel to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Dean, and senior leadership by assessing long-term financial implications, recommending evidence-based solutions, and ensuring alignment with broader University policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

This role oversees the financial operations of the School of Medicine, supporting budgeting, reporting, financial compliance, and informed decision-making. he Director also provides financial and advisory support to the Integrated Health Centre, including support for external financial reporting and audit requirements,, in close collaboration with TMU Financial Services and the University Planning Office.

In addition, the Director conducts financial research and analysis to inform policy development and long-term planning, and represents the CAO and the School of Medicine in TMU-wide planning discussions and committees.

Responsibilities Include

Financial planning, budgeting and management

Provides financial advice, analysis, and decision-support to departments within the School of Medicine to support budget development, financial planning, forecasting, and effective resource management.
Manages day-to-day financial activities for the School of Medicine, including monitoring and reconciling operating and payroll expenditures, and ensures that actual financial results reconcile with approved targets
Collaborates with the University Planning Office (UPO) to support the annual budget development process for the SoM.

Payroll Administration and Financial Oversight (SoM Residents and IHC Employees)

Oversees, reviews, and approves biweekly payroll registers before the third-party vendor releases payments and monthly reconciliations. Investigate unusual variances, adjustments, and exceptions.
Monitors payroll funding requirements, forecast upcoming payroll obligations, and ensure sufficient funds are available in the designated bank account before each payroll withdrawal
Oversee the processes, systems, and internal controls supporting the administration of payroll, benefits, and expense claims for medical learners (residents) and Integrated Health Centre (IHC) staff.
Provide leadership and oversight to staff responsible for processing payroll, benefits, and expenses, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable policies and requirements.
Establish and maintain effective procedures, workflows, and controls to support reliable and efficient administration of these functions.

Strategy and external collaboration

Conducts financial research and analysis to support the Dean and CAO in the development of a funding model for the School of Medicine and the Integrated Health Centres (IHC).
Monitors SOM activities relevant to external funding and reporting obligations, and ensures timely information sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Develops and implements a strategic roadmap for School-wide financial forecasting, planning, and internal financial controls, including long-term budget plan for the SoM that supports the academic, research, and operational priorities.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Venor is proud to partner with Commissionaires Nova Scotia in the recruitment of a Chief Financial Officer.

Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Commissionaires Nova Scotia (CNS) is the province’s leading not-for-profit security provider, delivering guarding, monitoring, investigative, and specialized security services to more than 200 sites across the province. With roughly 1,300 employees, a large share of them veterans of the Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP, CNS is the largest private-sector employer of veterans in Nova Scotia. As part of the national Commissionaires federation of over 22,000 security professionals across Canada, CNS reinvests more than 90% of its annual revenue directly into employee wages, training, and benefits.

On their behalf, we are seeking a strategic and hands-on Chief Financial Officer to join the executive team. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead the organization’s financial strategy, reporting, planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, capital allocation, risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Team, and Board of Governors, you’ll bring financial insight to strategic decision-making while leading a team of finance, IT, and procurement professionals and ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll lead the organization’s financial strategy and provide executive-level financial advice across all business lines. You’ll develop, implement, and maintain financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks, and oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, controllership, treasury management, and audit activities. You’ll also manage the enterprise financial systems and reporting platforms that keep the organization’s financial information timely and accurate, preparing and presenting financial reports to the CEO, Executive Team, Finance and Audit Committee, and Board of Governors, and developing the annual operating and capital budgets, including required submissions to Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).

You’ll provide strategic pricing guidance, including contract billing and labour rates, and ensure compliance with financial, regulatory, tax, and not-for-profit reporting requirements, including CRA obligations. Externally, you’ll manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, insurers, the national Commissionaires federation, and government partners, and contribute to organizational strategy through financial analysis, business cases, and recommendations that support sustainable growth. Internally, you’ll provide executive oversight of payroll, compensation, benefits, and related financial administration, and lead, mentor, and develop a finance team spanning budgeting, payroll and accounts, IT/cyber, and procurement.

What You’ll Bring

You bring a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and executive experience), along with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing. You have 10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and governance within a complex organization, and a track record of advising executive teams, Boards of Directors or Governors, and senior stakeholders. Your knowledge of financial management, accounting standards, regulatory compliance, risk management, and corporate governance is strong, and you’ve demonstrated the ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable financial plans and business cases. You’ve led and developed high-performing finance teams, and you communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, collaborative leader with strong business acumen and a genuine commitment to integrity, innovation, and service excellence. You’re as comfortable in the details of financial reporting as you are advising the boardroom, and you bring the judgment to manage competing priorities during budgeting, audit, and Board reporting cycles.

jobs.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Kraken Customer

What we do: build the most AI-driven, innovative, forward-thinking platform for energy management. From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry.

Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now.

Why it matters: There are singular moments in every industry where a tectonic shift reshapes the entire sector and unlocks previously unheard of possibilities. There are few industries remaining that are ripe for disruption. Those moments need leaders and the energy sector is in that moment. The disruption is happening now.

Our Kraken software and operating model enable our energy clients to lead this shift while enhancing their operational effectiveness. The accelerated adoption of Kraken means we need someone to lead a major North America client implementation to deliver world-changing results. Are you that leader?

The Company

Kraken launched to market five years ago, offering energy utilities one simple end-to-end customer management and local flexibility optimization solution to help them and their customers transition to a decarbonized future. The Kraken platform is effectively the operating system for utilities, at the core of how they run their business.

Kraken is growing rapidly, disrupting the incumbent tech landscape, with over 64 million end-customer accounts contracted across 11 markets globally and managing the optimisation of over 65GW. Kraken has secured licensing deals with large international energy clients to replace their core technology stack and re-image their operations with an unblemished track record of transformation success.

We are tracking toward 100 million customer accounts on the platform by 2027.

At the end of 2025 Kraken was independently valued at $8.65 billion, and received $1 billion in investment.

🏠 Where You'll Fit In

The individual in this role will serve as both the face of, and the delivery leader for the next North American utility transformation. This is a high profile role with a dedicated internal team of experienced Client Delivery Leaders, a dedicated Client Engineering team, as well as the attention of our 1000+ person Product and Engineering organization. Our ideal candidate will be comfortable briefing the CEO of a billion+ dollar utility, while also able to maintain a detailed understanding of the complicated dependencies across multiple work streams so as to successfully coach, guide, and support our talented delivery leaders throughout the transformation.

Be accountable for the successful execution of client implementation programs using our Build-Operate-Transfer methodology, which covers technology, business operations and culture transformation
Find solutions that bring our clients into the new software and operating model that both accelerates delivery and reduces risk
Develop deep trust with our C-suite client executives
Lead a team of Client Delivery Leads across functional delivery areas
Prioritise outcomes and delivery from a team of Client Engineers directly supporting this transformation, while collaborating with our VP of product for Vertically Integrated Utilities to ensure the entire 1000+ person development team at Kraken is delivering the capabilities required to exceed our client’s expectations
Communicate effectively to stakeholders at all levels, both internally and externally
Continuously demonstrate Kraken’s business value to the client and build a governance model which can last once the implementation program is completed
Set the direction and pace for implementation program execution. Managing internal and external expectations, removing blockers and making prioritisation decisions to enable successful client transformations
Understand the implementation program details and report progress to the client and internal stakeholders
Embody the Kraken ways of working. Provide support and feedback to members of the Kraken team and reinforce an environment of psychological safety.

🧠 What You'll Bring To The Party

Extensive experience in Regulated Utilities (ideally in the North American market)
Strong experience leading large, enterprise-level technology implementations and the significant transformation of business operations , ideally in utilities or similar industries (e.g. telecom, public sector)
Proven experience with C-suite clients, leading strategic conversations, negotiating win-wins, and advising on business transformation
Hands-on leader of global implementation teams consisting of experts representing implementation, product, data, engineering, change management, and enablement
Problem solver with an ability to focus conversations on the things that truly matter
Ability to understand what success looks like for the client and laser-focused on how to enable them to achieve that without always saying yes
Team player who can work effectively with national and global teams across Kraken
Excellent communication and facilitation skills. You are well respected with a natural gravitas
Client and quality focus; highly effective at building and improving customer relationships as peers
Mobile - You will be expected to invest in face-to-face relationship building with our clients and internal teams. Frequent travel will be expected.

Soft Skills

Kraken is at the forefront of innovation in the energy industry and we succeed in large part thanks to our people. To fit well at Kraken, you’ll also be:
Passionate about helping clients (without them, we don’t exist)
Passionate about technology (we are a tech business disrupting energy)
Committed to sustainability (we are all about speeding up the shift to a more sustainable world)
Open-minded, flexible and adaptable (we are constantly growing, changing and evolving)
Confident in decision-making
Supportive
Approachable and fun to work with
Inclusive
Resilient, working well under pressure
Believe in big ambitions and small egos
Embrace the servant leadership philosophy

Why You'll Love It Here

Opt in medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
Paid time off — we know working hard means also being able to recharge as needed, we trust our employees to get the work done and take the time they need.

Why this role is different and why to apply

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

jobs.title: Director, Data Governance
jobs.description:
Nutrien is a leading provider of crop inputs and services, and our business results make a positive impact on the world. Our purpose, Feeding the Future , is the reason we come to work each day. We’re guided by our culture of care and our core values: We put safety first. We act with integrity. We are stronger together. We deliver with excellence.

Through the collective expertise of our nearly 26,000 employees, we operate a world-class network of production, distribution, and ag retail facilities. We efficiently serve growers' needs and strive to provide a more profitable, sustainable, and secure future for all stakeholders.  Help us raise the expectation of what an agriculture company can be and grow your career with Nutrien.

Nutrien is looking for a Director, Data Governance to build and lead our enterprise data governance program—strengthening data ownership, quality, and controls across key data domains so Nutrien can confidently scale analytics, AI, and digital products. Reporting to the Sr Director, Data Office, you will partner across business, technology, and risk functions to set standards, enable adoption, and ensure regulatory, and policy requirements are met globally.

This role will ensure critical data at Nutrien is trusted, consistent, and compliant across all data domains and business areas. You will operate at the intersection of business, data, technology, and risk—enabling scalable analytics, AI, and digital products globally—while ensuring regulatory and policy requirements are met and maintained.

What You'll Do

Support the design and implementation of Nutrien’s global data governance framework across core data domains (e.g., product, customer, supplier, location, and asset)
Define enterprise standards for master/reference data domains and critical data elements
Drive the implementation of governance ownership and accountability across all data domains and lines of business, partnering with domain leaders to clarify roles, responsibilities, and adoption of governance practices
Balance enterprise consistency with business needs, regulatory requirements, and regional/functional nuances
Facilitate and support enterprise and business unit data governance forums (e.g., councils and working groups) ensuring alignment, issue escalation, and effective decision making
Drive continuous improvement of governance practices as the data and AI landscape evolves
Partner with IT and to define the enterprise data quality strategy, including standards, issue management, root-cause analysis, observability and remediation
Operationalize data governance policies and standards to ensure alignment with global and regional regulatory requirements (e.g., data privacy, residency, and confidentiality), working closely with Legal, Risk, and IT partners
Lead a team delivering master data maintenance for multiple data domains at Nutrien
Partner with Legal, Risk, and Compliance to support audits, client due diligence, and regulatory inquiries related to data and analytics
Lead data governance initiatives and change adoption efforts, influencing stakeholders and enabling consistent governance practices across domains and functions

What You'll Bring

Bachelors Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
15+ years of experience in data governance, data management, master data, or related enterprise data roles
5+ years of experience in a managerial role with demonstrated executive-level influence and stakeholder management, including leading governance councils and driving adoption across a matrixed organization
Proven experience building and launching a data governance program from the ground up
Experience operating in a global, matrixed organization with regional regulatory complexity
Deep knowledge of data governance concepts, frameworks, and best practices (e.g., DAMA-DMBOK)
Practical experience with ERP systems (specifically SAP), data hierarchies, and how master data is created and managed within large enterprises
Experience collaborating across multiple business areas and centralized functions within a large enterprise
Proven people leadership experience, with the ability to build, mentor, and scale a high-performing team and stewardship community

What You'll Get

Purpose-Driven Work – Make an impact as part of a global team feeding the future and support farmers locally and around the world
Excellent Benefits – Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage, plus a retirement program with generous employer matching for your future
Grow Your Career – Tuition assistance for future education and ongoing learning and training opportunities for career advancement pathways across the organization
Support When it Matters – Employee Assistance Programs, inclusive leaves, and paid time for holidays, volunteering, vacation, and wellness
Thrive in a Strong Culture – Guided by our core values we put safety first, act with integrity, are stronger together, and deliver with excellence in a collaborative, high-performing environment

Ready to make an impact with us? Apply today!  

The estimated salary that Indeed, Glassdoor and LinkedIn lists does not represent Nutrien's compensation structure. Nutrien is an equal opportunity employer.  We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.  

This job will remain posted until filled. In accordance with Nutrien policies, you will be required to undergo a background check, and may be required to undergo a substance test. While we appreciate all applications we receive, only candidates under consideration will be contacted. Applicants must meet minimum age requirements, as permitted by law. 

Our Recruitment Process: Application > Resume Review > Pre-screen/Interview > Offer > Pre-Employment Conditions > Welcome to Nutrien

LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As part of the Chief Data Office, collaborating closely with Chief Financial Office and Group Risk Management teams, the Associate Director is the first line of defense for data management risk and is responsible for building and maintaining a comprehensive inventory of data management practice components for Finance and Risk domains.

The ideal candidate will provide expertise and support to senior management in identification, documentation and maintenance of data risk management requirements, enhancing their ability to anticipate and manage data management risks effectively.

What will you do?

Act as a centre of excellence and advocate for data management best practices for Finance and Risk domains
Contribute to and support communication of data strategies, standards and initiatives to Finance and Risk partners
Facilitate building and maintaining a comprehensive inventory of data management practice components for each Finance and Risk domains
Document and analyze data management risk challenges against domain strategy
Prioritize business needs in managing data risks to support funding and business case development
Prepare and present data management risk analysis to stakeholders in Finance, Risk, CLAO, T&O, etc., in collaboration with Director and Senior Director
Guide CFO and GRM stakeholders in building execution plans and roadmaps for data risk management enablement for each Finance and Risk domains, e.g., addressing gaps, supporting 2LOD reviews, planning and achieving domain deliverables, etc.
Partner with CDO shared services to solidify options and provide quality/ timely execution services to Finance and Risk domains
Identify and prioritize data management service needs across Finance and Risk domains to facilitate the prioritization and provision by shared service provider(s)

What do you need to succeed?

Must Have:

5+ years’ experience in risk / data management
Exceptional stakeholder management skills to influence successful outcomes
Experience in Finance or Risk with understanding of key processes and data
Skills in data strategy, data management/ governance, and initiative risk assessment

Nice-to-Have:

Data analytics and reporting skills
Effective time management, multi-tasking and organizational skills to meet tight timelines as well as flexibility to adapt to changing priorities
Experience with regulators, regulatory examinations, and program execution

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team

Opportunities to do challenging work
Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities

Big Data Management, Communication, Critical Thinking, Data Administration, Data Governance, Data Movement, Data Warehousing (DW), Facilitation, Information Capture, Knowledge Organization, Long Term Planning, Organizing, Planning, Prioritization, Repository Tools, Risk Analysis, Teamwork, Time Management

Are You Ready to Build a Platform Company?

EDL Building Solutions is a strong, growing building services company today. A Fixer.
You do not accept broken processes, recurring inefficiencies, or unexplained results as part of doing business. You find root causes, challenge existing practices, and own the improvement.
A Thinker.
You are analytical, commercially minded, and naturally curious. You look past the financial statements to understand what is really happening in the business, and you turn that understanding into practical recommendations.
A Doer.
You move between strategy and execution without losing either. You can lead a financial strategy discussion in the morning and work directly with your team to solve an operational issue in the afternoon.

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

Role Expectations

This is an E3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level own company-wide outcomes, set the strategy for their function, and operate with broad autonomy in partnership with the CEO, the executive team, and the Board.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Act as a full strategic partner to the CEO and the Board, not only as a steward of the numbers.
Build and develop a finance organization that scales ahead of the business, hiring and coaching leaders who raise the bar.
Bring financial discipline to company-wide decisions on pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Own the accuracy and credibility of forecasting, reporting, and board materials.
Prepare the company for its next financing or strategic event well before it is needed.

What success looks like:

Forecasting and planning the executive team and Board trust and act on.
The systems, controls, and team in place to operate credibly at $200M+ in revenue.
Solink positioned and diligence-ready for its next strategic chapter.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, with prior scale-up CFO experience.
Proven track record scaling SaaS or technology companies from ~$50M to $200M+ revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep FP&A expertise with strong analytical and strategic planning capabilities.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising (Series C/D/E) or public markets experience.
Strong command of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue models.
Knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, compliance frameworks, and audit oversight.
Inspirational leader with the ability to develop high-performing finance teams.

Nice-to-Have:

M&A experience across due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration.
Experience in a Canadian company with US and international operations, including multi-currency and cross-border tax considerations.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian or American Citizen, or eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: A stellar benefits package, ensuring you're fully supported with anything you need.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Data Management, Computer Science, or a related discipline; Master is an asset.
8+ years of progressive experience across data governance, risk management, or audit, including at least 2 years leading people, and demonstrable end-to-end delivery of a control or governance environment.
Working knowledge of ICFR, SOC 1 / ISAE 3402, COSO 2013, ITGCs, and DAMA-DMBOK; CPA, CIA, CISA, or CDMP an asset. Familiarity with DCAM / CDMC and data contracts an asset.
Hands-on experience with data cataloguing and governance tooling (Microsoft Purview equivalents such as Collibra an asset) and with controls testing in an ICFR or SOX environment.
Working knowledge of a modern data-platform stack (Microsoft Fabric / lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Entra ID), enough to specify and validate controls.
Working knowledge of Yardi strongly preferred.
Investment and portfolio management literacy or business acumen
Proven ability to build controls that produce retained, re-testable evidence.
Ability to work across Finance, IT, and Data & Analytics, and turn technical and operational complexity into clear governance and control frameworks.
Comfortable preparing materials for senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
Comfortable building or growing an early-stage function.
Experience within real estate, asset management, pension, or investment management environments strongly preferred.

This is a newly created role within our organization.

The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $155,000 – $175,000.

Based on the position, QuadReal offers a competitive total rewards package in addition to the base pay, which may include a performance-based incentive plan, comprehensive health & dental benefits, pension plan, and paid time off.

The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity.

We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) technology — alongside human review — to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. Our recruitment team remains involved in all decisions.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada as the company does not provide work permit sponsorship for this role.

Note to Recruiters: QuadReal does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to QuadReal, directly or indirectly, will be considered QuadReal property. QuadReal will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. Conduct continuous reviews of revenue strategies, team processes, and systems to identify areas for improvement, scalability, and efficiency gains.

jobs.description:
Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

Director, Legal Counsel, Data & Privac
y | Brampton

The Data Trust Office is an enablement-first function. We embed privacy and data governance into products and services to build customer trust and loyalty, ensuring compliance by design.

As Director, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and driving Loblaw's enterprise privacy and data governance program. You will be accountable for executing the Data Trust strategy, overseeing risk management and compliance activities, developing policy, managing breaches, and fostering stakeholder engagement across the business.

As Legal Counsel, you will serve as a key partner to the commercial legal team, providing privacy, data and cybersecurity subject matter expertise on complex commercial arrangements and supporting the development, review and negotiation of appropriate contractual protections.

In both functions you will provide strategic, practical and business-oriented legal advice on privacy, data governance, CASL and related regulatory matters to the business, helping them navigate complex legal requirements while enabling the responsible use of data and innovation.

This role reports to the Enterprise Privacy Officer.

What You'll Do

Champion privacy as a business enabler by driving stakeholder engagement and embedding privacy and data governance into products and services.
Provide strategic legal advice on privacy, data governance, CASL and related regulatory matters across the business, including in connection with new products, services, technologies, digital initiatives, data uses, artificial intelligence, marketing and other strategic projects and transactions.
Advise on the interpretation and application of privacy laws, CASL, related regulatory requirements and regulator guidance, translating legal requirements into practical, business-oriented advice.
Conduct Data and Privacy Impact Assessments (DPIAs), identify and evaluate legal, regulatory, data and privacy risks, and provide practical, risk-based recommendations on appropriate controls and mitigation strategies.
Partner with commercial legal counsel as the privacy, data and cybersecurity subject matter expert on commercial agreements involving personal information, data sharing, technology, vendors, artificial intelligence or access to Loblaw systems and data. Provide practical legal advice and support the negotiation and resolution of complex or escalated privacy, data and cybersecurity issues.
Provide legal advice on consent and transparency requirements, data governance and lifecycle matters, and the responsible use of data, including in connection with artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
Oversee privacy breach, complaint and investigation management activities, including intake, escalation, investigation and response, and provide legal advice on notification obligations, regulatory risk, remediation and response strategy.
Advise on privacy and CASL regulatory matters and engage with regulators, as appropriate, in connection with regulatory inquiries, investigations, complaints and other regulatory matters, including engagement and management of external legal counsel as appropriate.
Recruit, lead, and develop a high-performing data and privacy team, including coaching and developing privacy professionals and fostering strong legal and risk judgment across the team.
Stay ahead of evolving national privacy and health privacy laws, global regulatory developments, privacy-enhancing technologies, and emerging innovations (e.g., AI/LLMs), CASL and related regulatory developments, and advise on their legal, regulatory and business implications.
Partner cross-functionally across the enterprise to continuously improve privacy-related policies, templates, guidance, processes and controls and create efficiencies while maintaining appropriate legal, cybersecurity and regulatory safeguards.

What You Bring

Law degree and member in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario, with 7-10 years of relevant experience in an in-house legal department and/or compliance function, including significant experience advising on privacy and related regulatory matters. Experience at a leading law firm is also considered an asset.
Practical, solutions-oriented and agile, with strong legal and business judgment and a demonstrated ability to navigate complexity and ambiguity, move beyond identifying risk, and develop creative, pragmatic solutions that enable business objectives while appropriately managing legal, privacy and data risk.
A supportive and engaged people leader who invests in the development of their team and creates an inclusive, high-performing environment where people are empowered, supported and accountable.
Thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, with the agility to manage competing priorities, make sound decisions and drive matters forward.
Strong collaborator and trusted advisor who builds effective relationships, influences stakeholders and facilitates practical solutions across the enterprise.
Excellent communication, organizational and presentation skills, with the ability to distill complex legal, technical and privacy issues into clear, concise and actionable advice for stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Demonstrated leadership experience delivering privacy and data programs and advising on complex privacy, data and regulatory matters within large, matrixed organizations.
Significant experience interpreting and applying Canadian federal and provincial privacy laws, CASL and related regulatory requirements to complex business and technology initiatives, including digital products and services, analytics, artificial intelligence, marketing and other data-driven activities.
Demonstrated experience conducting Data and Privacy Impact Assessments (DPIAs), evaluating risk and developing practical controls and mitigation strategies.
Proven experience managing regulatory risk and engaging directly with privacy regulators, including in connection with inquiries, investigations, complaints or other regulatory matters.
Experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating privacy and cybersecurity provisions in complex commercial agreements, including data processing, data sharing, technology and vendor arrangements.
Experience advising on privacy incidents and breach response, including assessing legal and regulatory obligations and supporting cross-functional response and remediation efforts.
Experience in corporate retail, direct-to-consumer or other complex, highly regulated environments is an asset.
CIPP-C or equivalent privacy certification preferred; AIGP and DCAM certifications are considered an asset.

jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

Most roles at RSM follow a hybrid workstyle, which means team members are aligned to an RSM office and come together in person when it best supports clients, teams, development or relationship-building.
