jobs.description:
About Patra

Patra is an outcome-focused operating partner working exclusively for the insurance industry. Combining expert global teams, process intelligence, and purpose-built technology, Patra delivers measurable results to clients. With 20 years of deep domain expertise, exceptional client retention rates, and significant sustained investment in AI, Patra partners with agencies, brokers, MGAs, MGUs, and carriers to transform how insurance operations are delivered.

Core Duties

AI and data are becoming foundational capabilities across Patra’s technology organization. The AI & Data Architecture function establishes the enterprise architecture, platforms, governance, and shared capabilities that enable product teams to build intelligent applications safely and at scale.

As AI Architect, you will lead Patra’s AI & Data Architecture function, operating at a Sr. Director-level scope with responsibility for its strategy, team formation and management, systems architecture, strategic priorities, and, most importantly, reliable and impactful execution.

The function has particular responsibility for document-intensive and unstructured-data environments, including retrieval-augmented generation, semantic and vector search, AI agents, evaluation datasets, enterprise analytics, and granular AI observability.

You will report to the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) and partner with senior leaders across Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, Business Intelligence, Operations, and other business functions.

What you'll do

Lead the AI & Data Architecture function. Own the strategy, organizational structure, technical direction, priorities, delivery, quality, and operating model for Patra’s enterprise AI and data capabilities.
Form and lead the organization. Determine staffing requirements and build multidisciplinary teams spanning AI engineering, data engineering, machine learning, enterprise data architecture, analytics infrastructure, and shared AI services, while personally delivering on urgent business priorities at the same time
Manage talent and performance. Establish objectives for direct reports as your team grows, evaluate performance, provide career and leadership development, and exercise delegated authority to make or recommend decisions concerning hiring, promotions, compensation, organizational assignments, and other personnel actions.
Own the enterprise AI and data architecture. Establish Patra’s target-state architecture for how data is ingested, governed, modeled, stored, streamed, retrieved, analyzed, and consumed by enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and AI systems.
Direct architecture for document-intensive and unstructured domains. Establish enterprise standards and approve architectural approaches for document ingestion,

metadata extraction, indexing, semantic retrieval, vector search, knowledge enrichment, and AI consumption. Detailed design and implementation are delegated to subordinate professional teams.

Industrialize the Agentic AI platform. Direct the evolution of agentic capabilities into production-grade enterprise infrastructure supporting agent orchestration, tool integration, retrieval-augmented generation, model interaction, security boundaries, evaluation, observability, and appropriate human oversight.
Own AI evaluation and data strategy. Establish the standards and organizational processes governing training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, and evaluation datasets, including quality, provenance, versioning, access, retention, and appropriate use.
Treat AI observability as a strategic data asset. Establish the architecture and governance for capturing and using event streams across agent activity, model interactions, retrieval operations, tool execution, quality signals, latency, cost, failures, and human interventions.
Lead the enterprise data platform strategy. Set direction for cloud-native data capabilities including AWS services such as S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, together with platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks where appropriate.
Establish enterprise data standards. Define and govern modern approaches to operational, analytical, event-driven, semantic, and AI-oriented data modeling and ensure common architectural standards are adopted across engineering teams.
Make Business Intelligence a first-class platform stakeholder. Ensure enterprise data capabilities support analytics, operational reporting, experimentation, decision support, and executive intelligence without relying on fragmented downstream data extraction.
Build governance into the architecture. Establish standards for data ownership, lineage, provenance, classification, quality, lifecycle management, access control, AI usage, auditability, and enterprise data governance.
Protect customer and tenant data. Establish architecture and controls for strict multi-tenant client-data segregation across storage, processing, analytics, retrieval, model interaction, evaluation, and observability systems.
Own jurisdiction-aware data architecture. Establish retention, archival, residency, and deletion strategies supporting differing contractual, regulatory, and jurisdictional requirements.
Set quality and reliability expectations. Establish SLAs, SLOs, quality metrics, and operational standards for critical data assets, pipelines, AI services, retrieval systems, and shared platform capabilities.
Establish reusable platform capabilities. Direct the development of common capabilities for identity, access, observability, model access, AI evaluation, security, compliance controls, tenancy, CI/CD, and data services that can be consumed across product organizations.
Direct enterprise integration architecture. Establish standards for integrating AI and data platforms with Patra products, internal business systems, partner platforms, APIs, event streams, and external data providers.
Run AI and data capabilities as enterprise products. Treat product engineers, analytics teams, business stakeholders, and other internal organizations as customers of the platform. Establish adoption, reliability, quality, and developer-productivity measures for shared capabilities.
Own architecture governance. Lead reviews of material AI, data, and platform architecture decisions; establish reference architectures and engineering standards; approve significant architectural approaches; and resolve cross-organizational technical decisions.
Direct the AI and data portfolio. Establish priorities across concurrent AI, data, and platform programs and allocate engineering and data-science resources according to business value, organizational capacity, technical dependencies, and enterprise risk.
Manage technology investment. Participate in annual planning, determine staffing and platform requirements, develop budget recommendations, evaluate strategic technology vendors, and make or recommend investment decisions involving AI, cloud, data, and infrastructure platforms.
Shape the multi-year technology roadmap. Partner with executive engineering and product leadership to define Patra’s AI and data roadmap and translate strategic objectives into sequenced, staffed, and measurable organizational programs.
Represent the function with senior leadership. Advise executives on AI strategy, enterprise data architecture, platform investments, organizational capacity, delivery risk, AI risk, governance, and major technology trade-offs.

How You Think About AI And Data Platforms

We are looking for a leader whose operating instincts align with how we build.

Build shared capabilities once. Identity, observability, model access, evaluation, security, governance, tenancy, CI/CD, and data access should be established as reusable platform capabilities rather than repeatedly implemented by individual teams.
Data is a product. Enterprise data, documents, application events, model interactions, evaluation results, and observability signals are strategic assets with defined owners, contracts, quality expectations, governance, and consumers.
AI-ready from ingestion onward. Documents, metadata, events, permissions, lineage, and semantic context should be designed so that they can safely support applications, analytics, machine learning, retrieval, and agentic systems.
Governance is architecture. Customer isolation, security, retention, residency, auditability, Responsible AI, and regulatory considerations are architectural requirements rather than controls added after systems have been built.
Evaluation precedes confidence. Production AI requires measurable success criteria, curated evaluation datasets, regression testing, observability, and mechanisms for detecting degraded behavior.
Observability is a first-class data asset. Agent activity, retrievals, model calls, tool calls, cost, latency, failures, quality signals, user feedback, and human interventions should produce structured and governed telemetry.
Automation over operational heroics. Repeated manual intervention represents an architectural or platform gap. Provisioning, deployment, evaluation, governance checks, and operational processes should increasingly be automated.
Self-service over central bottlenecks. The AI & Data Architecture organization exists to increase the leverage of engineering and product teams, not to become a ticket queue they must pass through.
Human oversight is intentional. Increasing autonomy should be accompanied by explicit decision boundaries, escalation mechanisms, auditability, and controls appropriate to the risk of the workflow.
Incremental over big-bang. Major platform transitions should produce measurable production value incrementally, with explicit migration plans and accountable milestones.
Specifications precede implementation. As AI accelerates implementation, clear requirements, contracts, architectural boundaries, evaluation criteria, and ownership become more important.
Decisions are explicit. Make trade-offs visible across cost, risk, reliability, security, scalability, and time-to-value. Once a decision is made, establish ownership and execute against it.

Qualifications

Technical and organizational depth. 10+ years of progressive experience across software engineering, enterprise architecture, data engineering, cloud platforms, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, including significant experience leading senior technical professionals.
Organizational leadership. Demonstrated experience forming, scaling, and leading multidisciplinary engineering and data organizations.
People management. Experience hiring professional employees, developing managers and technical leaders, evaluating performance, making promotion and compensation recommendations, planning organizational capacity, and allocating resources across teams and strategic initiatives.
Enterprise AI credibility. Deep understanding of production AI systems including LLM applications, RAG, embeddings, semantic and vector search, agentic architectures, AI orchestration, evaluation, observability, governance, and human-in-the-loop systems.
Enterprise data architecture. Significant experience directing the architecture of platforms supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured enterprise data.
Document-intensive domains. Experience with architectures where documents and unstructured information are important business assets supporting operational workflows, search, analytics, AI, and governance.
Cloud and modern data platforms. Experience establishing strategy around AWS-native data services including S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, as well as platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Enterprise AI
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Serve as a strategic advisor and execution partner to the Chief AI Officer, helping shape and deliver Equinix’s enterprise AI agenda. The role spans AI strategy and governance, enterprise adoption and value realization, organizational capability, and the external AI ecosystem. Translate priorities into funded plans and measurable outcomes, strengthen executive decision-making, and enable the AI leadership team to operate effectively across a global organization.

The successful candidate combines independent judgment, practical AI fluency, and hands-on execution. They anticipate what needs attention, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of complex work from initial framing through completion.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Executive Advisory

Partner with the CAIO to define and communicate the enterprise AI strategy, priorities, and investment roadmap, connecting internal transformation with Equinix’s broader AI business and ecosystem strategy
Develop decision briefs with clear recommendations, alternatives, financial implications, and risks. Provide candid advice and test the assumptions behind major proposals
Assess emerging AI capabilities, competitors, and partnerships, distinguishing developments that warrant action from those that warrant monitoring
Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from problem definition through delivery, establishing ownership and transitioning ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate teams

Business Operations & Execution

Own the AI leadership team’s operating rhythm, including planning, portfolio reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites. Structure forums around decisions, with clear owners, deadlines, and follow-through
Drive portfolio visibility across priorities, dependencies, investment, and results. Work with Finance and business owners to validate value assumptions and distinguish realized benefits from forecasts
Coordinate budget and workforce planning with Finance and HR. Surface resource trade-offs and recommend where to accelerate, adjust, or stop investment
Resolve execution barriers with accountable leaders and escalate material risks early, with options and a recommended course of action
Represent the CAIO as delegated, exercising judgment within agreed decision rights and keeping the CAIO informed of consequential commitments

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted partnerships with executive leaders, Chiefs of Staff, and business owners to secure sponsorship and drive enterprise AI adoption and value realization
Resolve cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities. Make ownership explicit and address difficult issues directly and constructively
Lead preparation of Board and executive materials, decision memos, and organizational communications, translating technical detail into clear business implications and specific asks
Prepare the CAIO for customer, partner, and industry engagements. Define the purpose of each engagement and drive follow-through, aligning external messaging with Communications and Marketing

Organizational Effectiveness & Transformation

Partner with the AI leadership team and HR on operating model evolution, workforce priorities, and leadership development. Identify capability gaps and clarify responsibilities as the organization scales
Coordinate with AI governance, Security, Legal, and other control functions to bring responsible AI requirements and unresolved risk decisions into portfolio planning and executive reviews
Advance AI fluency and change initiatives with business leaders, using adoption and outcome evidence to identify what needs to change
Improve how the organization works through simple processes and practical use of AI, reducing manual reporting and unnecessary meetings. Model a culture of High Standard, Low Bureaucracy, Zero Blame

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience

10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, consulting, Chief of Staff, product, data, AI, or related leadership roles, with demonstrated ownership of execution and business results
Strong understanding of enterprise AI and technology operating models, including generative AI, agents, shared platforms, adoption barriers, and AI economics and risk. Able to engage credibly with technical and business leaders
Proven experience delivering complex initiatives across a large, global, matrixed organization, including resolving competing priorities and recovering work that is off track
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with experience in business cases, investment prioritization, budget planning, and benefits measurement
Experience personally developing executive communications, Board materials, and strategic plans that require limited revision and support consequential decisions
Experience partnering with C-suite executives through ambiguity and organizational change. Prior Chief of Staff experience is valuable; equivalent operating leadership experience is equally relevant

Skills & Attributes

Strategic judgment: Frame the right problem, make trade-offs, and offer an independent point of view
Execution discipline: Take ownership without waiting for detailed direction and close commitments reliably
Executive communication: Synthesize complex issues into concise, accurate writing and clear discussion
Trust and discretion: Handle sensitive matters with integrity and the confidence to challenge respectfully
Influence and collaboration: Build credibility across functions and hold peers accountable while preserving trust
Learning agility: Develop technical and business context quickly, use AI tools effectively, and verify their outputs
Calm leadership: Remain effective under pressure, recognize when to act independently and when to escalate, and put team outcomes first

jobs.title: Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities

Reports to EVP Corporate Services

100% virtual

12-15 month engagement

Our client is a highly reputable Canadian organization
with a significant and multifaceted mandate. During a period of leadership transition, they are seeking an accomplished Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities
to provide stability, strong financial stewardship and experienced leadership while helping position the organization for its next chapter.

This is more than a maintenance assignment. It is an opportunity for an experienced finance executive to come in, make an immediate impact and elevate an already high-performing function
. The successful interim will inherit a capable team and will be expected to provide visible leadership, bring fresh perspective, strengthen financial insight and discipline, and identify opportunities to enhance the sophistication and effectiveness of the function.
The mandate spans financial reporting, planning, performance management, risk and controls, treasury, facilities and procurement, while providing senior leadership with thoughtful financial advice and insight.

The Mandate

Working closely with the senior executive team, the Interim VP will take leadership of the finance function and ensure continued strength in the organization's financial management during the transition.

This is a role for someone equally comfortable around the executive table and in the details
. The successful executive will be strategic when the situation requires it, but willing to roll up their sleeves, challenge assumptions, solve problems and help the team execute.

Key priorities will include:

Providing strong financial stewardship
, ensuring the continued integrity, accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting, forecasting and financial operations.
Leading and supporting a strong finance team, creating clarity, engagement and momentum through a period of change.
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership, bringing insight to organizational performance, longer-term planning and decision-making.
Reviewing existing financial processes, controls and practices and identifying opportunities to modernize, streamline and elevate the sophistication of the function.
Providing leadership across facilities management and procurement, ensuring strong governance, commercial discipline and effective execution.
Strengthening budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, risk management and performance reporting.
Working effectively with external advisors, auditors and other key stakeholders.
Supporting senior leadership and the organization's governance bodies with credible, thoughtful financial insight. The underlying position specifically supports Audit and Finance Committee and Board activities.
Looking beyond business-as-usual to identify opportunities to drive change, improve effectiveness and leave the organization stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

The Ideal Interim Executive

We are looking for a seasoned financial executive who knows how to enter an established organization, quickly understand the environment and add value without unnecessary disruption
.

Ideally, this individual will bring a combination of not-for-profit and commercial experience
, pairing an understanding of stewardship, governance and stakeholder accountability with the commercial instincts and operational discipline of the private sector.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant senior financial leadership experience within a complex organization.
A professional accounting designation, with strong technical grounding across accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and internal controls. The underlying profile calls for a CPA/CA-preferred designation and experience with IFRS, ASPE and ASNPO.
Experience leading strong teams through periods of transition, change or transformation
.
A genuinely hands-on style. Someone prepared to get into the numbers and issues rather than lead exclusively from 30,000 feet.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
.
Exposure to facilities, procurement and broader corporate services would be highly valuable.
Strong executive presence and the ability to establish credibility quickly with senior executives, employees, external advisors and governance stakeholders.
A pragmatic, collaborative leadership style with the confidence to respectfully challenge the status quo.
Experience operating across both mission-driven/not-for-profit and commercially oriented environments
would be particularly attractive.

Why This Assignment?

For the right interim executive, this offers the opportunity to do what great interims do best: step into an important organization at an important moment and make a measurable difference.

You will be joining a high-performing team rather than rebuilding a broken function. The opportunity is to provide leadership through transition, bring an objective external lens, elevate financial and operational practices, and create sustainable improvements that remain long after the assignment has concluded.

This is an assignment for someone who enjoys being more than a caretaker. It requires an executive who can protect what is working, challenge what can be better, and create momentum for what comes next.

Our interim executives step in with minimal downtime to meet specific objectives and deliver results. All have held senior positions in the past and have now chosen to offer their unique depth and breadth of experience to organizations on a limited engagement basis.

Vice President, Finance

Our Edmonton client is a privately held, internationally recognized healthcare technology organization providing specialized medical equipment, clinical solutions, and technical support to healthcare providers across North America. The company has established a reputation for operational excellence, strong customer partnerships, and a commitment to advancing patient care through innovative technologies.

Reporting to the CFO and serving as a key member of the leadership team, the Vice President, Finance will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s global finance function.

This role is responsible for ensuring the integrity of financial reporting, planning, controls, taxation, treasury, and compliance while providing timely financial insight that supports business strategy, sustainable growth, and informed decision-making. The successful candidate will lead a global finance team and partner closely with executive leadership, Operations, Commercial, and other functional leaders to align financial priorities with business objectives.

This opportunity is ideally suited for a collaborative finance leader who combines strong technical expertise with business partnership skills and enjoys operating in a complex, multi-entity, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Lead the global finance function, including financial reporting, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, taxation, compliance, and financial governance.
Ensure timely and accurate financial reporting in compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Provide financial reporting, analysis, and insight to the Board, executive leadership, lenders, and other relevant stakeholders.
Oversee global consolidated reporting, annual audits, bank reporting, and financial oversight across multiple entities and jurisdictions.
Lead the Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) function, including budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning, financial modelling, and performance analysis.
Provide financial insight and recommendations to support strategic and operational decisions.
Establish and maintain an effective global financial control environment, including policies, approval authorities, segregation of duties, and financial governance practices.
Manage the company's cash flow and liquidity, including cash management, investment governance, debt management, and foreign exchange risk management.
Ensure compliance with tax, legal, and regulatory requirements, including transfer pricing and global reporting obligations.
Serve as the finance leader responsible for the ongoing maintenance, optimization, and continuous improvement of the global ERP system.
Partner with Operations, Commercial, and executive leadership to evaluate investments, growth opportunities, pricing decisions, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead, develop, and support a high-performing finance team by setting clear expectations, fostering accountability and engagement, providing regular coaching and feedback, and managing performance to achieve objectives.

Candidate Experience

While no individual will embody every quality, the successful candidate will bring many of the following professional qualifications and personal competencies:

Recognized accounting designation (CPA).
University degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
10-15 years of progressive finance experience, including significant senior leadership experience.
Experience in global operations, manufacturing, or a similarly complex business environment.
Experience leading consolidated reporting, audits, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, taxation, and financial controls across multiple entities and jurisdictions.
Strong understanding of enterprise-scale global ERP systems and the ability to lead finance system optimization and adoption.
Advanced financial modelling, analysis, and reporting capabilities, including strong proficiency with Excel and enterprise reporting tools.
SAP experience is considered an asset.
In-depth knowledge of finance, accounting, budgeting, and cost accounting principles.
Strategic and commercially minded, with the ability to connect financial results to business priorities.
Demonstrates sound judgment, integrity, discretion, and accountability.
Builds trust and productive relationships across Operations, Commercial, and corporate functions.
Communicates complex financial information clearly to financial and non-financial audiences.
Demonstrates strong analytical, problem-solving, prioritization, and decision-making capabilities.
Strong leadership, coaching, and managerial skills.
Organized problem solver who excels in fast-paced environments and demonstrates strong judgment under pressure.

Edmonton, AB

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.
A final in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to explore mutual fit, discuss your vision for the role, and answer any remaining questions. Finalists may also have the opportunity to meet additional members of the leadership team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Job Description

The Finance Director leads core financial reporting, regulatory reporting, and FP&A activities while playing a key role in ongoing finance transformation initiatives. This role oversees month-end close, prepares and reviews financial statements and management reporting, and ensures audit-ready documentation and regulatory compliance. The Finance Director also supports IFRS 17 implementation, systems and process improvements, and provides strategic financial analysis and executive reporting in a collaborative, highly visible finance environment.

Responsibilities

Lead and support monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes, ensuring timely and accurate completion.
Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules for balance sheet and income statement accounts.
Analyze balance sheet and income statement fluctuations to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and communicate findings to leadership.
Prepare financial statements and comprehensive management reporting packages for senior leadership and key stakeholders.
Maintain audit-ready supporting documentation for all financial reporting activities and ensure strong internal controls.
Support internal and external audit requirements, including preparation of audit materials and responding to audit inquiries.
Oversee and support regulatory reporting activities, including OSFI and other regulatory filings.
Prepare reporting schedules, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for regulatory submissions.
Review regulatory filings to ensure reporting accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable regulations.
Support finance transformation initiatives, with a particular focus on IFRS 17-related process enhancements and implementation activities.
Participate in testing, controls validation, data verification, and user acceptance testing for new and enhanced finance processes and systems.
Contribute to finance systems and process improvement initiatives, including ERP, reporting, and finance system implementations and integrations.
Lead or support FP&A activities, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes.
Develop financial models and analytical reporting to support decision-making and strategic planning.
Perform variance analysis on financial results and provide clear, insightful explanations for executive reporting.
Prepare and deliver executive reporting and presentations that summarize financial performance, forecasts, and key insights.
Provide technical accounting guidance, including gap analysis and interpretation of complex accounting standards such as IFRS 17.
Collaborate closely with accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams to drive results and support enterprise-wide initiatives.
Demonstrate leadership within a small, highly visible finance team, contributing across multiple areas of finance as needed.
Adapt to changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong communication and collaboration across the organization.

Essential Skills

Proven experience in financial reporting, including preparation and review of financial statements and management reporting packages.
Strong background in month-end close processes, journal entries, reconciliations, and supporting schedules.
Expertise in forecasting, budgeting, and financial planning and analysis (FP&A).
Demonstrated ability to perform detailed variance analysis and provide clear, actionable insights.
Experience with regulatory reporting, particularly OSFI reporting requirements.
Hands-on experience with IFRS 17 and related technical accounting and process implications.
Strong technical accounting skills, including closing and reporting and gap analysis.
Experience supporting finance transformation and process improvement initiatives.
Proficiency with ERP and finance systems, including SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting.
Leadership experience in a finance function, with the ability to work in a small, highly visible team.
Knowledge of Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance financial and regulatory requirements.
Audit experience, including supporting internal and external audits.
Excellent analytical, reporting, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to executives and stakeholders.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

CPA designation.
Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field.
Experience working within Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance organizations.
Hands-on experience with SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting systems.
background in audit, either in public accounting or corporate audit functions.
Experience with integration projects and enterprise-wide system implementations.
Proven ability to support finance transformation initiatives and process improvements.
Comfort operating in a hands-on environment and contributing across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and strategic projects.
Ability to navigate changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong collaboration.
Track record of partnering with senior finance leadership, including CFO-level stakeholders.

Work Environment

This role operates within a small, collaborative, and highly visible finance team where professionals work closely with the CFO and finance leadership. The culture is hands-on, with a strong emphasis on adaptability, clear communication, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves wherever support is needed. The position follows a hybrid work model, with a company policy of three days per week in the office and a standard 37.5-hour workweek. The office is located in Toronto and provides exposure to major finance transformation initiatives, including IFRS 17 implementation, ERP and reporting system enhancements, and enterprise-wide process improvements. Team members partner across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams, gaining broad experience in financial reporting, accounting, FP&A, and strategic projects within a dynamic, transformation-focused environment.

Scopely
is seeking a Director, Cloud Governance
to lead efforts in establishing and enforcing standards, policies, and guardrails across Scopely’s multi-cloud environment. This is a remote opportunity for individuals in Canada or the United States.

As a Director, Cloud Governance
you will play a pivotal leadership role in defining and executing the Scopely’s Cloud Governance strategy. This team will define, implement, and enforce the policies and controls that govern how cloud infrastructure is used across a decentralized organization of game, platform, and product teams.

This role is critical to bringing structure, consistency, and guardrails to Scopely’s cloud footprint, and will be key in modernizing our overall governance posture. As a central leader, you will drive alignment across highly autonomous teams and translate governance into practical, adoptable solutions while balancing control and development velocity.

This is a foundational leadership role; you will establish governance from the ground up, introduce scalable and enforceable controls, and drive adoption and buy-in across various teams, stakeholders, and senior leaders.

What You Will Do

Build & Lead Cloud Governance

Build and lead a Cloud Governance team
Define the operating model for how governance partners with game teams, security, and FinOps
Establish clear ownership and enforcement mechanisms for cloud policies

Define & Enforce Cloud Guardrails

Design and implement enforceable controls across AWS and GCP, including:
AWS Organizations, Service Control Policies (SCPs)
GCP Organization Policies and IAM constraints

Establish guardrails around:
Resource provisioning and service usage
Region restrictions and data residency
Identity and access management
Network architecture and environment isolation

Own the mandate to enforce policies, including the ability to restrict or block non-compliant usage

Standardize Cloud Structure

Define and implement standards for:
AWS account structure and GCP project/folder hierarchy
Environment segmentation (prod, staging, dev)
Naming conventions and resource organization

Bring consistency across a fragmented, multi-team cloud footprint

Tagging & Governance

Define and enforce tagging standards in partnership with FinOps
Ensure all resources are attributable (ownership, environment, cost center)
Enable downstream cost allocation and operational visibility

Stakeholder Partnership

Collaborate with FinOps on cost allocation and optimization levers (budgets, quotas, usage controls)
Partner with Security to align governance with security and compliance requirements
Work directly with game teams to safely roll out and drive adoption of policies and standards

AI-Forward Governance & Automation

Define and execute an AI-native vision for cloud governance, transforming the function into an intelligent, policy-driven operating model powered by autonomous and agentic systems
Establish the organization’s strategy for governance autonomy, defining where fully autonomous operations, human-on-the-loop oversight, and human-in-the-loop approvals are appropriate based on risk, business impact, and compliance requirements
Architect and drive agentic governance capabilities that continuously monitor cloud environments, detect risk, and autonomously remediate anomalies at scale
Partner across engineering, data, and security, and platform teams to embed responsible AI governance into cloud platforms, establishing guardrails for AI adoption, autonomous decision-making, and auditability

What We're Looking For

10+ years in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or SRE
3–5+ years leading teams in complex, multi-team environments
Experience operating in decentralized or federated engineering organizations
Proven track record implementing cloud governance and enforcement at scale
Experience managing or influencing environments with $50M+ cloud spend
Deep hands-on experience with AWS and/or GCP
Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform)
Experience with policy-as-code and governance tooling (e.g., OPA, Sentinel, AWS Config)
Strong understanding of cloud networking, identity, and multi-account design

About Hatfield

Hatfield, a proudly Canadian company, has been serving our clients and our community for over 50 years. We have been recognized as one of Canada’s Top SME Employers in 2025. With 250 team members and growing, Hatfield provides high-quality environmental and social services for private and public sector clients around the world. When you join Hatfield, you choose a career that makes a difference in the lives of all those who share our planet.

Hatfield is seeking a Leader of Finance. This position will provide oversight of financial planning, management of financial risks, record-keeping, and financial reporting. The Leader of Finance will work closely with and is accountable to Hatfield’s Managing Partners and Board, reporting directly to the Senior Vice President & Managing Partner.

Responsibilities

Financial Operations:

Cash flow forecasting and monitoring cash flow to ensure the company has sufficient liquidity for operations and investments.
Leading financial forecasting, budgeting, and long-term planning.
Overseeing tax compliance and optimization strategies in collaboration with external advisors.
Ensuring the company’s financial systems are legally compliant and progressively support operations and future growth.
Overseeing the company’s annual operating budget to ensure that financial resources are used efficiently and effectively.
Collaborating with operations to optimize cost-effective sourcing, improve equipment tracking, and streamline charge-out processes to enhance operational efficiency.

Financial Oversight And Reporting

Overseeing the company’s financial operations and ensuring timely and accurate financial reports and practices.
Ensuring that financial reports are compliant with Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles and accurately represent the company’s financial position.
Maintaining effective internal controls and financial review processes to ensure the accuracy and reliability of financial statements.

Strategic Initiatives

Supporting company goals and objectives with progressive financial strategies.
Collaborating with other senior managers to make informed decisions about investments, capital structure, and profitability.

Leadership

Building and leading an effective finance and accounting team ensuring they are motivated and performing to the best of their abilities.
Leading the Hatfield Finance Committee and ensuring the Committee’s efforts support Hatfield’s financial objectives.
Overseeing financial planning and analysis functions to support strategic decision-making and business growth.

Risk Management

Managing insurance policy renewals, ensuring adequate coverage, and addressing compliance with regulatory requirements.
Identifying and addressing financial risks to the company and recommending measures to mitigate them.

Mergers And Acquisitions

Providing financial analysis and recommendations on potential M&A opportunities.
Evaluating financial viability and risks factors associated with potential acquisitions.

Board Consultation

Advising the Hatfield Board and the Managing Partners on corporate financial strategies.
Providing insights into financial implications of corporate strategic decisions to ensure alignment with Hatfield’s financial goals.

Outputs To The Managing Partners And Finance Committee

Provide ongoing financial and business intelligence metrics derived from Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, supporting operational decision making at Corporate and Group Director levels.
Provide monthly and year-to-date financial reports including income statements, fee and cashflow projections, Accounts Receivable (A/R), Write-off, and Work in Progress (WIP) reports.
Provide quarterly recommendations to the Finance Committee on cash management and capital allocation, considering operational needs and financing requirements.
Provide monthly comparison of budgeted financials vs actual performance, identifying any significant variances and providing justification and recommended actions.
Coordinate the review of annual financial statements provided by Hatfield’s external accountants, as well as corporate valuation and interim valuation.

Education and Experience

CPA designation and a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or related field.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role overseeing and leading a team.
Strong knowledge of accounting principles and a background with data analysis.
Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central (or comparable mid-market ERP), including optimizing system use, financial reporting, controls, and process optimization.
Strong working knowledge of Power BI, including using, interpreting, and presenting financial dashboards. Experience designing dashboards is an asset.
Proven track record in strategic planning, improving operational efficiency, and leading finance and accounting teams.
Strong knowledge of Canadian tax regulations, corporate finance, and risk management.

Experience partnering with IT / ERP consultants during system implementation or optimization is a strong asset.
Experience in a project-based professional services firm, ideally environmental consulting, engineering, or a related field, is an asset.
Proactive approach to problem-solving with strong decision-making capability.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving business consulting environment.
Strong leadership and interpersonal skills.
High attention to detail and accuracy.

Friendly and down-to-earth work culture

Comprehensive health insurance – medical/dental/vision coverage

Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.

Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. Full time, 40 hours per week, flexible between 7am and 7pm EST. This role is client facing.
📍 Location:
Remote, Canada

The role

You carry a portfolio of eCommerce clients as their strategic finance partner. You lead financial reviews with founders, own forecasting and cash flow strategy, and make sure the numbers tell the story of the business rather than just closing correctly.

Our clients are 7 to 9 figure eCommerce and digital first brands, usually in high growth. You will work alongside our Accounting Managers and Controllers, reviewing their month end work before it reaches the client, and in some cases working directly with accountants. Portfolio size varies with client size and complexity. What stays constant is that you are holding several businesses in your head at once and switching context cleanly between them.

You work a 40 hour week aligned to EST, flexible between 7am and 7pm. You can live anywhere in Canada, and you are welcome to work from abroad for up to two months a year while staying on EST hours. This is not an in house finance role and it is not oversight only. You will build models yourself, present to founders yourself, and be in the detail when the detail matters.

⭐ Must have

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance
Experience managing several clients or business units at once, rather than a single in house employer
Experience reviewing month end work produced by others, for logic as well as accuracy
Advanced financial modelling and forecasting, hands on
Strong understanding of full cycle accounting and financial operations
Confidence presenting to founders and executives. You will be leading these conversations, not supporting them.
English at C1 level or above, written and spoken. Our clients are North American and this role is client facing.

✨ Nice to have

CPA designation, or your country's equivalent. In progress counts.
MBA
eCommerce or consumer products exposure
Experience across varied industries. Retail, manufacturing, and multi industry backgrounds translate particularly well here.
QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite. We do not expect all three.
FP&A leadership in a high growth environment

✅ What you will do

Act as the trusted finance advisor to founders across your client portfolio
Review month end work from Accounting Managers and Controllers before it reaches the client
Lead KPI, profitability, and unit economics reviews
Build and refine forecasting models and cash flow projections
Guide clients on liquidity, financing needs, and capital allocation
Present financial reviews directly to client leadership
Keep accounting operations, financial insight, and client strategy connected

🔍 What the job actually looks like

Client review meetings are the spine of the month, and preparation for them is the bulk of the work
You get real ownership of your portfolio fast. That is the upside and the expectation.
You will be reviewing month end work regularly, not occasionally
You will be presenting to founders regularly, not occasionally
You have biweekly strategic finance office hours with our founder to pressure test your thinking and get quick answers
Some of our processes are mature and others are still being built. When you hit a gap, we expect you to help close it.

🚫 This role is not for you if

You have only ever worked in house for a single business and prefer it that way
You want to step back from hands on modelling and analysis
You are uncomfortable being the person in the room delivering hard numbers to a founder
You want a process that is already finished

🎁 Perks and benefits

🌴 Time off:
Paid time off, Me Days, statutory holidays, and a company wide closure from December 24th to January 2nd or 3rd.
❤️ Health benefits;
Coverage through Sun Life with 75% employer contribution, including paramedical services, dental, vision, and life insurance.
📚 Continuous learning:
CPA membership dues and required professional development covered, plus certifications and internal training.
📈 Grow with us:
We promote from within based on performance and impact.
💻 Equipment:
A laptop plus two to four monitors, your choice, along with a mouse and keyboard.
🔥 Fully remote and async first:
You will report directly to our CEO.

💙 How we hire

Our process is transparent, efficient, and respectful of your time:
Apply via Typeform. Short questions and a brief video. No cover letter.
Intro call with the People Team, 30 minutes
Scenario based assessment, reviewed by our leadership team
Final interview with leadership, 45 minutes
Offer. If it is a mutual fit, we move quickly.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________

Le poste

Vous prenez en charge un portefeuille de clients en commerce électronique à titre de partenaire financier stratégique. Vous dirigez les analyses financières avec les fondateurs, vous êtes responsable des prévisions et de la stratégie de trésorerie, et vous veillez à ce que les chiffres racontent réellement l'histoire de l'entreprise, et pas seulement à ce que la clôture soit exacte.

Nos clients sont des marques de commerce électronique et des entreprises numériques dont les revenus se chiffrent en millions ou en dizaines de millions, généralement en forte croissance. Vous travaillerez aux côtés de nos gestionnaires comptables et de nos contrôleurs, en révisant leur travail de fin de mois avant qu'il ne parvienne au client, et dans certains cas directement avec les comptables. La taille du portefeuille varie selon l'envergure et la complexité des clients. Ce qui demeure constant, c'est que vous gérez plusieurs entreprises en parallèle et que vous passez de l'une à l'autre avec aisance.

Vous travaillez 40 heures par semaine selon le fuseau HNE, avec souplesse entre 7 h et 19 h. Vous pouvez résider partout au Canada, et vous pouvez travailler de l'étranger jusqu'à deux mois par année, à condition de demeurer aligné sur les heures HNE. Il ne s'agit ni d'un poste de finance à l'interne, ni d'un rôle de supervision seulement. Vous construirez les modèles vous-même, vous présenterez aux fondateurs vous-même, et vous serez dans le détail lorsque le détail compte.

⭐ Exigences

Baccalauréat en comptabilité, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe
Au moins 7 ans d'expérience progressive en comptabilité et en finance

Title:
Director of Finance
Role:
Full-Time, Permanent
Reports to:
CFO
Application Deadline:
December 1, 2026

Who We Are

Other.™ is raising the bar in the North American advertising industry, setting a new standard for measurable impact, transparency, and accountability, for both our team and the clients we partner with.

We're a privately owned, Toronto-based team of about 50, led by a small Leadership Team. Our work runs on Propel™, our proprietary operating methodology, and PerformanceLock™, our outcome-linked compensation model, so clients get a system that's been refined across hundreds of engagements rather than a team starting from scratch on every account.

Our growth speaks for itself: we've been named to The Globe & Mail's list of Canada's Top Growing Companies for three consecutive years, and to the Financial Times' The Americas' Fastest Growing Companies 2026 list. This role sits right at the center of what's next: we're bringing Planning and Performance together into one integrated function for the first time, and this hire is who builds it.
Our headquarters is in Toronto's Financial District, steps from Union Station, with a second office steps from Parliament Hill in Ottawa. We operate as a hybrid team, with no in-office mandate.

What You’d Be Up To

As Director of Finance, you’ll play a critical role in shaping the financial health, operational efficiency, and multi-entity growth of the company. You’ll serve as the primary in-house financial anchor, balancing direct oversight of day-to-day operations across our Canadian and US entities with strategic partnership at the executive level, ensuring we’re running with financial precision today and set up to scale cleanly tomorrow.

Who You’ll Lead & Work With

Reporting to
: Chief Financial Officer
Direct Reports & Vendor Oversight
: Direct management of in-house finance operations across Canadian and US entities, with direct oversight and day-to-day operational leadership of fractional resources, including a fractional Controller and a fractional Bookkeeper.

Responsibilities

Financial Accuracy, Operations & Multi-Entity Governance

Serve as the primary in-house owner for the overall accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of company financials across Canadian and US entities, ensuring books are tight, consolidated, and audit-ready at all times.
Lead and manage external fractional partners (Controller and Bookkeeper), establishing clear SLAs, review protocols, and quality control for monthly close cycles.
Maintain strict internal controls and governance over month-end close, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and reconciliations managed by fractional partners.
Partner with the fractional Controller and external tax advisors to ensure full compliance with Canadian and US federal, state/provincial tax, audit, and regulatory requirements.

US Operations, Cross-Border & Intercompany Management

Structure and manage scalable financial operations, banking infrastructure, and accounting workflows for our US corporation.
Oversee intercompany accounting, transfer pricing compliance, and intercompany agreements to ensure clean multi-entity consolidation and regulatory alignment.
Coordinate cross-border tax strategy, corporate filings, and state-level compliance (e.g., state sales tax, state income tax, nexus considerations) with specialized external advisors.

Treasury, Cash & Foreign Exchange Management

Own consolidated liquidity visibility across CAD and USD accounts; build and maintain rolling 13-week cash flow models to drive proactive cash planning and inform CFO decision-making.
Operationalize treasury management strategies established by the CFO while ensuring seamless working capital across entities.
Monitor FX risk across multi-currency revenue and expense streams; execute CFO-approved hedging strategies, forward contracts, and intercompany currency transfers to protect against volatility.
Manage day-to-day banking workflows, user access, account administration, and credit line monitoring across Canadian and US financial institutions.

Systems, Process Improvement & Vendor Management

Evaluate, implement and optimize the finance tech stack
Identify and execute automation and system integrations to streamline financial workflows, accelerate month-end closes, and eliminate manual reporting errors across entities.
Manage relationships and service agreements with software providers and external financial vendors in both regions.

Strategic FP&A, Commercial Insight & Executive Advisory

Partner directly with the CFO on consolidated budgeting, multi-year forecasting, and strategic capital allocation across business units.
Analyze agency-specific metrics—including client profitability, billable realization rates, and team utilization—to advise leadership on pricing structures and resource planning.
Build dynamic models to evaluate new business scenarios, US expansion initiatives, and service lines.

Who This Role is For

Education & Credentials:
CPA designation or equivalent financial/accounting qualification required.
Experience:
8+ years of progressive experience in finance and accounting, with leadership responsibility.
Industry Experience:
Experience in advertising, marketing services, or professional services agencies (managing billable rates, project profitability, and client retainers) strongly preferred.
Cross-Border Expertise:
Practical familiarity with multi-entity financial management, consolidated reporting, and cross-border (US/Canada) tax and regulatory structures (hands-on or via external specialized advisors).
Technical Mastery:
Strong knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, experience managing cash flow modeling, and experience selecting & implementing financial tech into an organization.
Core Competencies:
Strong analytical skills, high ownership, meticulous attention to financial detail, and exceptional collaboration skills across executive leadership teams.

Things You'd Like About Our Team

Company Standing:
Part of an award-winning, Globe & Mail Top Growing Company.
Compensation:
Competitive compensation bands that form part of a strong total compensation package. Target Salary Range: $150,000 – $170,000 CAD per year base salary (plus performance bonus).
Benefits:
Top 1% benefit program of similar-sized agencies including leading mental health coverage, dental, annual health spending allowance, and more.
Work-Life Balance:
Permanent flexible hybrid-working model, including a 4.5-day work week allowing for better balance and control over your time.
Locations:
Modern offices steps from Union Station in Toronto and in downtown Ottawa.
Career Growth:
Clear career levels and review processes developed in partnership with Bright & Early.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
new_jobs.description:
The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.
Ensures the Museum maintains its tax-exempt charitable status and meets all related tax compliance requirements, including tax reporting, disbursement quotas, and dealings with the CRA.
Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.
Coordinate the integration of enterprise risk management with business continuity planning and reporting to the Board and relevant Committees.
Provide executive oversight of procurement, ensuring appropriate policies, competitive practices, delegated authorities, contract controls and value for money.

Commercial Activities

Provide financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.
Work with the responsible operational leaders to establish and monitor appropriate revenue, margin and performance targets and ensure effective financial controls and reporting.
Evaluate significant new commercial opportunities for financial viability, organizational capacity, risk and alignment with the Museum’s mission and strategic priorities.
Establish and monitor commercial performance targets.

Qualifications & Experience 

CPA designation.
MBA or graduate degree in business, finance, or a related field is an asset.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership or executive role.
Proven expertise in financial leadership, strategic planning, organizational performance, risk management, and governance.
Experience providing financial and strategic oversight of commercial activities.
Experience presenting to Boards and leading multidisciplinary teams.
Nonprofit and/or charitable sector experience in arts, culture, hospitality, tourism, entertainment, education, or other mission-driven organizations preferred.

To Apply

Please send your resume to akm.hr@akdn.org
by November 5, 2026.

The Museum thanks all those who apply; however, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please note that the Museum is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fair and accessible employment practices. Upon request, suitable accommodations are available under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act for applicants invited to an interview. The Museum encourages applications by individuals identifying as Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/persons of colour, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ+ persons, members of visible minorities and/or anyone belonging to equity-deserving groups.

Ready for the Seat You've Been Working Toward?

Not every great CFO starts with the title.

Many earn it through leadership, execution, business acumen, and the ability to help an organization reach its next level.

If you're a VP Finance, Director of Finance, or rising finance leader who has been waiting for the right opportunity to step into a CFO role, this may be exactly what you've been looking for.

Beam is seeking an ambitious, strategic, and hands-on Chief Financial Officer who wants to make a meaningful impact on a growing healthcare organization. This is a unique opportunity to join a collaborative leadership team, work directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a dynamic, physician-led business.

We believe great CFOs are more than financial experts. They're business leaders. They influence strategy. They develop people. They create accountability. They see opportunities others miss. They help organizations grow.

As a hands-on member of the senior leadership team, the CFO serves as a trusted business partner, providing reliable financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, cash flow oversight, and business analysis to support strategic decision-making, operational excellence, and the achievement of the organization's objectives.

Own the monthly, quarterly and annual financial close and ensure accurate, timely financial statements.

Coordinate the annual external audit and support tax compliance, regulatory reporting and year-end requirements.
Prepare annual budgets, forecasts, variance analysis and recurring management.
Monitor cash balances, working capital, collections and payment processes; support treasury and banking administration.
Lead and develop the accounting team while improving processes, documentation, systems and automation.
