Standardize and accelerate the month-end close with dependable reporting deadlines.
Strengthen reconciliations, internal controls, accounting policies and financial documentation.
Improve accounts receivable, collections, working-capital reporting and cash visibility.
Build useful budget-to-actual and location/service profitability reporting.
Assess accounting team responsibilities and identify opportunities for system and process automation.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

CPA designation strongly preferred.

Strong technical accounting, financial reporting, controls and close-management capabilities.
Experience in a private, entrepreneurial or multi-location operating company preferred.
Hands-on leadership style with the ability to review detail while maintaining strong deadlines and accountability.
Advanced budgeting, forecasting, Excel and financial systems skills; experience improving ERP/reporting processes is an asset.

Clear communicator who can explain financial results to both finance and non-finance managers.
Proactive, hands-on, and willing to roll up their sleeves.
Strong leadership skills.
Able to think outside the box and find creative solutions.
High energy and driven.
Genuinely passionate about healthcare, MedTech, and innovation.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Accurate and timely reporting
Faster and disciplined close
Strong controls and reconciliations
Improved collections and working capital
Reliable budgets and forecasts
Efficient accounting processes
A capable and accountable finance team

WHY JOIN BEAM?

This is more than a CFO role. It's an opportunity to step into a key leadership position, partner directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization. If you're ready to build, lead, influence, and make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land, Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

The onus is on candidates in receipt of foreign post-secondary education credentials to have their foreign credentials assessed through a recognized Canadian education institution. Failure to do so may result in the rejection of their application.

Aperçu

Depuis 1987, EDF solutions électriques fournit des solutions d'énergie propre aux États-Unis, au Canada et au Mexique. Nous sommes un producteur d'énergie indépendant et un fournisseur de services de premier plan sur le marché, offrant aux services publics, aux entreprises, aux industries, aux communautés, aux institutions et aux investisseurs des solutions énergétiques fiables et à faible émission de carbone qui aident à répondre à une demande croissante.

Faites partie d'une équipe collaborative et innovante qui s'engage à fournir des solutions renouvelables pour promouvoir la transition vers un avenir énergétique durable.

Avantages Et Bénéfices

EDF solutions électriques offre des avantages sociaux de premier choix, dont les suivants:

Des bonis compétitifs. Ce poste est éligible à notre programme de bonis annuels.
Une couverture médicale complète. Nous fournissons une couverture santé et bien-être aux employés et leur personnes à charges.
REER/RPDP gratifiant. Nous fournissons une généreuse contribution de contrepartie.

Nous Sommes Également Fiers D'offrir

Des programmes de congés payés avantageux.
Des opportunités d'apprentissage, de développement de carrière et d'avancement gratifiantes.
Des programmes de mentorat et de jumelage.

Échelle salariale : La fourchette salariale complète pour ce poste est entre 144,700$ - 241,100$ par an, et le salaire de départ estimé pour ce poste à l'embauche est comp ris entre 165,000$ et 180,000$ par an. Nous basons généralement nos décisions salariales sur des facteurs tels que, entre autres, l'expérience professionnelle et le leadership, la formation, les performances démontrées, l'équité interne et, dans certains cas, la situation géographique.

Objectif de l'emploi : Le directeur.trice des rapports financiers supervise l'ensemble des activités comptables et des obligations en matière de reporting de l'équipe Canada - Finance.

Responsabilités

Responsabilités

Dirige et assure la communication relative à l'ensemble de la comptabilité et du reporting financier interne pour les activités canadiennes, y compris l'élaboration et la mise à jour des plans financiers, des prévisions, des budgets, des activités et projets en cours, ainsi que d'autres prévisions et projets prospectifs. Identifie les problèmes et formule des commentaires sur les résultats financiers trimestriels, les prévisions et les projections à l'intention de la direction générale.
Identifie, recrute, développe et fidélise les talents afin de garantir une équipe hautement performante ; renforce les équipes de comptabilité et de reporting à l'échelle de l'organisation. Encadre et développe les autres collaborateurs.
Garantit l'exactitude des prévisions et le rapprochement entre le budget et les prévisions réelles et historiques pour les opérations canadiennes. Supervise les audits, résout les problèmes d'audit et gère la conformité aux exigences canadiennes en matière de divulgation. S'assure que toutes les exigences relatives aux rapports internes et externes sont respectées.
Consolide, analyse et examine les données et indicateurs financiers pour le budget d'exploitation annuel du Canada. Dirige les examens, analyse et communique les rapports de coûts pour les projets organisationnels.
Supervise, développe et documente les processus tout en mettant en œuvre des solutions technologiques cohérentes avec, et favorisant la création d'une organisation consolidée qui répond aux besoins actuels et est évolutive pour la croissance future, tant organique qu'anorganique.
Agit en tant qu'interface principale entre la fonction financière et l'entreprise, plus précisément l'AO et les parties prenantes du développement, en s'assurant que toutes les exigences en matière de rapports sont respectées pour les besoins internes et externes, tels que les rapports destinés aux partenaires et aux prêteurs.
Autres tâches assignees.

Supervision du personnel:
Deux subordonnés directs occupant des postes de direction. Dirige les services de reporting financier et de comptabilité au Canada.

Conditions de travail : Environ 95 % du temps est passé dans un environnement de bureau, à utiliser des ordinateurs ainsi que d'autres équipements de bureau. Cela implique l'utilisation fréquente du téléphone, du matériel de bureau courant et de divers logiciels, notamment, mais sans s'y limiter, les produits de la suite Microsoft Office, SAP et BusinessObjects Financial Consolidation (BOFC).

Responsabilités financières : Contribue à l'élaboration du budget de la planification et de l'analyse financières (FP&A).

Qualification

Formation/Expérience

Baccalauréat en comptabilité. Le titre de CPA et/ou un MBA sont fortement appréciés.
Au moins 10 ans d'expérience dans un poste en comptabilité ou en finance.
Expérience en consolidation requise.

Compétences/Connaissances/Aptitudes

Capacité à réagir et à prendre des décisions avec des informations limitées dans des situations de forte pression.
Maîtrise de SAP requise. Une expérience avec BOFC est un atout.
Capacité à traiter de grands volumes de données.
Excellentes compétences en communication
Capacité à gérer simultanément plusieurs projets et missions dans les délais impartis et à fournir un travail de haute qualité.
Sens aigu des affaires ainsi que des compétences en résolution de problèmes et en présentation.
Excellentes compétences en leadership au sein des services et entre eux
Exigence, intégrité et éthique.
Esprit d'initiative et orientation vers les résultats.
Bilingue anglais et français.

Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

À propos de Crowe BGK

Depuis 75 ans, Crowe BGK S.E.N.C.R.L. est un chef de file de confiance en matière de services de comptabilité et de conseil au Canada. Notre équipe compte plus de 250 professionnels qui servent nos clients à partir de nos bureaux de Montréal et d’Ottawa. Nous offrons des services d’audit, de fiscalité, de conseil et de consultation, aidant les particuliers et les sociétés privées à relever des défis complexes. Nous sommes fiers d’avoir été nommés parmi les 100 meilleurs employeurs de PME au Canada et parmi les meilleurs employeurs de Montréal, car nous croyons qu’il est essentiel de créer un milieu de travail où les gens se sentent soutenus, valorisés et inspirés à progresser.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

expérimenté(e) et pratique pour aider Crowe BGK à maintenir un environnement technologique fiable et à faire progresser l’utilisation des logiciels à l’échelle du cabinet. La personne retenue combinera une compréhension des processus d’affaires, une discipline opérationnelle et une expertise technologique afin d’améliorer le service à la clientèle, l’efficacité, l’évolutivité et l’expérience employé.

Vous Serez Responsable De

Stratégie et gouvernance des logiciels d’entreprise

Élaborer et maintenir la feuille de route pluriannuelle des applications du cabinet, l’inventaire des logiciels, le modèle de propriété et la gouvernance pour la sélection, les accès, les changements, les intégrations, les renouvellements et le retrait.
Identifier les lacunes en matière de capacités, les dédoublements, les outils sous-utilisés ou non pris en charge ainsi que les occasions émergentes; conseiller le ou la COFO, les associé(e)s et la direction sur les priorités, les investissements, les compromis, la normalisation et les coûts.

Amélioration des processus d’affaires et innovation

Analyser et repenser les processus dans les services à la clientèle et les fonctions corporatives, en mobilisant les parties prenantes afin de résoudre les irritants, les lacunes de contrôle, le travail à refaire, les problèmes de données et les besoins non satisfaits avant l’automatisation.
Utiliser les données et les commentaires pour prioriser les améliorations à forte valeur ajoutée et évaluer les flux de travail, l’automatisation, l’analytique, l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes en tenant compte de la confidentialité, de la qualité, des contrôles et de la supervision humaine appropriés.

Évaluation des logiciels et analyses de rentabilité

Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences mesurables sur les plans fonctionnel, technique, des données, de la sécurité, de l’intégration, des contrôles, du service et des utilisateurs; diriger les démonstrations, les projets pilotes, les vérifications de références, les grilles d’évaluation, la diligence raisonnable des fournisseurs et la comparaison objective des risques et des solutions de rechange.
Préparer et présenter des analyses de rentabilité pour les décisions d’aller de l’avant ou non, couvrant le coût total de possession, le rendement du capital investi, les échéanciers, les ressources, l’incidence du changement, la formation, l’atténuation des risques, le soutien et les coûts de sortie; soutenir les négociations commerciales et contractuelles.

Gouvernance et responsabilité de la mise en œuvre

Agir à titre de responsable imputable du volet affaires et technologie, en partenariat avec le ou la gestionnaire de projet attitré(e), afin de définir la portée, les résultats, le budget, les ressources, la gouvernance, les jalons, les droits décisionnels, les risques, les communications et les mesures de succès.
Coordonner les parties prenantes et veiller à la conception des processus, à la configuration, aux intégrations, à la conversion des données, aux essais, aux contrôles, à la formation, à la mise en production, au soutien, à la préparation, à la stabilisation, à l’adoption et à la réalisation des bénéfices; faire remonter les lacunes importantes et maintenir la visibilité auprès de la direction.

Gestion du portefeuille, des fournisseurs, des données et des risques

Gérer les budgets logiciels, les licences, l’utilisation, les renouvellements, les fournisseurs, les contrats, les niveaux de service, les indicateurs du portefeuille, la rationalisation et le retrait des solutions.
Collaborer avec les ressources en TI, cybersécurité, protection de la vie privée, affaires juridiques et gestion des risques afin d’encadrer les intégrations, les données, les contrôles d’accès, la continuité des activités, les risques liés aux tiers, l’intelligence artificielle et l’automatisation.

Leadership du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes

Établir des relations de confiance avec les associé(e)s, les dirigeant(e)s, le personnel, les fournisseurs et les prestataires de services; diriger les employé(e)s attitré(e)s et les équipes interfonctionnelles en assurant une responsabilisation claire et une forte orientation vers le service.
Diriger les communications, la formation, l’adoption, la documentation, le soutien et la propriété des applications; développer des ambassadeurs internes, contribuer au plan d’affaires du cabinet et tenir le ou la COFO ainsi que les parties prenantes informés.

Autorité et responsabilité

Responsable du portefeuille de logiciels, de la feuille de route des applications, des normes de gouvernance et de la direction des équipes de mise en œuvre des TI et des processus dans le cadre de la stratégie et des budgets approuvés; peut exiger les examens appropriés en matière d’affaires, de sécurité, de protection de la vie privée, d’intégration, de contrôle et de mise en œuvre.
Recommande la sélection, le séquencement, le renouvellement, l’expansion, la consolidation ou le retrait des logiciels; peut suspendre ou faire remonter les préoccupations non résolues et est responsable de la qualité des recommandations, de la gouvernance de la mise en œuvre, de l’adoption, de la stabilisation et des bénéfices approuvés.

Mesures de succès

Gérer un inventaire à jour des logiciels, une propriété claire, une gouvernance rigoureuse, une feuille de route approuvée, des analyses de rentabilité crédibles et des dépenses contrôlées.
Réaliser les mises en œuvre avec une gouvernance, une préparation, des contrôles, une adoption et un soutien durable efficaces, ainsi qu’avec la réalisation des bénéfices approuvés.
Obtenir des améliorations mesurables en matière d’efficacité, de capacité, de qualité, de fiabilité des données, d’expérience employé et client, de performance des fournisseurs, de gestion des risques et de confiance des parties prenantes.

Les Qualifications Qui Comptent

Baccalauréat en systèmes d’information, administration des affaires, comptabilité, finance, informatique, génie ou dans un domaine connexe; une combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience sera considérée.
Sept années ou plus d’expérience progressive en logiciels, systèmes d’affaires, amélioration des processus, transformation technologique, gestion de produits ou gestion de programmes, dont au moins trois années dans un rôle de leadership ou de responsabilité à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Une expérience dans un cabinet comptable ou un autre environnement de services professionnels est privilégiée, avec une compréhension des décisions dirigées par les associé(e)s, du service à la clientèle soumis à des échéanciers, de la confidentialité et du changement entre les groupes de pratique.
Succès démontré dans la direction d’évaluations de logiciels, d’analyses de rentabilité, de sélection de fournisseurs et de mise en œuvre de solutions SaaS à l’échelle du cabinet ou de l’entreprise.
Expérience pratique de la cartographie et de la refonte des processus, des exigences, des essais, de la formation, de la gestion du changement et de la réalisation des bénéfices.

Vous Pouvez Compter Sur Nous Pour

Une rémunération compétitive
Un modèle de travail hybride flexible
Des assurances collectives complètes dès le premier jour d’emploi pour soutenir votre bien-être global
Des vacances généreuses et 8 journées personnelles pour responsabilités familiales
Des fermetures du cabinet pendant les Fêtes pour décrocher pleinement
Des vendredis d’été avec fermeture hâtive durant la saison estivale
Stationnement gratuit sur place ou remboursement du transport en commun
Une allocation annuelle mieux-être pour soutenir la santé physique et mentale
Une allocation pour l’aménagement du bureau à domicile afin d’assurer un environnement confortable et productif
Une culture de bureau dynamique et accueillante, où les chiens sont les bienvenus et où l’énergie est au rendez-vous. Entre les 5 à 7 animés, les cours de spinning hebdomadaires, les ateliers de peinture en équipe, les soirées quiz et karaoké, il y a toujours une activité rassembleuse. Sans oublier notre Camp Crowe, une expérience estivale unique remplie d’activités amusantes qui favorisent la camaraderie et créent des souvenirs mémorables

Si vous cherchez un endroit où vos idées comptent et où votre carrière peut s'épanouir, postulez dès aujourd'hui!

Cultivez votre curiosité. Inspirez votre esprit. Façonnez votre carrière.

Nous maintenons un environnement de travail inclusif et offrant des chances égales afin que chaque professionnel de Crowe BGK puisse réaliser son potentiel d'évolution. Nous considérons tous les candidats qualifiés pour un emploi sans distinction de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe, d'orientation sexuelle, d'identité de genre, d'origine nationale, d'âge, d'état matrimonial, de handicap, de statut d'ancien combattant protégé ou de tout autre facteur protégé par la loi.

Nous remercions tous les candidats pour leur intérêt et nous ne contacterons que ceux que nous souhaitons poursuivre.

Director of Software Technology and Innovation

About Crowe BGK

For 75 years, Crowe BGK LLP has been a trusted leader in accounting and advisory services in Canada. We are a team of 250+ professionals serving clients from our Montreal and Ottawa offices. We provide audit, tax, advisory, and consulting services, helping individuals and private companies navigate complex challenges. We’re proud to be named one of Canada’s Top 100 SME Employers and one of Montreal’s Top Employers, because we believe in creating a workplace where people feel supported, valued, and inspired to grow.

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Director of Software Technology and Innovation

to help Crowe BGK maintain a reliable technology environment and advance the use of software across the firm. The successful candidate will combine business process insight, operational discipline, and technology expertise to improve client service, efficiency, scalability, and the employee experience.

You Will Be Accountable For

Enterprise Software Strategy and Governance

Develop and maintain the firm's multi-year application roadmap, software inventory, ownership model, and governance for selection, access, changes, integrations, renewals, and retirement.
Identify capability gaps, duplication, underused or unsupported tools, and emerging opportunities; advise the COFO, partners, and leadership on priorities, investments, trade-offs, standardization, and cost.

Business Process Improvement and Innovation

Analyze and redesign processes across client service and corporate functions, engaging stakeholders to address pain points, control gaps, rework, data issues, and unmet needs before automation.
Use data and feedback to prioritize high-value improvements and evaluate workflow, automation, analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies with appropriate confidentiality, quality, controls, and human oversight.

Software Evaluation and Business Cases

Translate business needs into measurable functional, technical, data, security, integration, control, service, and use

new_jobs.description:
Location:

North Vancouver, BC or New Westminster, BC

About Hatfield

Hatfield, a proudly Canadian company, has been serving our clients and our community for over 50 years. We have been recognized as one of Canada’s Top SME Employers in 2025. With 250 team members and growing, Hatfield provides high-quality environmental and social services for private and public sector clients around the world. When you join Hatfield, you choose a career that makes a difference in the lives of all those who share our planet.

Hatfield is seeking a Leader of Finance. This position will provide oversight of financial planning, management of financial risks, record-keeping, and financial reporting. The Leader of Finance will work closely with and is accountable to Hatfield’s Managing Partners and Board, reporting directly to the Senior Vice President & Managing Partner.

Responsibilities

Financial Operations:

Cash flow forecasting and monitoring cash flow to ensure the company has sufficient liquidity for operations and investments.
Leading financial forecasting, budgeting, and long-term planning.
Overseeing tax compliance and optimization strategies in collaboration with external advisors.
Ensuring the company’s financial systems are legally compliant and progressively support operations and future growth.
Overseeing the company’s annual operating budget to ensure that financial resources are used efficiently and effectively.
Collaborating with operations to optimize cost-effective sourcing, improve equipment tracking, and streamline charge-out processes to enhance operational efficiency.

Financial Oversight and Reporting:

Overseeing the company’s financial operations and ensuring timely and accurate financial reports and practices.
Ensuring that financial reports are compliant with Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles and accurately represent the company’s financial position.
Maintaining effective internal controls and financial review processes to ensure the accuracy and reliability of financial statements.

Strategic Initiatives

Supporting company goals and objectives with progressive financial strategies.
Collaborating with other senior managers to make informed decisions about investments, capital structure, and profitability.

Leadership:

Building and leading an effective finance and accounting team ensuring they are motivated and performing to the best of their abilities.
Leading the Hatfield Finance Committee and ensuring the Committee’s efforts support Hatfield’s financial objectives.
Overseeing financial planning and analysis functions to support strategic decision-making and business growth.

Risk Management:

Managing insurance policy renewals, ensuring adequate coverage, and addressing compliance with regulatory requirements.
Identifying and addressing financial risks to the company and recommending measures to mitigate them.

Mergers and Acquisitions:

Providing financial analysis and recommendations on potential M&A opportunities.
Evaluating financial viability and risks factors associated with potential acquisitions.

Board Consultation:

Advising the Hatfield Board and the Managing Partners on corporate financial strategies.
Providing insights into financial implications of corporate strategic decisions to ensure alignment with Hatfield's financial goals.

Outputs to the Managing Partners and Finance Committee:

Provide ongoing financial and business intelligence metrics derived from Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, supporting operational decision making at Corporate and Group Director levels.
Provide monthly and year-to-date financial reports including income statements, fee and cashflow projections, Accounts Receivable (A/R), Write-off, and Work in Progress (WIP) reports.
Provide quarterly recommendations to the Finance Committee on cash management and capital allocation, considering operational needs and financing requirements.
Provide monthly comparison of budgeted financials vs actual performance, identifying any significant variances and providing justification and recommended actions.
Coordinate the review of annual financial statements provided by Hatfield’s external accountants, as well as corporate valuation and interim valuation.

Education and Experience:

CPA designation and a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or related field.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role overseeing and leading a team.
Strong knowledge of accounting principles and a background with data analysis.
Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central (or comparable mid-market ERP), including optimizing system use, financial reporting, controls, and process optimization.
Strong working knowledge of Power BI, including using, interpreting, and presenting financial dashboards. Experience designing dashboards is an asset.
Proven track record in strategic planning, improving operational efficiency, and leading finance and accounting teams.
Strong knowledge of Canadian tax regulations, corporate finance, and risk management.

Other Assets/Skills:

Experience partnering with IT / ERP consultants during system implementation or optimization is a strong asset.
Experience in a project-based professional services firm, ideally environmental consulting, engineering, or a related field, is an asset.
Proactive approach to problem-solving with strong decision-making capability.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving business consulting environment.
Strong leadership and interpersonal skills.
High attention to detail and accuracy.

What's In It For You
?

Friendly and down-to-earth work culture
Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
Biweekly Earned Days Off (EDO) program
Matching group retirement plan
Comprehensive health insurance - medical/dental/vision coverage
Competitive vacation and special leave

About Gambler First Nation

Gambler First Nation (GFN) is an Ojibway First Nation located near Binscarth in southwestern Manitoba, within Treaty 4 territory. The Nation’s primary reserve, Gambler 63, is situated in a rural setting along the Assiniboine Valley, offering a close‑knit community environment rooted in strong cultural traditions and a deep connection to the land. GFN is one of the smaller First Nations in Manitoba, with a total registered membership of approximately 330 members, the majority of whom live off‑reserve. Despite its size, the Nation maintains an active governance structure and delivers a range of programs and services to support the wellbeing of its members, both on‑ and off‑reserve.

The Nation is a member of the West Region Tribal Council and works collaboratively with regional partners and other First Nations to advance shared priorities and access collective services. Gambler First Nation is led by an elected Chief and Council and is focused on responsible governance, community wellbeing, and sustainable administration. As Gambler First Nation continues to strengthen its organizational capacity and financial stewardship, it is committed to transparent, accountable management of its resources in support of current community needs and future generations.

Download the Full Job Description: Gambler First Nation - Director of Finance - Position Profile.pdf

About The Director Of Finance Position

Reporting to the Chief and Council, the Director of Finance plays a critical leadership role in supporting the financial stewardship and long‑term sustainability of Gambler First Nation. This position is responsible for overseeing the Nation’s financial management, reporting, budgeting, and compliance functions while providing trusted advice to Chief and Council on financial strategy and decision‑making.

The Director of Finance ensures that financial practices align with legislative requirements, funding agreements, and sound governance principles, while also supporting operational leaders in managing programs and services effectively. The role balances strong technical financial expertise with a practical, community‑focused approach, recognizing the unique governance, funding, and accountability environment of a First Nation organization.

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director of Finance contributes to organizational planning, risk management, and capacity building, and plays an important role in strengthening financial systems, controls, and reporting processes in support of transparency, accountability, and service to GFN members.

Gambler First Nation’s administrative office is transitioning from Russell, Manitoba, to Brandon, Manitoba, with the move anticipated by late Fall. The Director of Finance may work remotely, with an expectation of working in the Brandon office a minimum of two days per week once the Brandon office is fully operational.

Financial And Operational Accountabilities

Contribute to the development and execution of Gambler First Nation’s strategic and operational plans by providing financial leadership, analysis, and advice that supports community priorities and long‑term sustainability.
Lead the overall finance and accounting functions, including annual budgeting and forecasting, financial planning and analysis, reporting, capital planning, audits, insurance, asset management, cost control, and related financial activities.
Establish annual financial objectives that align with GFN’s strategic priorities, funding agreements, and governance expectations.
Translate strategic and operational plans into effective financial and accounting plans, ensuring alignment between organizational goals and day‑to‑day financial management.
Review historical financial results and emerging trends, and analyze anticipated changes to inform leadership decision‑making and future planning.
Develop and maintain financial models to support long‑term planning, scenario analysis, and risk‑informed decision‑making.
Monitor financial performance against approved budgets, analyze variances, and provide clear, timely reporting to support discussion and informed decisions by senior leadership and Council.
Ensure all financial reporting requirements are met, including those related to funding agreements, financial administration policies, and reporting obligations to government and other funding partners.
Identify financial and organizational risks within a risk‑management framework and design, implement, and maintain appropriate internal controls to mitigate those risks.
Oversee the development of processes to assess and report on the overall financial and operational performance of the organization.
Maintain effective, efficient, and compliant financial systems, processes, and practices in accordance with recognized accounting standards, policies, and procedures.
Lead the year‑end audit process, including coordination with external auditors and oversight of working papers, schedules, analyses, and supporting documentation.
Evaluate the financial performance of the organization in relation to long‑term operational goals, budgets, and forecasts, and provide strategic insights and recommendations.
Provide Chief and Council and senior leadership with accurate, timely historical, current, and projected financial information to support governance and management decisions.
Coordinate the development, review, and ongoing improvement of financial and administrative policies and procedures that support strong governance, accountability, and sound management practices.

Education And Experience Requirements

Gambler First Nation is seeking a highly collaborative Director of Finance who values relationship‑building, teamwork, and shared accountability. This role is central to supporting the Nation’s long‑term financial sustainability and requires the ability to work closely and respectfully with Chief and Council, the Band Manager, program leaders, staff, external partners, and community stakeholders.

The Director of Finance is expected to build, lead, and sustain a high‑performing finance and administration function. Chief and Council and the organization will rely on the individual in this role for sound professional judgment, strategic financial advice, and technical expertise that supports effective governance and informed decision‑making.

The ideal candidate brings experience working in First Nations or Indigenous organizational environments and understands the governance, funding, and accountability context in which First Nation governments operate.

Education

A post‑secondary degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field, combined with significant progressive experience in finance, accounting, and auditing, including senior‑level leadership of a finance function. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
A professional accounting designation, such as Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) or Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM), is considered a strong asset.
Required experience in First Nations or Indigenous finance, including work within a First Nation government, Indigenous organization, tribal council, or Indigenous advisory or accounting services environment.

Experience

Demonstrated expertise in strategic financial stewardship, including budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, business planning, asset management, cost controls, and the application of generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
Proven experience in financial modelling, financial analysis, cash‑flow management, and the monitoring and management of investments.
Strong working knowledge of federal and provincial legislation, public policy, and funding frameworks applicable to First Nation governments and entities.
Proficiency with financial systems and tools or financial and reporting applications.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex financial data and prepare clear, accurate financial reports, statements, and long‑term projections for a variety of audiences.
A highly collaborative leadership style, with the ability to work effectively across functions and build strong, respectful working relationships throughout the organization.
Demonstrated ability to clearly communicate financial information and concepts to leadership, Council, and staff who may not have financial expertise.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including presentation and negotiation skills appropriate to executive and governance‑level settings.

If you are interested in learning more about this opportunity, please call or submit your resume to:

Lillian Wong, Director, Executive Search and Professional Recruitment

Lillian.Wong@mnp.ca

Come shape the future of brand experience.

At Jack Morton, we design and build

The Opportunity

We're looking for a commercially minded and operationally focused Finance Director, Fabrication Operations
to serve as the finance lead and strategic business partner for our North American fabrication network.

Partnering directly with the Head of Fabrication, you will help build the financial and operational foundation for a growing multi-site production organization. This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and operations, can connect financial performance to what is happening on the production floor, and enjoys transforming data into actionable business decisions.

You will play a critical role in improving profitability, building reporting and forecasting capabilities, optimizing capacity utilization, and supporting the integration and standardization of fabrication operations across the network.

What You'll Do

Financial Performance & Cost Management

Build and maintain consistent individual and consolidated P&Ls across four fabrication facilities, along with separate P&Ls for storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Conduct a comprehensive assessment of facility cost structures, labor models, capacity utilization, and current reporting practices.
Develop budgeting, forecasting, and scenario-planning models covering labor, overtime, freelance resources, subcontracting, storage, fleet, and facility expenses.
Establish project profitability reviews to compare estimated versus actual margins and create feedback loops that improve future estimating and pricing decisions.
Analyze labor productivity, utilization, overhead absorption, and operational drivers of profitability.
Partner with operational leaders to identify opportunities to improve margins, reduce waste, optimize labor deployment, and increase financial discipline.
Lead monthly performance reviews with fabrication leadership teams.

Capacity Planning & Network Optimization

Map capacity against demand across the fabrication network and develop reporting that supports more effective planning and resource allocation.
Improve pipeline visibility to provide a reliable view of future fabrication demand and workload requirements.
Separate fabrication, non-fabrication, and insourced work streams to support accurate capacity planning and decision-making.
Support long-term network planning, including facility footprint decisions, capability investments, and capital expenditure evaluations.
Build financial models that support insource versus outsource decisions, staffing strategies, overtime management, and facility investments.
Support vendor consolidation initiatives, rebate tracking, and procurement savings opportunities.

Reporting, KPIs & Integration

Develop and implement a standardized KPI framework across all fabrication locations, including utilization, throughput, overtime, on-time delivery, rework, and profitability metrics.
Launch and maintain executive dashboards covering network performance, financial performance, pipeline, capacity utilization, storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Establish standardized reporting and performance management processes across all locations.
Support the integration of Jack Morton and Impact XM fabrication operations through common definitions, metrics, and processes for job costing, work orders, change orders, and markup structures.
Support D365 adoption and help reduce reliance on manual processes and offline workarounds.
Partner across Fabrication, Finance, Commercial, Estimating, Creative, Account, and Project Management teams to improve planning, visibility, profitability, and operational execution.

What We're Looking For

8-12+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing, fabrication, production, logistics, or other operational environments.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, job costing, labor utilization, overhead allocation, margin analysis, and operational performance management.
Experience supporting multiple facilities, locations, or operating units.
Demonstrated ability to build financial models, forecasting processes, dashboards, and KPI frameworks from the ground up.
Experience driving finance process improvements, operational standardization, and systems adoption within growing or transforming organizations.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable operational recommendations.
Experience evaluating capital investments and developing ROI-based business cases.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence leaders across functions.
Comfortable working in fast-paced, project-based environments where priorities can shift quickly.
Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills; experience with ERP systems and business intelligence tools preferred.
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. CPA, CMA, or MBA is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first six months, you will have:

Assessed the financial and operational performance of all fabrication facilities and support operations.
Established consistent facility, storage, rental, and fleet P&Ls.
Implemented a standardized KPI and reporting framework across the network.
Launched fabrication performance dashboards that provide clear visibility into profitability, utilization, capacity, and demand.
Built forecasting and scenario-planning tools that support operational decision-making.
Established a regular performance review cadence with facility leaders.
Improved visibility into project profitability and manufacturing economics.
Helped advance the integration and standardization of production operations across Jack Morton.

Success in this role means creating financial visibility where it does not exist today, improving profitability and operational performance, establishing disciplined forecasting and reporting processes, and helping build a scalable fabrication organization capable of supporting future growth.

new_jobs.description:
About Toronto Metropolitan

For more than 75 years, Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly known as Ryerson University) has been shaping the next generation of leaders through its uniquely innovative, entrepreneurial and career-focused approach to higher education. Driven by bold leadership, cutting-edge research and a deep commitment to academic excellence, TMU collaborates with students, faculties, staff and partners to push boundaries, reimagine solutions and create meaningful change in an increasingly interconnected world.

For a more in-depth understanding of our vision, core values and ongoing work, please see our academic plan

TMU welcomes those who have demonstrated a commitment to upholding the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion and will assist us in realizing the benefits of embedding these values into the work at every level and in every unit of the university. In addition, to correct the conditions of disadvantage in employment in Canada and to bring lived experiences to the work, we encourage applications from members of equity deserving groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples in Canada, First Nations Peoples in the United States, racialized people, Black people, persons with disabilities, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ people. Preference will be given to candidates with lived experiences as people from equity deserving groups, as well as experience working with these communities with which the University works every day. Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and we welcome newcomers and immigrants to Canada.

In April 2022, the university announced its new name of Toronto Metropolitan University. Learn more about our next chapter.

About The School Of Medicine

It’s time to transform medical education. Toronto Metropolitan University’s School of Medicine has been designed from the ground up to shift the paradigm of healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of individuals, families and communities. With a community-driven, intentionally inclusive approach, the new school is training doctors whose cultural awareness and humility are as crucial as their medical skills.

Led by Dr. Teresa M. Chan, a forward-thinking educational leader, TMU’s School of Medicine draws on the university’s commitment to community, equity, and innovation to address rapidly changing healthcare needs. The school will train a new generation of physicians who are ready to learn, to adapt, and ultimately to be agents of change.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Finance Director to join the School of Medicine! This newly created role leads the development and implementation of school-wide financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and resource management strategies that advance the academic, research, and operational priorities of the School of Medicine.

Serving as a trusted strategic advisor, the position provides expert financial counsel to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Dean, and senior leadership by assessing long-term financial implications, recommending evidence-based solutions, and ensuring alignment with broader University policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

This role oversees the financial operations of the School of Medicine, supporting budgeting, reporting, financial compliance, and informed decision-making. he Director also provides financial and advisory support to the Integrated Health Centre, including support for external financial reporting and audit requirements,, in close collaboration with TMU Financial Services and the University Planning Office.

In addition, the Director conducts financial research and analysis to inform policy development and long-term planning, and represents the CAO and the School of Medicine in TMU-wide planning discussions and committees.

Responsibilities Include

Financial planning, budgeting and management

Provides financial advice, analysis, and decision-support to departments within the School of Medicine to support budget development, financial planning, forecasting, and effective resource management.
Manages day-to-day financial activities for the School of Medicine, including monitoring and reconciling operating and payroll expenditures, and ensures that actual financial results reconcile with approved targets
Collaborates with the University Planning Office (UPO) to support the annual budget development process for the SoM.

Payroll Administration and Financial Oversight (SoM Residents and IHC Employees)

Oversees, reviews, and approves biweekly payroll registers before the third-party vendor releases payments and monthly reconciliations. Investigate unusual variances, adjustments, and exceptions.
Monitors payroll funding requirements, forecast upcoming payroll obligations, and ensure sufficient funds are available in the designated bank account before each payroll withdrawal
Oversee the processes, systems, and internal controls supporting the administration of payroll, benefits, and expense claims for medical learners (residents) and Integrated Health Centre (IHC) staff.
Provide leadership and oversight to staff responsible for processing payroll, benefits, and expenses, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable policies and requirements.
Establish and maintain effective procedures, workflows, and controls to support reliable and efficient administration of these functions.

Strategy and external collaboration

Conducts financial research and analysis to support the Dean and CAO in the development of a funding model for the School of Medicine and the Integrated Health Centres (IHC).
Monitors SOM activities relevant to external funding and reporting obligations, and ensures timely information sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Develops and implements a strategic roadmap for School-wide financial forecasting, planning, and internal financial controls, including long-term budget plan for the SoM that supports the academic, research, and operational priorities.
Provides expert analysis and strategic advice on financial risk management for proposed and approved School initiatives.

Financial evaluation and program analysis

Conducts financial evaluations of revenue-generating proposals and new initiatives, and analyzes program costing reports.

Accounting management, reporting & analysis

Manages a wide range of operating, trust, and project accounts (research and non-research) for the SoM and IHC.
Supports University-wide interim and year-end financial statement audits by coordinating SoM responses, and responds to audit inquiries related to IHC and SoM special purpose audits.
Leads the planning and execution of financial analysis to support strategic and operational decisions, and oversees the development and maintenance of statistical analysis systems and integrated financial tracking tools.

HR management

Manages and supervises staff, assigns and prioritises tasks, establishes goals, sets expectations and evaluates performance.

Qualifications

To help us learn more about you, please provide a cover letter and resume describing how you meet the following required qualifications:

Completion of a university degree program in finance, accounting, business or public administration, or a relevant field.
A minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in financial management within a post-secondary, public sector, or MUSH (municipalities, universities, school boards, hospitals) environment, including experience managing complex budgets, government funding, and resource planning.
Equivalent experience or a combination of equivalent experience and education may be accepted in place of education.
Demonstrated work experience in statistical analysis to support forecasting, financial modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) is an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including variance analysis and financial interpretation.
Knowledge of statistical analysis measurement theory to support forecasting, modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
In-depth knowledge of accounting and finance principles and associated technical and security considerations.
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel/Google Sheet and financial systems/software applications to support modelling and reporting.
Knowledge of post-secondary education systems, funding structures and sector-specific financial issues.
Demonstrated skill in developing and implementing financial policies, procedures and processes for new or evolving business initiatives.
Strong project and time management skills in a fast-paced environment.
Effective communication skills to convey complex financial information with stakeholders.
Troubleshooting skills, particularly in identifying causes of financial variances.
Ability to work on team-based projects, and prepare and present accurate reports to senior management.
Ability to organize and manage a complex financial process with accuracy and consistency.
Systems-wide thinking skills, with ability to assess financial and operational implications across units and stakeholder groups.

Leadership Competencies

Leaders at TMU are required to demonstrate the following Leadership Competencies:

Acts with Integrity: Demonstrates behaviors aligned with high ethical standards and personal integrity and acts in accordance with TMU values.
Builds Relationships of Trust & Collaboration: Actively builds a culture of trust and fosters meaningful relationships.
Leads Inclusively: Creates an inclusive environment where everyone is respected, recognized, empowered to achieve their potential, and valued for their differences.
Demonstrates Organizational Acumen: Understands and respectfully navigates complex internal and external environments using sound judgment, diplomacy, and tact.
Drives Vision & Results: Creates and implements a vision grounded in sound decision-making to achieve desired outcomes.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
new_jobs.description:
Venor is proud to partner with Commissionaires Nova Scotia in the recruitment of a Chief Financial Officer.

Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Commissionaires Nova Scotia (CNS) is the province’s leading not-for-profit security provider, delivering guarding, monitoring, investigative, and specialized security services to more than 200 sites across the province. With roughly 1,300 employees, a large share of them veterans of the Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP, CNS is the largest private-sector employer of veterans in Nova Scotia. As part of the national Commissionaires federation of over 22,000 security professionals across Canada, CNS reinvests more than 90% of its annual revenue directly into employee wages, training, and benefits.

On their behalf, we are seeking a strategic and hands-on Chief Financial Officer to join the executive team. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead the organization’s financial strategy, reporting, planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, capital allocation, risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Team, and Board of Governors, you’ll bring financial insight to strategic decision-making while leading a team of finance, IT, and procurement professionals and ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll lead the organization’s financial strategy and provide executive-level financial advice across all business lines. You’ll develop, implement, and maintain financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks, and oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, controllership, treasury management, and audit activities. You’ll also manage the enterprise financial systems and reporting platforms that keep the organization’s financial information timely and accurate, preparing and presenting financial reports to the CEO, Executive Team, Finance and Audit Committee, and Board of Governors, and developing the annual operating and capital budgets, including required submissions to Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).

You’ll provide strategic pricing guidance, including contract billing and labour rates, and ensure compliance with financial, regulatory, tax, and not-for-profit reporting requirements, including CRA obligations. Externally, you’ll manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, insurers, the national Commissionaires federation, and government partners, and contribute to organizational strategy through financial analysis, business cases, and recommendations that support sustainable growth. Internally, you’ll provide executive oversight of payroll, compensation, benefits, and related financial administration, and lead, mentor, and develop a finance team spanning budgeting, payroll and accounts, IT/cyber, and procurement.

What You’ll Bring

You bring a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and executive experience), along with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing. You have 10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and governance within a complex organization, and a track record of advising executive teams, Boards of Directors or Governors, and senior stakeholders. Your knowledge of financial management, accounting standards, regulatory compliance, risk management, and corporate governance is strong, and you’ve demonstrated the ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable financial plans and business cases. You’ve led and developed high-performing finance teams, and you communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, collaborative leader with strong business acumen and a genuine commitment to integrity, innovation, and service excellence. You’re as comfortable in the details of financial reporting as you are advising the boardroom, and you bring the judgment to manage competing priorities during budgeting, audit, and Board reporting cycles.

Notre croissance s’accélère à travers plusieurs entités et nous recherchons un leader en finance capable d’apporter structure, visibilité et rigueur à notre fonction financière. Le ou la directeur(trice) des finances est responsable de l’ensemble de la fonction financière et travaille directement avec les propriétaires de l’entreprise sur les décisions qui façonnent son avenir.

Principales responsabilités

▪ Diriger la fonction financière pour l’ensemble des entités du groupe : comptabilité, comptes clients, comptes fournisseurs, paie et rapports financiers

▪ Superviser les clôtures mensuelles, trimestrielles et annuelles, la consolidation ainsi que la préparation des états financiers

▪ Élaborer les budgets, les prévisions et les projections de flux de trésorerie, et présenter les écarts à l’équipe de direction

Western Alliance Logistics, a division of Western Alliance, is a fast-growing 3PL logistics company specializing in freight forwarding. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Montréal, we move freight by truck, rail, air and sea across Canada, the United States and Mexico.

We are scaling quickly across multiple entities and need a finance leader who can bring structure, visibility and discipline to the numbers. The Director of Finance owns the entire finance function and works directly with ownership on the decisions that shape the business.

new_jobs.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Kraken Customer

What we do: build the most AI-driven, innovative, forward-thinking platform for energy management. From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry.

Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now.

Why it matters: There are singular moments in every industry where a tectonic shift reshapes the entire sector and unlocks previously unheard of possibilities. There are few industries remaining that are ripe for disruption. Those moments need leaders and the energy sector is in that moment. The disruption is happening now.

Our Kraken software and operating model enable our energy clients to lead this shift while enhancing their operational effectiveness. The accelerated adoption of Kraken means we need someone to lead a major North America client implementation to deliver world-changing results. Are you that leader?

The Company

Kraken launched to market five years ago, offering energy utilities one simple end-to-end customer management and local flexibility optimization solution to help them and their customers transition to a decarbonized future. The Kraken platform is effectively the operating system for utilities, at the core of how they run their business.

Kraken is growing rapidly, disrupting the incumbent tech landscape, with over 64 million end-customer accounts contracted across 11 markets globally and managing the optimisation of over 65GW. Kraken has secured licensing deals with large international energy clients to replace their core technology stack and re-image their operations with an unblemished track record of transformation success.

We are tracking toward 100 million customer accounts on the platform by 2027.

At the end of 2025 Kraken was independently valued at $8.65 billion, and received $1 billion in investment.

🏠 Where You'll Fit In

The individual in this role will serve as both the face of, and the delivery leader for the next North American utility transformation. This is a high profile role with a dedicated internal team of experienced Client Delivery Leaders, a dedicated Client Engineering team, as well as the attention of our 1000+ person Product and Engineering organization. Our ideal candidate will be comfortable briefing the CEO of a billion+ dollar utility, while also able to maintain a detailed understanding of the complicated dependencies across multiple work streams so as to successfully coach, guide, and support our talented delivery leaders throughout the transformation.

🚀 What You'll Own

Be accountable for the successful execution of client implementation programs using our Build-Operate-Transfer methodology, which covers technology, business operations and culture transformation
Find solutions that bring our clients into the new software and operating model that both accelerates delivery and reduces risk
Develop deep trust with our C-suite client executives
Lead a team of Client Delivery Leads across functional delivery areas
Prioritise outcomes and delivery from a team of Client Engineers directly supporting this transformation, while collaborating with our VP of product for Vertically Integrated Utilities to ensure the entire 1000+ person development team at Kraken is delivering the capabilities required to exceed our client’s expectations
Communicate effectively to stakeholders at all levels, both internally and externally
Continuously demonstrate Kraken’s business value to the client and build a governance model which can last once the implementation program is completed
Set the direction and pace for implementation program execution. Managing internal and external expectations, removing blockers and making prioritisation decisions to enable successful client transformations
Understand the implementation program details and report progress to the client and internal stakeholders
Embody the Kraken ways of working. Provide support and feedback to members of the Kraken team and reinforce an environment of psychological safety.

🧠 What You'll Bring To The Party

Extensive experience in Regulated Utilities (ideally in the North American market)
Strong experience leading large, enterprise-level technology implementations and the significant transformation of business operations , ideally in utilities or similar industries (e.g. telecom, public sector)
Proven experience with C-suite clients, leading strategic conversations, negotiating win-wins, and advising on business transformation
Hands-on leader of global implementation teams consisting of experts representing implementation, product, data, engineering, change management, and enablement
Problem solver with an ability to focus conversations on the things that truly matter
Ability to understand what success looks like for the client and laser-focused on how to enable them to achieve that without always saying yes
Team player who can work effectively with national and global teams across Kraken
Excellent communication and facilitation skills. You are well respected with a natural gravitas
Client and quality focus; highly effective at building and improving customer relationships as peers
Mobile - You will be expected to invest in face-to-face relationship building with our clients and internal teams. Frequent travel will be expected.

Soft Skills

Kraken is at the forefront of innovation in the energy industry and we succeed in large part thanks to our people. To fit well at Kraken, you’ll also be:
Passionate about helping clients (without them, we don’t exist)
Passionate about technology (we are a tech business disrupting energy)
Committed to sustainability (we are all about speeding up the shift to a more sustainable world)
Open-minded, flexible and adaptable (we are constantly growing, changing and evolving)
Confident in decision-making
Supportive
Approachable and fun to work with
Inclusive
Resilient, working well under pressure
Believe in big ambitions and small egos
Embrace the servant leadership philosophy

Why You'll Love It Here

Opt in medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
Paid time off — we know working hard means also being able to recharge as needed, we trust our employees to get the work done and take the time they need.
Flexible working environment: you need to shift around your schedule? You do you, we genuinely believe in work/life balance.

While the broad salary range is listed, not all candidates will be placed at the top of the range—this will be determined by the overall fit for the position. If you have questions about this, just ask! Our recruiters are happy to provide more context.

Why this role is different and why to apply

This is an opportunity to be part of the business that is revolutionising the energy sector. We are looking for someone who is experienced and eager to disrupt the industry and the incumbent software players. Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Managing Director, Strategy & Transformation provides strategic direction, transformation leadership, executive advisory support and oversight for the Strategy & Transformation function. The Managing Director operates as a senior partner to the EVP business heads and key enterprise partners, translating Wealth Management priorities into integrated plans, governance routines, insights and measurable outcomes. The role leads a multi-disciplinary team responsible for strategic projects, executive reporting, employee engagement, client insights and change enablement, while ensuring activities are conducted in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies and procedures.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Lead and drives a customer focused culture throughout their team to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems and knowledge.

new_jobs.title: Director, Delivery CX AI
new_jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

Compensation Range: CA$150K - CA$190K

The ideal candidate will provide expertise and support to senior management in identification, documentation and maintenance of data risk management requirements, enhancing their ability to anticipate and manage data management risks effectively.

Act as a centre of excellence and advocate for data management best practices for Finance and Risk domains
Contribute to and support communication of data strategies, standards and initiatives to Finance and Risk partners
