new_jobs.title: Director of Finance
new_jobs.description:
Most finance leaders can tell you what happened. We need someone who can help determine what happens next.

Are You Ready to Build a Platform Company?

EDL Building Solutions is a strong, growing building services company today. Over the next five to seven years, we intend to become a platform company through acquisition, disciplined integration, and organic growth. This is a ground floor seat in building it. You will join the senior leadership team at the point where the decisions you make shape what EDL becomes, not just how it reports.

We are looking for a Director of Finance who is equally comfortable setting long term financial strategy, evaluating an acquisition, and rolling up their sleeves to fix an immediate problem. Reporting to the Vice President and partnering with the President, you will lead Finance, Human Resources, and Information Technology, three functions that must work together to make growth repeatable.

Who We Are

EDL Building Solutions is Alberta's trusted multi trade partner, providing HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and building automation solutions for commercial and industrial facilities. We give our clients peace of mind through reliability, comfort, and efficiency.

The Person We're Looking For

A Fixer.
You do not accept broken processes, recurring inefficiencies, or unexplained results as part of doing business. You find root causes, challenge existing practices, and own the improvement.
A Thinker.
You are analytical, commercially minded, and naturally curious. You look past the financial statements to understand what is really happening in the business, and you turn that understanding into practical recommendations.
A Doer.
You move between strategy and execution without losing either. You can lead a financial strategy discussion in the morning and work directly with your team to solve an operational issue in the afternoon.

What You'll Do

•    Partner with the Vice President and President on strategy, governance, and the decisions that shape EDL's future.
•    Lead Finance, HR, and IT, building the systems, structure, and capability to support growth.
•    Own financial reporting, budgeting, and rolling forecasts that look forward, not just backward.
•    Drive enterprise value through sustainable earnings, recurring revenue, cash generation, and return on invested capital.
•    Lead the financial side of acquisitions, including valuation, due diligence, financing, and post acquisition integration.
•    Manage inter-company transactions across operating entities and holding companies, including allocations, eliminations, and consolidated reporting.
•    Support the design and administration of the company wide short term incentive and bonus plan, including calculation and payout.
•    Manage cash flow, working capital, and treasury, including banking and lender relationships.
•    Partner with operational leaders on margins, labour utilization, job costing, pricing, and overhead, and challenge the numbers when they do not add up.
•    Lead, coach, and develop the Finance, HR, and IT teams, and hold them to clear standards of accountability.

What You Bring

•    A professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).
•    Progressive finance leadership experience, including several years leading a finance function at a senior level.
•    Multi entity and inter-company accounting experience, including holding company structures and consolidation.
•    Hands on mergers and acquisitions experience: valuation, due diligence, financing, and integration.
•    Experience leading or overseeing functions beyond finance, ideally HR and IT.
•    Strong commercial judgement and the confidence to challenge senior leaders constructively.
•    Experience with Jonas ERP software, particularly job costing, service management, project accounting, and financial reporting, is considered a strong asset.
•    Experience across construction, service, or a comparable multi trade environment will set you apart.

What You'll Get

•    Annual base salary: $130,000 - $180,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
•    Target short term incentive (STIP): 20% of annual base salary, subject to plan terms and performance.
•    Company paid benefits package and life insurance.
•    Paid vacation and paid personal time off.
•    RRSP matching.
•    The opportunity to build enterprise value, and share in the result.

Other Requirements

•    Valid driver's license and a clean criminal record.
•    Based primarily out of EDL's Edmonton office.

Ready to Build Something Great?

If you are ready to help take EDL from a strong building services company to a platform company, we would like to hear from you.

Apply today. Our HR team reviews applications daily and will connect with qualified candidates to discuss next steps.

﻿

EDL Building Solutions | Reliability. Passion. One Team. Results.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director of Finance And Operations (OTE: upto $175k )
new_jobs.description:
Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is redefining how private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program as one of North America’s fastest-growing technology companies, BFX brings together practice management software, digital marketing, and AI-powered solutions to help healthcare providers build stronger, more profitable businesses.

With offices across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and India, we are building a global healthcare technology company with an ambitious vision: to become the AI operating system and growth infrastructure for private-pay healthcare.
Our next phase requires financial leadership and operational discipline to turn rapid growth into lasting enterprise value.

As Director of Finance & Operations
, you will work closely with the CEO and leadership team to shape strategic plans, strengthen financial oversight, and improve performance across the business.
This is a hands-on leadership opportunity with meaningful influence over how BFX invests, operates, and scales. We are looking for an accomplished CPA who brings verifiable experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies—and the judgment, ownership, and execution skills to help build our next stage of growth.

Your Role in a Nutshell

You will lead financial oversight, strategic planning, board reporting, and operational performance management across multiple business lines and international markets.
Working closely with the CEO and departmental leaders, you will translate business strategy into budgets, forecasts, operating priorities, and measurable results. You will strengthen cash management, improve profitability, evaluate growth investments, and ensure leadership has accurate information to make timely decisions.
The ideal candidate combines rigorous accounting and financial management skills with commercial judgment and proven operational leadership. You must be comfortable challenging assumptions, holding teams accountable, and moving between strategic analysis and detailed execution.

What You Will Do

Financial Oversight and Control

Oversee accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, and the integrity of financial information across the business.
Lead timely monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, including financial statements, variance analysis, and management commentary.
Oversee billing, revenue recognition, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and payroll controls.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors, and tax advisers to meet reporting and compliance obligations.
Strengthen financial policies, approval processes, and controls as the company scales.

Cash Management and Profitability

Own cash-flow planning, including a rolling 13-week cash forecast and longer-term liquidity projections.
Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline, and visibility into cash commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service, customer segment, and market.
Identify and execute opportunities to improve gross margins, control operating costs, and increase cash generation.
Evaluate spending and investment proposals against expected returns, payback periods, and business priorities.

Operational Oversight

Partner with departmental leaders to establish operating plans, budgets, KPIs, and clear accountability for results.
Lead regular performance reviews, identifying gaps and ensuring corrective actions have owners and deadlines.
Oversee cross-functional improvement initiatives that strengthen productivity, resource utilization, and execution.
Assess headcount plans, vendor contracts, procurement, and operating expenditures.
Improve workflows, reporting systems, and data quality through automation and appropriate use of AI.
Lead and mentor finance team members while building effective partnerships across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product, and Operations.

Strategic Planning and Business Analysis

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, and the financial component of strategic planning.
Develop financial models, scenario analyses, and business cases for hiring, pricing, product investments, partnerships, and international expansion.
Monitor SaaS and recurring-revenue metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition costs, and payback.
Translate financial and operational data into clear recommendations on where to invest, improve, defer, or stop.
Balance growth opportunities with disciplined progress toward sustainable profitability.
Support financing, due diligence, acquisitions, and other strategic initiatives as required.

Board and Executive Reporting

Own preparation of board financial packages, executive dashboards, and performance presentations.
Provide clear analysis of financial results, forecasts, cash position, business risks, and recommended actions.
Explain the operational drivers behind performance and highlight material changes against plan.
Ensure board and executive reporting is accurate, consistent, timely, and supported by reliable information.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

Role Expectations

This is an E3 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level own company-wide outcomes, set the strategy for their function, and operate with broad autonomy in partnership with the CEO, the executive team, and the Board.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Act as a full strategic partner to the CEO and the Board, not only as a steward of the numbers.
Build and develop a finance organization that scales ahead of the business, hiring and coaching leaders who raise the bar.
Bring financial discipline to company-wide decisions on pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Own the accuracy and credibility of forecasting, reporting, and board materials.
Prepare the company for its next financing or strategic event well before it is needed.

What success looks like:

Forecasting and planning the executive team and Board trust and act on.
The systems, controls, and team in place to operate credibly at $200M+ in revenue.
Solink positioned and diligence-ready for its next strategic chapter.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, with prior scale-up CFO experience.
Proven track record scaling SaaS or technology companies from ~$50M to $200M+ revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep FP&A expertise with strong analytical and strategic planning capabilities.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising (Series C/D/E) or public markets experience.
Strong command of SaaS metrics and recurring revenue models.
Knowledge of GAAP/IFRS, compliance frameworks, and audit oversight.
Inspirational leader with the ability to develop high-performing finance teams.

Nice-to-Have:

M&A experience across due diligence, valuation, and post-close integration.
Experience in a Canadian company with US and international operations, including multi-currency and cross-border tax considerations.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian or American Citizen, or eligible to work in Canada or the United States.
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: A stellar benefits package, ensuring you're fully supported with anything you need.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro Call with Our Talent Team
Interview with the Hiring Manager
Interview with Senior Director, People & Culture and Chief Corporate & Legal Officer (Individual 45-Minute Slots)
Final Interviews with Two Board Members
Reference Checks
Offer & Onboarding

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

new_jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Data Governance
new_jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Data Management, Computer Science, or a related discipline; Master is an asset.
8+ years of progressive experience across data governance, risk management, or audit, including at least 2 years leading people, and demonstrable end-to-end delivery of a control or governance environment.
Working knowledge of ICFR, SOC 1 / ISAE 3402, COSO 2013, ITGCs, and DAMA-DMBOK; CPA, CIA, CISA, or CDMP an asset. Familiarity with DCAM / CDMC and data contracts an asset.
Hands-on experience with data cataloguing and governance tooling (Microsoft Purview equivalents such as Collibra an asset) and with controls testing in an ICFR or SOX environment.
Working knowledge of a modern data-platform stack (Microsoft Fabric / lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Entra ID), enough to specify and validate controls.
Working knowledge of Yardi strongly preferred.
Investment and portfolio management literacy or business acumen
Proven ability to build controls that produce retained, re-testable evidence.
Ability to work across Finance, IT, and Data & Analytics, and turn technical and operational complexity into clear governance and control frameworks.
Comfortable preparing materials for senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
Comfortable building or growing an early-stage function.
Experience within real estate, asset management, pension, or investment management environments strongly preferred.

This is a newly created role within our organization.

The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $155,000 – $175,000.

Based on the position, QuadReal offers a competitive total rewards package in addition to the base pay, which may include a performance-based incentive plan, comprehensive health & dental benefits, pension plan, and paid time off.

The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity.

We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) technology — alongside human review — to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. Our recruitment team remains involved in all decisions.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada as the company does not provide work permit sponsorship for this role.

Note to Recruiters: QuadReal does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to QuadReal, directly or indirectly, will be considered QuadReal property. QuadReal will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. A recruiting agency must first have a valid, written and fully executed agency agreement contract for engaged services to submit resumes.

QuadReal Property Group will provide reasonable accommodation at any time throughout the hiring process for applicants with disabilities or for those needing job postings in an alternate format. If you require accommodation, please advise the Talent Acquisition team member you are working with and include the following: Job posting #, your name and your preferred method of contact.

Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

Director, Legal Counsel, Data & Privac
y | Brampton

The Data Trust Office is an enablement-first function. We embed privacy and data governance into products and services to build customer trust and loyalty, ensuring compliance by design.

As Director, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and driving Loblaw's enterprise privacy and data governance program. You will be accountable for executing the Data Trust strategy, overseeing risk management and compliance activities, developing policy, managing breaches, and fostering stakeholder engagement across the business.

As Legal Counsel, you will serve as a key partner to the commercial legal team, providing privacy, data and cybersecurity subject matter expertise on complex commercial arrangements and supporting the development, review and negotiation of appropriate contractual protections.

In both functions you will provide strategic, practical and business-oriented legal advice on privacy, data governance, CASL and related regulatory matters to the business, helping them navigate complex legal requirements while enabling the responsible use of data and innovation.

This role reports to the Enterprise Privacy Officer.

What You'll Do

Champion privacy as a business enabler by driving stakeholder engagement and embedding privacy and data governance into products and services.
Provide strategic legal advice on privacy, data governance, CASL and related regulatory matters across the business, including in connection with new products, services, technologies, digital initiatives, data uses, artificial intelligence, marketing and other strategic projects and transactions.
Advise on the interpretation and application of privacy laws, CASL, related regulatory requirements and regulator guidance, translating legal requirements into practical, business-oriented advice.
Conduct Data and Privacy Impact Assessments (DPIAs), identify and evaluate legal, regulatory, data and privacy risks, and provide practical, risk-based recommendations on appropriate controls and mitigation strategies.
Partner with commercial legal counsel as the privacy, data and cybersecurity subject matter expert on commercial agreements involving personal information, data sharing, technology, vendors, artificial intelligence or access to Loblaw systems and data. Provide practical legal advice and support the negotiation and resolution of complex or escalated privacy, data and cybersecurity issues.
Provide legal advice on consent and transparency requirements, data governance and lifecycle matters, and the responsible use of data, including in connection with artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
Oversee privacy breach, complaint and investigation management activities, including intake, escalation, investigation and response, and provide legal advice on notification obligations, regulatory risk, remediation and response strategy.
Advise on privacy and CASL regulatory matters and engage with regulators, as appropriate, in connection with regulatory inquiries, investigations, complaints and other regulatory matters, including engagement and management of external legal counsel as appropriate.
Recruit, lead, and develop a high-performing data and privacy team, including coaching and developing privacy professionals and fostering strong legal and risk judgment across the team.
Stay ahead of evolving national privacy and health privacy laws, global regulatory developments, privacy-enhancing technologies, and emerging innovations (e.g., AI/LLMs), CASL and related regulatory developments, and advise on their legal, regulatory and business implications.
Partner cross-functionally across the enterprise to continuously improve privacy-related policies, templates, guidance, processes and controls and create efficiencies while maintaining appropriate legal, cybersecurity and regulatory safeguards.

What You Bring

Law degree and member in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario, with 7-10 years of relevant experience in an in-house legal department and/or compliance function, including significant experience advising on privacy and related regulatory matters. Experience at a leading law firm is also considered an asset.
Practical, solutions-oriented and agile, with strong legal and business judgment and a demonstrated ability to navigate complexity and ambiguity, move beyond identifying risk, and develop creative, pragmatic solutions that enable business objectives while appropriately managing legal, privacy and data risk.
A supportive and engaged people leader who invests in the development of their team and creates an inclusive, high-performing environment where people are empowered, supported and accountable.
Thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, with the agility to manage competing priorities, make sound decisions and drive matters forward.
Strong collaborator and trusted advisor who builds effective relationships, influences stakeholders and facilitates practical solutions across the enterprise.
Excellent communication, organizational and presentation skills, with the ability to distill complex legal, technical and privacy issues into clear, concise and actionable advice for stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Demonstrated leadership experience delivering privacy and data programs and advising on complex privacy, data and regulatory matters within large, matrixed organizations.
Significant experience interpreting and applying Canadian federal and provincial privacy laws, CASL and related regulatory requirements to complex business and technology initiatives, including digital products and services, analytics, artificial intelligence, marketing and other data-driven activities.
Demonstrated experience conducting Data and Privacy Impact Assessments (DPIAs), evaluating risk and developing practical controls and mitigation strategies.
Proven experience managing regulatory risk and engaging directly with privacy regulators, including in connection with inquiries, investigations, complaints or other regulatory matters.
Experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating privacy and cybersecurity provisions in complex commercial agreements, including data processing, data sharing, technology and vendor arrangements.
Experience advising on privacy incidents and breach response, including assessing legal and regulatory obligations and supporting cross-functional response and remediation efforts.
Experience in corporate retail, direct-to-consumer or other complex, highly regulated environments is an asset.
CIPP-C or equivalent privacy certification preferred; AIGP and DCAM certifications are considered an asset.

new_jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities

Reports to EVP Corporate Services

100% virtual

12-15 month engagement

Our client is a highly reputable Canadian organization
with a significant and multifaceted mandate. During a period of leadership transition, they are seeking an accomplished Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities
to provide stability, strong financial stewardship and experienced leadership while helping position the organization for its next chapter.

This is more than a maintenance assignment. It is an opportunity for an experienced finance executive to come in, make an immediate impact and elevate an already high-performing function
. The successful interim will inherit a capable team and will be expected to provide visible leadership, bring fresh perspective, strengthen financial insight and discipline, and identify opportunities to enhance the sophistication and effectiveness of the function.
The mandate spans financial reporting, planning, performance management, risk and controls, treasury, facilities and procurement, while providing senior leadership with thoughtful financial advice and insight.

The Mandate

Working closely with the senior executive team, the Interim VP will take leadership of the finance function and ensure continued strength in the organization's financial management during the transition.

This is a role for someone equally comfortable around the executive table and in the details
. The successful executive will be strategic when the situation requires it, but willing to roll up their sleeves, challenge assumptions, solve problems and help the team execute.

Key priorities will include:

Providing strong financial stewardship
, ensuring the continued integrity, accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting, forecasting and financial operations.
Leading and supporting a strong finance team, creating clarity, engagement and momentum through a period of change.
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership, bringing insight to organizational performance, longer-term planning and decision-making.
Reviewing existing financial processes, controls and practices and identifying opportunities to modernize, streamline and elevate the sophistication of the function.
Providing leadership across facilities management and procurement, ensuring strong governance, commercial discipline and effective execution.
Strengthening budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, risk management and performance reporting.
Working effectively with external advisors, auditors and other key stakeholders.
Supporting senior leadership and the organization's governance bodies with credible, thoughtful financial insight. The underlying position specifically supports Audit and Finance Committee and Board activities.
Looking beyond business-as-usual to identify opportunities to drive change, improve effectiveness and leave the organization stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

The Ideal Interim Executive

We are looking for a seasoned financial executive who knows how to enter an established organization, quickly understand the environment and add value without unnecessary disruption
.

Ideally, this individual will bring a combination of not-for-profit and commercial experience
, pairing an understanding of stewardship, governance and stakeholder accountability with the commercial instincts and operational discipline of the private sector.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant senior financial leadership experience within a complex organization.
A professional accounting designation, with strong technical grounding across accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and internal controls. The underlying profile calls for a CPA/CA-preferred designation and experience with IFRS, ASPE and ASNPO.
Experience leading strong teams through periods of transition, change or transformation
.
A genuinely hands-on style. Someone prepared to get into the numbers and issues rather than lead exclusively from 30,000 feet.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
.
Exposure to facilities, procurement and broader corporate services would be highly valuable.
Strong executive presence and the ability to establish credibility quickly with senior executives, employees, external advisors and governance stakeholders.
A pragmatic, collaborative leadership style with the confidence to respectfully challenge the status quo.
Experience operating across both mission-driven/not-for-profit and commercially oriented environments
would be particularly attractive.

Why This Assignment?

For the right interim executive, this offers the opportunity to do what great interims do best: step into an important organization at an important moment and make a measurable difference.

You will be joining a high-performing team rather than rebuilding a broken function. The opportunity is to provide leadership through transition, bring an objective external lens, elevate financial and operational practices, and create sustainable improvements that remain long after the assignment has concluded.

This is an assignment for someone who enjoys being more than a caretaker. It requires an executive who can protect what is working, challenge what can be better, and create momentum for what comes next.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

new_jobs.title: Director of Finance, FP&A
new_jobs.description:
A growing, project-driven organization is seeking a Director of Finance, FP&A to play a key role in financial planning, analysis, treasury, and business decision support. This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys working closely with senior leadership while also getting into the details of the numbers and operations.

About The Role

This position will lead core FP&A activities while supporting cash management, financing, and project-level financial analysis. The successful candidate will bring a commercial mindset, strong financial modelling capabilities, and the ability to turn complex financial information into practical recommendations.The role will also have an opportunity to strengthen and evolve the organization's financial planning and reporting processes as the business continues to grow.

What You'll Do

Lead the annual budgeting process and coordinate ongoing financial planning activities
Own regular forecasting and reforecasting, ensuring leadership has a clear view of expected financial performance
Develop financial models and forward-looking analysis to support business planning and decision-making
Analyze budget-to-actual results, identify meaningful variances, and communicate key drivers to leadership
Monitor financial trends, risks, opportunities, and performance indicators
Prepare management reporting, analysis, and presentations for senior leadership and ownership
Support cash flow forecasting, liquidity planning, and day-to-day treasury activities
Assist with banking relationships, financing requirements, and ongoing lender reporting
Prepare financial analysis and supporting information for debt financing and banking partners
Evaluate project-level financial performance, including costs, profitability, cash requirements, and projected returns
Support project accounting and finance activities as required
Provide financial insights to inform operational, investment, and strategic decisions
Identify opportunities to improve FP&A, reporting, forecasting, and financial planning processes

What You Bring

Senior Manager or Director-level experience in finance, FP&A, corporate finance, or a related discipline
Significant experience leading budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes
Strong financial modelling and analytical capabilities
Experience with treasury, cash flow forecasting, and liquidity management
Exposure to bank financing, debt facilities, and lender relationships
Strong understanding of financial performance analysis and variance reporting
Experience supporting project-based, capital-intensive, or operationally complex businesses is an asset
Ability to confidently present financial information and recommendations to senior leadership
Strong commercial and operational judgment, with an ability to connect financial results to business performance
Comfortable operating in a hands-on environment rather than focusing exclusively on high-level strategy
CPA designation is an asset, although strong FP&A and corporate finance experience will be highly valued
Adaptable and comfortable working within an evolving organizational structure

Why Join

This is an opportunity to take on a visible finance leadership role within a growing organization where your analysis can directly influence business decisions. You'll have meaningful exposure to senior leadership, ownership, financing activities, and project performance while helping build more effective financial planning and reporting practices.

Deputy Chief Financial Officer

Prince Rupert, BC

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with the Prince Rupert Port Authority (PRPA) to recruit a Deputy Chief Financial Officer (Deputy CFO) to join their leadership team.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Deputy CFO will provide leadership across accounting, treasury, financial planning and analysis, procurement, financial reporting, and capital finance. This role will play a key part in supporting strategic decision-making, overseeing day-to-day financial operations, and ensuring the organization maintains strong financial management, governance, and reporting practices.

• Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes in support of organizational priorities and capital investment plans.

• Coordinate the annual external audit process and ensure compliance with regulatory, taxation, and reporting requirements.
• Prepare materials and reporting for the Executive Leadership Team, Audit Committee, and Board of Directors.
• Partner with leaders across the organization to support budgeting, resource allocation, and operational decision-making.
• Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance team while fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

• Strong knowledge of IFRS, financial reporting, treasury management, internal controls, and financial planning practices.
